en: Vājasaneyi-Saṃhitā (Śukla-Yajurveda): For the sake of food, thee! For the sake of strength, thee! You are the winds. May the divine Savitṛ impel you toward the most excellent work. Swell, O inviolable ones, for Indra’s portion; may you be rich in offspring, free from disease, and free from sickness. Let not the thief master you, nor the malevolent man. Be firm in this lord of cattle; be many. Protect the cattle of the sacrificer.

Thou art the purifier of wealth; thou art heaven, thou art earth; thou art the cauldron of Mātariśvan, thou art all-sustaining. Be firm with the highest support; do not waver, and let not thy lord of the sacrifice waver.

You are the purifier of wealth, with a hundred streams; you are the purifier of wealth, with a thousand streams. May the god Savitṛ purify you with the purifier of wealth, with a hundred streams, with a good strainer. What desire have you milked?
She is all-life; she is the maker of all; she is the sustainer of all. I extend thee, the portion of Indra, with Soma. O Viṣṇu, protect the oblation!
O Agni, Lord of Vows, I shall perform the vow; may I be able to do it, may it be successful for me. Here I approach truth from untruth.
Who yokes you? He yokes you. For whom does he yoke you? For him he yokes you. For your work, for your service.
The Rakṣas is burnt away; the enemies are burnt away. The Rakṣas is scorched away; the enemies are scorched away. I move along the wide mid-air.
You are the yoke; injure him who injures us; injure him whom we injure. You are the best bearer among the gods, the most uniter, the most fulfiller, the most beloved, the best invoker of the gods.

Thou art unswerving, the vessel for the oblation; be firm, do not waver, and may the lord of the sacrifice not waver. May Viṣṇu step upon thee. Wide space for the wind! The Rakṣas is struck down. May the five [fingers] restrain [thee].
At the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins and the hands of Pūṣan, I take [thee] acceptable to Agni; I take [thee] acceptable to Agni and Soma.

For the being, not for the enemy; may I behold the light of heaven. May the dwellings on earth be firm. I traverse the wide mid-air. I set thee in the navel of the earth, in the lap of Aditi; O Agni, guard the oblation.

You two are purifiers, belonging to Viṣṇu. At the impulse of Savitṛ, I purify you with an unbroken purifier, with the rays of the sun. O divine waters, moving forward, flowing forward, lead this sacrifice today to the front, and the lord of the sacrifice to the front—a well-established lord of the sacrifice who seeks the gods.

Indra chose you for the slaying of Vṛtra; you chose Indra for the slaying of Vṛtra. You are sprinkled. I sprinkle you, acceptable to Agni. I sprinkle you, acceptable to Agni and Soma. Be purified for the divine rite, for the sacrifice to the gods. Whatever impurities have struck you while you were unpurified, that I now purify for you.

Thou art a refuge. Shaken off is the Rakṣas, shaken off are the enemies. Thou art the skin of Aditi; may Aditi recognize thee. Thou art a stone, born of the tree; thou art a pressing-stone with a broad base; may the skin of Aditi recognize thee.

You are the body of Agni, the release of speech; I take you for the enjoyment of the gods. You are the great pressing-stone, born of the tree; as such, prepare this oblation for the gods—prepare it well, prepare it perfectly! O preparer of the oblation, come! O preparer of the oblation, come! O preparer of the oblation, come!

You are a cock with a honeyed tongue; speak for us food and vigor. Through you may we conquer every host. You are increased by rain; let that which is increased by rain recognize you. Winnowed away is the Rakṣas, winnowed away are the enemies. Struck down is the Rakṣas. May Vāyu sift you apart. May the god Savitṛ, the golden-handed, receive you with his flawless hand.

You are the bold one. O Agni, drive away the raw-eating fire; expel the flesh-eater; bring hither the fire that sacrifices to the gods. You are firm; make the earth firm. I place you down, winner of the *brahman*, winner of the *kṣatra*, winner of kinsmen, for the destruction of the enemy.

O Agni, accept this sacred formulation (*brahman*). You are the support; make firm the intermediate space. I set you down, you who win the *brahman*, who win the sovereignty (*kṣatra*), and who win the kinsmen, for the destruction of the enemy. You are the sustainer; make firm the sky. I set you down, you who win the *brahman*, who win the sovereignty, and who win the kinsmen, for the destruction of the enemy. I set you down for all the quarters. You are the layers; you are the upward-facing layers. Heat yourselves with the fervor of the Bhrigus and the Aṅgirases.

Thou art a refuge. Shaken off is the Rakṣas, shaken off are the enemies. Thou art the skin of Aditi; may Aditi recognize thee. Thou art Dhiṣaṇā, the daughter of the mountain; may Parvatī recognize thee. Thou art the pillar of heaven. Thou art Dhiṣaṇā, the daughter of the mountain; may Parvatī recognize thee.

You are grain; satisfy the gods! For out-breathing you; for up-breathing you; for diffused-breathing you. May I bestow long extension for the sake of life. May the god Savitṛ, the golden-handed, receive you with his flawless hand. For sight you; you are the milk of the great ones.

At the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins and the hands of Pūṣan, I mix you together. May the waters be united with the plants; may the plants be united with the sap. May the wealthy ones be mixed with the moving ones; may the honeyed ones be mixed with the honeyed ones.

I mix thee for Janayati. This is for Agni; this is for Agni and Soma. For food, thee! Thou art the Gharma, the life of all. O wide-expanding one, expand widely; may the lord of the sacrifice expand widely for thee. May Agni not harm thy skin. May the divine Savitṛ cook thee upon the highest firmament.
Do not fear; do not tremble. May the sacrifice be unwearied; may the offspring of the sacrificer be unwearied. For Trita you; for Dvita you; for Ekata you.

At the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins and the hands of Pūṣan, I take you, the performer of the sacrifice for the gods. You are the right arm of Indra, thousand-edged and hundred-fold sharp; you are Vāyu, keenly sharp, the slayer of the enemy.

O Earth, place of sacrifice for the gods, may I not harm your root, O herb. Go to the fold, to the cow-pen. May the sky rain for you. Bind him, O God Savitṛ, upon the furthest earth with a hundred fetters—him who hates us and whom we hate—and do not release him from there.

May I bind *araru* away from the earth, the place of sacrifice to the gods. Go to the pen, to the stall! May the sky rain for you! Bind him, O god Savitṛ, with a hundred snares upon the furthest earth—he who hates us and whom we hate—do not release him from there! *Araru*, do not fly up to heaven! Let not your drop leap to the sky! Go to the pen, to the stall! May the sky rain for you! Bind him, O god Savitṛ, with a hundred snares upon the furthest earth—he who hates us and whom we hate—do not release him from there!

I enclose you with the Gāyatrī metre; I enclose you with the Triṣṭubh metre; I enclose you with the Jagatī metre. You are gentle and auspicious; you are pleasant and a good seat; you are full of vigor and full of milk.

In ancient times, O mighty one, you took up the earth that bestows life from the spreading Krūra; that which they set in motion within the moon by means of funeral offerings (svadhā), the wise, pointing toward it, worship.
Set down the sprinkling waters; you are the slayer of the hater.

The *rakṣas* is burnt away; the enemies are burnt away. The *rakṣas* is scorched away; the enemies are scorched away. You are sharpened, the destroyer of rivals; I cleanse you, the vigorous one, for the attainment of vigor. The *rakṣas* is burnt away; the enemies are burnt away. The *rakṣas* is scorched away; the enemies are scorched away. You are sharpened, the destroyer of rivals; I cleanse you, the vigorous one, for the attainment of vigor.

Thou art the girdle of Aditi; thou art the sacrificial seat of Viṣṇu. For strength thee! With an unimpaired eye I gaze upon thee. Thou art the tongue of Agni, a good invoker for the gods. Be present for me at every station, for every sacrificial formula (yajus)!

At the impulse of Savitṛ, I purify you with a flawless strainer, with the rays of the sun. At the impulse of Savitṛ, I purify you all with a flawless strainer, with the rays of the sun. You are brilliance; you are pure; you are immortality. You are the abode by name; you are the beloved of the gods, the inviolable place of sacrifice for the gods.

Thou art black, dwelling in the lair; I sprinkle thee, acceptable to Agni. Thou art the altar; I sprinkle thee, acceptable to the sacrificial grass. Thou art the sacrificial grass; I sprinkle thee, acceptable to the offering-spoons.

Thou art the unmoistening for Aditi. Thou art the tuft of Viṣṇu. I strew thee, soft as wool, a good seat for the gods. Svāhā to the Lord of the Earth! Svāhā to the Lord of the World! Svāhā to the Lord of Beings!

May Viśvāvasu, the Gandharva, place thee around for the safety of all and for the protection of the sacrificer; thou art the enclosure, O Agni, praised with the *iḍā* invocation. Thou art the right arm of Indra; may Viśvāvasu place thee around for the safety of all and for the protection of the sacrificer; thou art the enclosure, O Agni, praised with the *iḍā* invocation. May Mitra and Varuṇa place thee around from the north with steadfast law for the safety of all and for the protection of the sacrificer; thou art the enclosure, O Agni, praised with the *iḍā* invocation.
O Sage, we kindle you, the radiant Vītihotra, the great Agni at the sacrifice.

You are the fuel-stick. May Sūrya protect you from the east against any curse. You two are the arms of Savitṛ. I spread you out, soft as wool, a comfortable seat for the gods. May the Vasus, the Rudras, and the Ādityas sit upon you.

Ghṛtācī art thou, Juhū by name; sit here upon this dear seat with thy dear abode. Ghṛtācī art thou, Upabhṛt by name; sit here upon this dear seat with thy dear abode. Ghṛtācī art thou, Dhruvā by name; sit here upon this dear seat with thy dear abode. Sit upon this dear seat with thy dear abode. They have sat down firm in the womb of Ṛta; protect them, O Viṣṇu! Protect the sacrifice! Protect the lord of the sacrifice! Protect me, the performer of the sacrifice!
O Agni, winner of the prize, I cleanse you, the winner of the prize, as you are about to run for the prize. Homage to the gods! Svadhā to the ancestors! May you two be well-yoked for me.

May I today bring together for the gods the unspilled clarified butter. O Viṣṇu, may I not step upon you with my foot. O Agni, may I abide in your shadow, which possesses wealth; O Viṣṇu, you are the station. From here Indra performed his heroic deed; upright he has stood at the sacrifice.

O Agni, you have accepted the office of the Hotṛ; you have accepted the office of the messenger. May Heaven and Earth favor you; may you, as the Sviṣṭakṛt, favor Heaven and Earth. O Indra, may you be present for the gods with the clarified butter as the oblation, Svāhā! May light be united with light.

May Indra bestow this power upon me; may wealth attend us, O Maghavan. May our blessings be fulfilled; may our blessings be true. Mother Earth has been invoked; may Mother Earth call to me. Agni from the Āgnīdhra fire, svāhā!

Father Heaven has been invoked; may Father Heaven invoke me in return. From the *āgnīdhra* fire, Agni [invokes]. *Svāhā!* At the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins and the hands of Pūṣan, I receive you. With the mouth of Agni, I eat you.
O God Savitṛ, they declare this sacrifice of yours to Bṛhaspati, the Brahman.
By that protect the sacrifice, by that protect the lord of the sacrifice, by that protect me.
May the mind, swift as thought, enjoy the clarified butter; may Bṛhaspati extend this sacrifice. May he establish this sacrifice unharmed; may all the gods rejoice here. Om! Stand firm!
This is your fuel, O Agni; through it, may you grow and may you swell.
And may we increase, and may we swell with abundance.
O Agni, winner of the prize, I cleanse you, who have run for the prize, the winner of the prize.
Following the victory of Agni and Soma, may I conquer; I propel myself forward by the impulse of strength.
May Agni and Soma drive away him who hates us and whom we hate; by the impulse of strength, I cast him out.

Following the victory of Indra and Agni, may I conquer. With the impulse of strength (*vāja*), I push it forward. May Indra and Agni drive away him who hates us and whom we hate; with the impulse of strength, I cast him out.

For the Vasus, thee! For the Rudras, thee! For the Ādityas, thee! May Heaven and Earth come to an understanding! May Mitra and Varuṇa favor thee with rain. May the birds go forth, licking what has been anointed. Go to the spotted mares of the Maruts; having become a speckled cow, go to heaven, and from there bring down rain for us. O Agni, you are the protector of sight; protect my sight.

O divine Agni, that enclosing-stick which you placed around yourself while being hidden by our hands—that very one I bring back to you according to your pleasure, so that it may not be alienated from you.
The beloved food of Agni has been drunk.

O great gods, you who partake in the flowing libations, you who stand upon the sacrificial grass and you who are stationed around the altar—receiving with favor all this speech, sit down upon this sacred grass and rejoice!
Svāhā! Vāṭ!

You two are the butter-dripping draft-horses; protect us. You two are in favor; place me in favor. O Sacrifice, homage to you! And come near, O auspicious one of the sacrifice; settle yourself in my well-offered oblation. May you settle yourself in my well-offered oblation.

O Agni, of unerring life-force, most cooling one, protect me from the lightning bolt; protect me from bondage; protect me from ill-sacrificed offerings; protect me from bad food. Make our nourishment free from poison. In a well-seated womb, Svāhā! Vāṭ! To Agni, Lord of Resting Places, Svāhā! To Sarasvatī, sister of glory, Svāhā!

You are the Veda; O God, by that [means] through which you became the Veda for the gods, by that may you become the Veda for me. O gods who know the way, having found the way, go upon the way. O Lord of the mind, O God, place this sacrifice in the wind—*svāhā*.

Let the sacrificial grass be anointed with the oblation of clarified butter; let it be united with the Ādityas, the Vasus, and the Maruts; let Indra be anointed together with the Viśvedevas; may that which is offered with *svāhā* go to the celestial sky.
Who releases you? He releases you. For whom does he release you? For him he releases you—for prosperity.
You are the portion of the Rākṣasas.

We have united with splendor, with nourishment, and with our bodies, and with a gracious mind. May Tvaṣṭṛ, the bounteous giver, bestow wealth upon us; may he smooth over whatever in our bodies is injured.

In the sky Viṣṇu strode out with the Jagatī metre; from there he has excluded him who hates us and whom we hate. In the intermediate space Viṣṇu strode out with the Jagatī metre; from there he has excluded him who hates us and whom we hate. On the earth Viṣṇu strode out with the Jagatī metre; from there he has excluded him who hates us and whom we hate. From this food, from this foundation, we have gone to the light; we have become united with the light.
You are self-existent, you are the best ray; you are the giver of splendor, grant me splendor. I turn following the turning of the sun.

O Agni, lord of the house, may I be a good lord of the house through you, O Agni, as lord of the house; may you be a good lord of the house through me, O Agni, as lord of the house. May our household duties not be deficient for a hundred winters. I turn according to the turning of the sun.
O Agni, Lord of Vows, I have performed the vow; I was able to do it, and it has been successful for me. Here I am, truly who I am.
Svāhā to Agni Kavyavāhana! Svāhā to Soma accompanied by the Pitṛs! The Asuras and Rakṣas who sit upon the sacrificial altar are struck down!
Those who, assuming various forms, being Asuras, move about by means of their own inherent power; those who carry away both outer forts and inner strongholds—Agni drives them forth from this world.
O ancestors, rejoice here; according to your respective portions, come forth like bulls. The ancestors have rejoiced; according to their respective portions, they have come forth like bulls.

Homage to you, O Fathers, for the sake of sap; homage to you, O Fathers, for the sake of withering; homage to you, O Fathers, for the sake of life; homage to you, O Fathers, for the sake of *svadhā*; homage to you, O Fathers, for the sake of the terrible; homage to you, O Fathers, for the sake of wrath; homage to you, O Fathers, homage to you, O Fathers! Give us houses, O Fathers; we give to you what we have, O Fathers. Put on this garment, O Fathers.
O Fathers, bestow the embryo, a boy wearing a lotus wreath, so that there may be a man here.
Carrying strength, nectar, clarified butter, milk, sweet drink, and flowing liquor—you are the *svadhā* offerings; satisfy my ancestors.
Honor Agni with fuel; awaken the guest with clarified butter; offer the oblations into him.
Offer intense clarified butter to the well-kindled flame, to Agni Jātavedas.
We strengthen you, O Aṅgiras, with fuel-sticks and with clarified butter; blaze brightly, O youngest one!
O beloved Agni, let the ladles, filled with oblations and dripping with ghee, approach you; graciously accept my fuel-sticks.
Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! Like the sky in its abundance, like the earth in its vastness.
Upon her back, O Earth, place of divine sacrifice, I establish Agni, the eater of food, for the sake of obtaining food.
This spotted bull has come; he has settled before his mother, and advancing toward heaven, he has reached his father.
Moving within the luminous realms, breathing out from his breath, the Great One has revealed the sky.
He shines across the thirty realms; speech is bestowed upon the Bird, day after day, through the days of the dawn.

Agni is light, light is Agni, svāhā! Sūrya is light, light is Sūrya, svāhā! Agni is splendor, light is splendor, svāhā! Sūrya is splendor, light is splendor, svāhā! Light is Sūrya, Sūrya is light, svāhā!
In harmony with the god Savitṛ, in harmony with the night that possesses Indra—may Agni, being pleased, partake; Svāhā!
In harmony with the god Savitṛ, in harmony with the Dawn accompanied by Indra—may Sūrya, being pleased, partake; Svāhā!
Approaching the sacrifice, let us address a prayer to Agni, who hears us even from afar.
Agni is the head of heaven, the summit, the lord of this earth; he quickens the seeds of the waters.
O Indra and Agni, I invoke you both; may you both rejoice together in the gift of wealth. You both are givers of food and riches; I call upon you both for the winning of booty.
This is your seasonal womb, from which once born you shone forth; knowing it, O Agni, ascend it, and then increase our wealth.

This one has been established here as the first by the ordainers, the most excellent invoker, to be praised at the sacrifices—he whom Apnavāna and the Bhṛgus caused to shine forth, the wonderful and pervasive one, for every clan within the woods.
Following his ancient splendor, the bold ones have milked the bright milk from the seer who wins a thousandfold.

O Agni, you are the protector of the body; protect my body. O Agni, you are the giver of life; give me life. O Agni, you are the giver of splendor; give me splendor. O Agni, whatever is deficient in my body, fill that up for me.

Kindling thee, may we kindle thee for a hundred winters, O radiant one; being full of vigor, may we kindle thee who art the creator of vigor; being powerful, may we kindle thee who art the creator of power, O Agni, the subduer of rivals—unassailable ones, may we kindle thee the unassailable. O thou of wondrous wealth, may I safely reach thy further shore.

O Agni, you have united with the splendor of the sun, with the hymn of the seers, and with that which is dear. May I unite with long life, with splendor, with offspring, and may I attain increase of wealth.

You are food; may I partake of your food. You are greatness; may I partake of your greatness. You are vigor; may I partake of your vigor. You are the increase of wealth; may I partake of your increase of wealth.
O Revatīs, rejoice in this womb, in this stall, in this world, in this dwelling!
Stay right here; do not go away.
You are the *saṃhitā*, possessing all forms; enter me with vigor and with lordship over cattle. O Agni, illuminator of the darkness, we come to you day by day with prayer, bringing homage.
Shining over the sacrifices, the radiant guardian of the cosmic order, increasing in his own abode.
O Agni, be easy of access to us as a father is to his son; attend to us for our well-being.
O Agni, be our closest friend, our protector, and our gracious refuge. As the Vasu Agni, renowned for wealth, come toward us and grant us most splendid riches.
O most radiant one, O shining one, we now entreat you for the welfare of our friends. As such, be mindful of us, hear our call, and deliver us from every harmful person.
Iḍā, come hither! Aditi, come hither!
Desired by you, may there be in me the fulfillment of your desires.
O Brahmaṇaspati, make Soma the one who hears our call, even as Kakṣīvat, the son of Uśij.
May he who is wealthy, the dispeller of disease, the finder of riches, and the increaser of prosperity—may he, the swift one, be with us.
Let not the curse of the stingy one, nor the treachery of a mortal, destroy us; protect us, O Brahmaṇaspati!
May the great, heavenly protection of the three—of Mitra, Aryaman, and Varuṇa—be ours; it is invincible.
For neither at home nor on the paths among the obstacles does the evil-speaking enemy have power over them.
For those sons of Aditi bestow eternal light upon the mortal so that he may live.
Never art thou barren, O Indra; thou never failest the worshipper. More and more, O Maghavan, is thy gift as a god increased.
We meditate upon that most excellent splendor of the divine Savitṛ; may he impel our thoughts.
May your unassailable chariot reach us from every side—the one with which you protect those who offer oblations.

Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! May I be rich in offspring through my children, rich in heroes through my men, and rich in nourishment through my possessions. O protector of men, guard my offspring; O worthy of praise, guard my cattle; O unwearied one, guard my food.
We have come to you, O omniscient one, who are the best finder of wealth for us; O Agni, sovereign ruler, bestow upon us splendor and power.
This Agni is the lord of the house, the Gārhapatya, the best finder of wealth for his progeny. O Agni, lord of the house, bestow upon us splendor and power.
This Agni of the soil is rich in wealth, the increaser of prosperity; O Agni of the soil, bestow upon us splendor and power.
O houses, do not fear, do not tremble; bringing strength, we come to you. Bringing strength, well-disposed and wise, I enter your houses with a joyful mind.
Those from whom one studies while living abroad, and in whom one has much goodwill—those houses we invoke; may they recognize us as we recognize them.

Invoked here are the cows; invoked are the goats and sheep. And so, the sweet essence of food is invoked in our homes. For your security and for peace, I enter what is auspicious, what is helpful, what brings well-being—well-being, well-being!
We invoke the voracious Maruts, the destroyers of enemies, who are in harmony with the groats.
Whatever sin we have committed in the village, whatever in the forest, whatever in the assembly, or whatever in the senses—this very sin we now expiate; *svāhā*!

O Indra, do not abandon us here in the battles along with the gods; for you, O impetuous one, possess this devotion. For the song of the one who offers oblations praises the Maruts—the offspring of that great and bounteous one.
Performers of ritual action, perform your work together with speech that brings well-being; having performed the work for the gods, go home, you who are companions.

O Avabhṛtha, O Nicumpuṇa, you are the gliding one, O Nicumpuṇa. Through the gods, I have washed away the sin committed against the gods; through mortals, I have washed away the sin committed against mortals. O God, protect me from the harm of the many-crying foe.
O ladle, fly away full; fly back again well-filled. Like two bargaining merchants, O Śatakratu, let us exchange food and strength.
Give to me; I give to you. Bestow upon me; I bestow upon you. You take away my tribute; I take away your tribute. Svāhā!
They have eaten and they have rejoiced; the dear ones have adorned themselves. The self-luminous inspired singers have offered praise with their settled hymn: now, O Indra, yoke your two bay steeds.
O Maghavan, we shall pay homage to you who are so beautiful to behold. Now, O you whose chariot-seat is full, being praised, you go according to your will; now, O Indra, yoke your two bay horses.
We now summon the mind with the Nārāśaṃsa hymn and with the prayers of the Fathers.
May our mind come back to us again for the sake of will, for strength, and for the oblation, so that we may behold the sun from the earth.
May our fathers and the divine folk grant us back our mind; may we be united with the company of the living.
O Soma, bearing your will within our bodies according to our sacred law, may we, possessing offspring, abide in your favor.
This, O Rudra, is your portion, together with your sister Ambikā; accept it, Svāhā! This, O Rudra, is your portion; the mouse is your sacrificial animal.
We entreat Rudra for mercy; we entreat the god Tryambaka for mercy, so that he may make us more prosperous, so that he may make us better, and so that he may cause us to attain our goals.
You are medicine; you are medicine for the cow, for the horse, and for man; you are medicine for the ram and the ewe. May there be well-being!
We worship Tryambaka, the fragrant, the increaser of prosperity. May I be liberated from death, as a cucumber from its stem, yet not be separated from immortality.
We worship Tryambaka, the fragrant, the bestower of husbands. May I be released from this world like a cucumber from its stem, but not from that [other] world.
This, O Rudra, is your provision; with it, pass beyond the Mūjavat mountains. With your bow unstrung, carrying the Pināka staff, clothed in a skin, and being auspicious, pass by without harming us.
The triple life-span of Jamadagni, the triple life-span of Kaśyapa; that which is the triple life-span among the gods—may that triple life-span be ours.

Thou art named Śiva; the axe is thy father; homage be unto thee! Do not harm me. I turn thee down for the sake of food-eating, procreation, increase of wealth, possession of good offspring, and heroic vigor.

We have come to this place of sacrifice on earth, where all the gods took delight; crossing over by means of the *Ṛg*, *Sāman*, and *Yajus* verses, may we rejoice in the increase of wealth and in nourishment. May these divine waters be auspicious to me! O Herb, protect him! O Axe, do not harm him!

May the Waters, our mothers, purify us; may those who cleanse with ghee purify us with ghee. For these goddesses carry away every impurity. From them, bright and purified, I emerge. You are the body of consecration and austerity; as such, I clothe myself in you, the auspicious and effective one, nourishing my blessed form.
You are the milk of the earth; you are the giver of luster, grant me luster. You are the pupil of Vṛtra’s eye; you are the giver of sight, grant me sight.

May the Lord of Thought purify me; may the Lord of Speech purify me; may the divine Savitṛ purify me with a flawless filter, with the rays of the sun. O Lord of the Filter, purified by your filter, whatever desire I purify myself for, may I be able to accomplish that.
O Gods, we seek your favor as the sacrifice proceeds; O Gods worthy of worship, we invoke you for our blessings.
Svāhā! [I offer] the sacrifice from the mind. Svāhā! From the wide mid-air. Svāhā! To Heaven and Earth. Svāhā! I take hold from the wind; Svāhā!

To Ākūti, to Prayuj, to Agni, Svāhā! To Medhā, to Manas, to Agni, Svāhā! To Dīkṣā, to Tapas, to Agni, Svāhā! To Sarasvatī, to Pūṣan, to Agni, Svāhā! O divine waters, vast, bringing welfare to all; O Heaven and Earth, O wide atmosphere! Let us worship Bṛhaspati with an oblation, Svāhā!
May every mortal choose the friendship of the divine leader; everyone strives for wealth, and may he choose glory so that he may prosper—svāhā!

You two are the artistic forms of the Ṛg and Sāman; I take hold of you both. May you two protect me until the conclusion of this sacrifice. You are a refuge; grant me refuge. Homage be to you; do not harm me.

Thou art strength, belonging to Aṅgiras; soft as wool, bestow strength upon me. Thou art the hem of Soma’s garment. Thou art the protection of Viṣṇu; be a protection for the sacrificer. Thou art the womb of Indra. Make the harvests and the ploughings fruitful. Rise up, O Lord of the Forest; standing erect, protect me from distress until the conclusion of this sacrifice.

Perform the vow! Agni is the Brahman, Agni is the sacrifice, the holy Vanaspati. We meditate upon the divine thought, the most gracious, for our aid—the bestower of splendor, the bearer of the sacrifice. May it be well-guided in our control. Those gods who are born of mind, yoked by mind, whose will is their power—may they protect us, may they guard us; to them, Svāhā!
O Waters, when drunk, become refreshing; be very kind within our bellies. May those divine, immortal waters—increasers of Truth, free from disease, free from sickness, and sinless—be sweet for us.
This is your sacrificial body; I release the waters, not the offspring. Released from distress and consecrated with *svāhā*, enter the earth; become one with the earth.
O Agni, you be well awake; may we be well exhilarated. Protect us with undivided attention, and restore us to wakefulness again.

May mind come back to me, may life-span come back to me; may breath come back to me, may the self come back to me; may sight come back to me, may hearing come back to me. May Agni Vaiśvānara, the undeceived protector of the body, protect us from misfortune and from blame.

O Agni, you are the guardian of vows, a god among mortals; you are to be praised at the sacrifices. Grant us this much, O Soma, bring more! May the divine Savitṛ, the giver of wealth, bestow riches upon us.
This is your body, O Śukra; this is your luster. Be united with it; go to radiance. You are swift, held by the mind, and beloved by Viṣṇu.
In the impulse of that [Soma] of true impulsion, may I attain the control of my body; Svāhā! You are bright, you are radiant, you are immortal, you belong to all the gods.

You are consciousness, you are thought, you are meditation, you are the sacrificial fee, you are the ruling power, you are worthy of sacrifice, you are Aditi, whose head is on both sides. As such, be favorable to us when we advance and favorable when we return. May Mitra bind you by the foot; may Pūṣan protect you on the paths for Indra, the overseer.
May your mother approve of you, may your father, may your brother born of the same womb, and may your friend belonging to the same herd approve of you.
Go to the god, O goddess; for Indra, bring the Soma; may Rudra turn you back; with well-being and the Soma as your friend, come back again.
You are Vasvī, you are Aditi, you are Ādityā, you are Rudrā, you are Candrā. May Bṛhaspati cause you to rest in happiness; Rudra with the Vasus has looked upon you with favor.

I sprinkle you upon the head of Aditi, on the earth’s place of sacrifice to the gods; you are the footprint of Iḍā, full of ghee—svāhā! Rejoice in us! Our kinship is with us! In you are riches; in me are riches! May we not be separated from the abundance of wealth! From there come riches!
I have been united with the divine wisdom and with the far-seeing Dakṣiṇā. Do not steal away my life, nor may I steal yours. O Goddess, may I find a hero in your sight.

"Tell Soma for me: 'This is your Gāyatra portion'; tell Soma for me: 'This is your Triṣṭubh portion'; tell Soma for me: 'This is your Jagatī portion'; tell Soma for me: 'May he attain sovereignty over the names of the meters.'"
Thou art ours; thy bright portion is to be taken up; may they separate thee who are already separated.
I praise that god Savitar between the two worlds, the one of prophetic wisdom, whose impulse is true, the bestower of jewels, the beloved sage of inspired thought.
He whose lofty splendor has shone forth at his impulsion—the golden-handed one of good wisdom has measured out the light with his form.
For the sake of the subjects, I take you.
May the subjects breathe after you; may you breathe after the subjects.

I buy you, the bright, with the bright; the radiant, with the radiant; the immortal, with the immortal. Yours is the cow for the assembly; yours are the radiant [gems] for us. You are the body of ascetic heat, the form of Prajāpati; you are bought with the supreme animal. May I thrive with thousandfold prosperity.

Come to us as a friend, bestowing good friendship; enter the right thigh of Indra, desiring him who desires you, being pleasant to him who is pleasant to you. O Svāna, Bhrāja, Aṅghāri, Bambhāri, Hasta, Suhasta, Kṛśānu—these are your Soma-purchasers; guard them, let them not deceive you.
O Agni, protect me from evil conduct; grant me a share in good conduct. With long life and a full span of life, I have arisen following the immortals.
We have set out upon the path that leads to well-being and is free from danger, by which one avoids all enemies and finds wealth.

Thou art the skin of Aditi; sit upon the seat of Aditi. The Bull has propped up the sky and measured out the breadth of the mid-region; the Sovereign has taken his seat over all beings—all these are the ordinances of Varuṇa.
Varuṇa has spread the mid-air across the forests; he placed speed in horses, milk in the cows, mental power in hearts, fire among the people, the sun in heaven, and Soma upon the mountain.
Ascend the eye of the sun, the pupil of the eye of Agni, where you move with your rays, shining brightly, O wise one.
O two oxen, come hither; be yoked as draft-animals, tearless and not slayers of heroes, inciters of sacred prayer. Go in safety to the house of the sacrificer.
You are auspicious for me; descend, O Lord of the World, toward all your stations.
May those who lie in ambush not find you; may those who waylay you not find you; may the malevolent wolves not find you.
Becoming a hawk, fly away; go to the house of the sacrificer. That is prepared for us both.
Homage to the eye of Mitra and Varuṇa! Pay worship to that great god; proclaim it as the Truth (Ṛta) to Sūrya, the far-seeing, the banner born of the gods, the son of Heaven.
Thou art the upstayer of Varuṇa. Ye two are the releasers of the pillar of Varuṇa. Thou art the seat of Varuṇa’s Truth. Thou art the abode of Varuṇa’s Truth. Sit upon the abode of Varuṇa’s Truth.

Those abodes of yours which they worship with oblation—may all those encompass this sacrifice. Increasing our wealth, furthering us, possessing brave sons, and not slaying our heroes, O Soma, enter the dwellings.

Thou art the body of Agni; for Viṣṇu, thee! Thou art the body of Soma; for Viṣṇu, thee! Thou art the hospitality of the guest; for Viṣṇu, for the falcon that brings the Soma, thee! For Agni, thee! For Viṣṇu, the giver of increase of wealth, thee!

Thou art the birthplace of Agni. Ye two are the testicles. Thou art Urvaśī. Thou art Āyu. Thou art Purūravas. I churn thee with the Gāyatrī metre; I churn thee with the Triṣṭubh metre; I churn thee with the Jagatī metre.
Be of one mind with us, of one heart, and stainless; do not harm the sacrifice nor the lord of the sacrifice, O Jātavedas; be auspicious to us today.

Fire moves, having entered into fire; the son of the seers, the protector against curses. May he, being gracious, sacrifice for us here with a well-performed sacrifice; may he, never neglecting it, carry the oblation to the gods—svāhā!

I take you for the one who falls upon, for the one who falls around; for Tanūnapāt, for the powerful Śākvara, for the most mighty. You are unassailed, the unassailable vigor of the gods; you are beyond reproach, the protector against reproach, and yourself beyond reproach. May I straightway attain truth; place me in well-being.

O Agni, guardian of vows, you are the guardian of vows. That body of yours which is here, let it be in me; that body of mine which is here, let it be in you. O Lord of Vows, may our vows be united. May the Lord of Consecration approve my consecration; may the Lord of Penance approve my penance.

Portion by portion, O divine Soma, may you swell for Indra, the winner of the sole prize. May Indra swell for you; may you swell for Indra. Swell us, your friends, with gain and with wisdom. O divine Soma, may I attain well-being through your pressing.
Desired riches for the impulse and for fortune; truth for those who speak the truth; homage to Heaven and Earth!

O Agni, that body of yours which lies in iron, most lofty, dwelling in the abyss—may it drive away the fierce word, may it drive away the dazzling word; Svāhā! O Agni, that body of yours which lies in dust, most lofty, dwelling in the abyss—may it drive away the fierce word, may it drive away the dazzling word; Svāhā! O Agni, that body of yours which lies in gold, most lofty, dwelling in the abyss—may it drive away the fierce word, may it drive away the dazzling word; Svāhā!

Thou art my path of heat; thou art my path of wealth. Save me from distress; save me from agitation. Agni has found Nabhas by name. O Agni Aṅgiras, come hither with life as thy name! Whatever invincible, sacrifice-worthy name thou hast on this earth, with that I establish thee. Agni has found Nabhas by name. O Agni Aṅgiras, come hither with life as thy name! Whatever invincible, sacrifice-worthy name thou hast on the second earth, with that I establish thee. Agni has found Nabhas by name. O Agni Aṅgiras, come hither with life as thy name! Whatever invincible, sacrifice-worthy name thou hast on the third earth, with that I establish thee. [I follow] thee for the feast of the gods.
Thou art a lioness, subduing rivals; be prepared for the gods. Thou art a lioness, subduing rivals; be purified for the gods. Thou art a lioness, subduing rivals; be adorned for the gods.

May Indraghoṣa protect you from the east with the Vasus; may Pracetas protect you from the west with the Rudras; may Manojava protect you from the south with the Pitṛs; may Viśvakarman protect you from the north with the Ādityas. Here I cast out this heated water away from the sacrifice.

Thou art a lioness, svāhā! Thou art a lioness, winning the Ādityas, svāhā! Thou art a lioness, winning the Brahman and winning the Kṣatra, svāhā! Thou art a lioness, winning good offspring and winning the increase of wealth, svāhā! Thou art a lioness; bring the gods for the sacrificer, svāhā! For the beings, thee!
You are firm; make the earth firm. You are of firm abode; make the intermediate region firm. You are of unshakable abode; make the sky firm. You are the loose soil of Agni.

The inspired priests harness their minds and harness their thoughts for the sake of the great, inspired, wise one. He alone, the knower of the sacred ways, ordains the priestly functions. Great indeed is the praise of the divine Savitṛ. Svāhā!
Vishnu strode across this; in three places he planted his step. It is gathered together in his footstep-dust. Svāhā!

For you two have become expansive, rich in milch-cows, providing good pasture for Manu as a favor. O Viṣṇu, you have propped apart these two worlds; you have supported the earth on all sides with your rays. Svāhā!

O you who are heard by the gods, proclaim among the gods! Moving eastward, prepare the sacrifice; lead the rite upward; do not falter! Speak to your own stall, O divine dwellings; do not speak away our life-span, do not speak away our progeny! Rejoice here upon the summit of the earth.
Now, indeed, shall I proclaim the heroic deeds of Viṣṇu, who measured out the earthly realms; he who, striding out in three steps, the wide-strider, propped up the highest dwelling-place.
For Viṣṇu, you!
O Viṣṇu, from heaven or from earth, or from the great and wide mid-air, O Viṣṇu, fill both your hands with wealth; bestow it from the right hand and from the left.
For Viṣṇu, you!
For that heroic deed Viṣṇu is praised, like a fearsome wild beast that wanders and dwells in the mountains; he upon whose three wide strides all worlds abide.
You are the forehead of Viṣṇu. You two are the corners of Viṣṇu’s mouth. You are the needle of Viṣṇu. You are the fixed point of Viṣṇu. You belong to Viṣṇu; for Viṣṇu, you!

At the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins and the hands of Pūṣan, I take you up. You are a woman. Here I cut off the necks of the Rākṣasas. You are great, you have a great sound; utter a great voice for Indra!

The slayer of demons, the destroyer of secret spells, belonging to Viṣṇu. Here do I dig up that secret spell which a stranger or a kinsman has buried for me; here do I dig up that secret spell which one who is equal to me or one who is unequal to me has buried for me; here do I dig up that secret spell which one who is related to me or one who is unrelated to me has buried for me; here do I dig up that secret spell which one who is born of the same lineage as me or one who is not born of the same lineage as me has buried for me. I dig up the sorcery.
You are self-ruling; you are the ruler of the sacrificial session, the slayer of the arrogant. You are the ruler of the people, the slayer of demons. You are the ruler of all, the slayer of enemies.

I sprinkle you, the slayers of Rakṣases, the destroyers of secret spells, belonging to Viṣṇu. I pour you down, the slayers of Rakṣases, the destroyers of secret spells, belonging to Viṣṇu. I spread you out, the slayers of Rakṣases, the destroyers of secret spells, belonging to Viṣṇu. I place you two down, the slayers of Rakṣases, the destroyers of secret spells, belonging to Viṣṇu. I pile you around, the slayer of Rakṣases, the destroyer of secret spells, belonging to Viṣṇu. You belong to Viṣṇu; you all belong to Viṣṇu.

At the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins, with the hands of Pūṣan, I take thee. Thou art a woman. Here do I cut off the necks of the Rākṣasas. Thou art barley; bar away from us hatred, bar away enemies. For heaven thee, for the atmosphere thee, for the earth thee! May the worlds, the seats of the fathers, be purified. Thou art the seat of the fathers.

Support the sky, fill the mid-air, and be firm upon the earth. May the radiant Maruts set thee up, and may Mitra and Varuṇa with steadfast law. Desiring spiritual power, desiring princely power, and desiring the increase of wealth, I enclose thee. Make firm the spiritual power, make firm the princely power, make firm life, and make firm progeny.
You are firm; may this sacrificer be firm in this dwelling-place with offspring and cattle. May Heaven and Earth be filled with clarified butter. You are the roof of Indra, the shade for all people.
May these songs encompass you on every side, O lover of song; may these increases follow after your long life, and may these delights be pleasing to you.
You are the needle of Indra; you are the fixed point of Indra; you belong to Indra; you belong to the Viśvedevas.
You are the pervasive one, the carrier away; you are the bearer, the conveyer of the oblation. You are the strengthening one, the wise; you are Tutha, the knower of all.

You are the eager one, the sage; you are the swift one, the supporter; you are the seeker of aid, the worshipper; you are the purifier, the place of cleansing; you are the sovereign ruler, the archer; you are the one to be approached, the flowing one; you are the cloud, the swift mover; you are the cleansed one, the preparer of the oblation; you are the abode of Truth, the light of heaven.

Thou art the ocean, all-encompassing. Thou art Aja Ekapād. Thou art the serpent of the deep. Thou art speech; thou art Indra’s; thou art the seat. O two doors of the Eternal Order, do not consume me! O Lord of the paths, lead me forward; may there be well-being for me on this path that leads to the gods.

Behold me with the eye of a friend! O Agnis, you are the Sagaras; you are the Sagaras by name. With your fierce host, O Agnis, protect me! Sustain me, O Agnis; guard me! Homage be to you! Do not harm me!

You are light, multiformed; you are the kindling-stick of all the gods. O Soma, you are the wide-extending protector against bodily injuries and against hostilities wrought by others. Svāhā! May the swift one, enjoying the clarified butter, partake of it. Svāhā!
O Agni, lead us by a good path to wealth, O God who knows all ways; remove from us the sin that leads astray, and we shall offer you the most abundant homage.
May this Agni create wide space for us; may he go before us, shattering our adversaries. May he win prizes in the contest for booty; may he, exulting, conquer the enemies. Svāhā!
O Viṣṇu, stride out widely; make wide room for our dwelling. O you whose source is ghee, drink the ghee; prolong the life of the lord of the sacrifice—svāhā!

O God Savitṛ, this is your Soma; protect it, let them not deceive you. O divine Soma, as a god you have approached the gods; here I, along with the increase of wealth, approach men. Svāhā! I am released from the bonds of Varuṇa.

O Agni, guardian of vows, you are the guardian of vows. That body of yours which was in me—let it now be in you; that body of mine which was in you—let it now be in me. O Lord of Vows, according to their respective order, let our vows be fulfilled. May the Lord of Consecration approve my consecration, and may the Lord of Austerity approve my austerity.
Stride out widely, O Viṣṇu; make wide room for our dwelling. Drink the clarified butter, O you whose source is clarified butter; prolong the life of the lord of the sacrifice—svāhā!

I have passed beyond one [set of people], I have not approached another; I have found you on this side of those who are beyond, and beyond those who are below. We delight in you, O divine Lord of the Forest, for the sacrifice to the gods; may the gods delight in you for the sacrifice to the gods. For Viṣṇu, I take you! O Plant, protect him! O Axe, do not harm him!

Do not scratch the sky; do not harm the mid-air; become one with the earth. For this well-sharpened axe has brought you forward for great good fortune. Therefore, O divine Lord of the Forest, grow forth with a hundred branches; may we grow forth with a thousand branches.

At the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins and the hands of Pūṣan, I take thee. Thou art a woman. Here do I cut off the necks of the Rākṣasas. Thou art barley; bar away from us our haters, bar away our enemies. For the sky thee, for the atmosphere thee, for the earth thee! May the worlds, the seats of the fathers, be purified. Thou art the seat of the fathers.

You are the leader, easy of access for the Unnetṛs; may he know this, for he shall stand upon you. May the god Savitṛ anoint you with honey. For the plants with good fruit. With your top you have touched heaven, with your middle you have filled the atmosphere, with your base you have made firm the earth.
Those abodes of yours which we desire to reach, where the many-horned, tireless cows dwell—there indeed has been set down that highest step of the wide-striding Viṣṇu, full of abundance.
I enclose you, the winner of the Brahman, the winner of the Kṣatra, the winner of the increase of wealth. Make firm the Brahman; make firm the Kṣatra; make firm life; make firm progeny.
Behold the deeds of Viṣṇu, through which he has made his vows manifest; he is the close ally and friend of Indra.
The wise ever behold that supreme abode of Viṣṇu, like an eye extended in the sky.

You are the encircler; may the divine subjects encircle you, and may the riches of men encircle this sacrificer. You are the son of heaven. This is your place upon the earth; the wild animal is your sacrificial victim.
Thou art the invoker. The divine clans, the eager ones, the best of bearers, have approached the gods. O God Tvaṣṭṛ, delight in the wealth; may the oblations be sweet to thee.
O Revatī, rejoice; O Bṛhaspati, bestow riches! I bind you, O divine oblation, with the noose of Ṛta; be bold, O mortal!

At the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins and the hands of Pūṣan, I bind you, acceptable to Agni and Soma. For the waters and for the plants; may your mother permit you, may your father permit you, may your brother born of the same womb permit you, may your friend of the same herd permit you. I sprinkle you, acceptable to Agni and Soma.

Thou art the drinker of the waters. May the divine waters sweeten [this], which is already well-prepared, the oblation for the gods. Let thy breath unite with the wind; let thy limbs unite with the sacrificial vessels; let the lord of the sacrifice unite with his blessing.

Anointed with ghee, protect the animals! O wealthy one, bestow what is dear upon the sacrificer; enter him. From the wide mid-air, in harmony with the divine Vāta, sacrifice this oblation yourself; become one with his body. Bestow the sacrifice upon the sacrificer in this most excellent sacrifice. Svāhā to the gods! To the gods, svāhā!
May you not become a viper, may you not become a serpent. Homage to you, O stretched-out one; go forward, unhindered, along the streams of ghee, following the paths of Truth.
O divine waters, pure ones, carry us well-served among the gods; may we, being well-served, become providers for others.
I purify your speech; I purify your breath; I purify your eye; I purify your ear; I purify your navel; I purify your penis; I purify your anus; I purify your limbs.

May your mind swell; may your speech swell; may your breath swell; may your eye swell; may your ear swell. Whatever in you is harsh, whatever is solidified—may that swell for you, may it settle down; may that be purified for you. Peace to the days! O herb, protect him! O axe, do not harm him!

Thou art the portion of the Rākṣasas. The Rākṣasa is cast out. Here I trample upon the Rākṣasa; here I drive away the Rākṣasa; here I lead the Rākṣasa to the lowest darkness. O Heaven and Earth, cover yourselves with clarified butter! O Vāyu, do thou accept the drops. May Agni accept the clarified butter, Svāhā! To that which is consecrated by Svāhā, go ye to the Maruts of the upward sky.

O Waters, carry away this which is blameworthy and this which is impure; whatever treachery or falsehood I have committed, and whatever cruel oath I have sworn—may the Waters and Pavamāna release me from that sin.

May your mind unite with the [sacrificer's] mind, and your breath with his breath. You are the *reṭ* (the cauldron); may Agni cook you; may the waters have united with you. For the speed of Vāta, for the rush of Pūṣan, may the heat cause [your enemy] to tremble. May hatred be cast away.

O drinkers of clarified butter, drink the clarified butter; O drinkers of fat, drink the fat. You are the oblation of the intermediate space; *svāhā*! To the quarters! To the intermediate quarters! To the directed quarters! To the intermediate directions! To the upward quarters! To the quarters, *svāhā*!

May Indra’s out-breath settle within every limb; may Indra’s in-breath be established in every limb. O divine Tvaṣṭṛ, let your many forms come together, so that what is of diverse form may become uniform. As you go among the gods for protection, may your friends, your mother, and your father rejoice after you.

Go to the ocean, svāhā! Go to the intermediate space, svāhā! Go to the god Savitṛ, svāhā! Go to Mitra and Varuṇa, svāhā! Go to day and night, svāhā! Go to the meters, svāhā! Go to heaven and earth, svāhā! Go to the sacrifice, svāhā! Go to Soma, svāhā! Go to the celestial sky, svāhā! Go to Agni Vaiśvānara, svāhā! Grant me mind and heart. Let your smoke go to heaven, let your light go to the sun, and fill the earth with your ashes, svāhā!

Do not harm the waters, do not harm the plants. O King Varuṇa, from every place release us. Since we swear by "the inviolable ones" and by "Varuṇa," from that, O Varuṇa, release us. May the waters and the plants be friendly to us; may they be unfriendly to him who hates us and whom we hate.
These waters are rich in oblation; he who offers the oblation desires to win them. May the divine sacrifice be rich in oblation, and may Sūrya be rich in oblation.

I set you down in the seat of Agni, whose house is unassailable. You are the portion of Indra and Agni; you are the portion of Mitra and Varuṇa; you are the portion of all the gods. Those [waters] which are near the sun, or those with which the sun is joined—may they speed our sacrifice.
For the heart thee, for the mind thee, for the sky thee, for the sun thee! Lift up this sacrifice; bestow the priestly offices upon the gods in heaven.

O King Soma, descend upon all creatures; let all creatures descend upon you. May Agni hear my call with his fuel; may the Waters and the divine Dhiṣaṇās hear; may the pressing-stones hear the sacrifice as those who know; may the god Savitṛ hear my call. Svāhā!

O divine Waters, O Child of the Waters, that wave of yours which is purifying, endowed with power, and most intoxicating—give that to the gods among the gods, to those drinkers of the bright [Soma], whose portion you are; Svāhā!
Thou art a furrow. I lead thee up for the imperishability of the ocean. The waters have united with the waters; the plants with the plants.
O Agni, that mortal whom you protect in battles and whom you urge on in the contests for booty—he shall be the master of eternal nourishments. Svāhā!

At the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins and the hands of Pūṣan, I take you up. You are the giver; make this sacrifice deep for Indra, most excellently prepared. With your supreme blade, [make it] full of vigor, honeyed, and rich in milk. You are the Nigrābhya waters, heard by the gods; satisfy me!
Satisfy my mind; satisfy my speech; satisfy my breath; satisfy my sight; satisfy my hearing; satisfy my self; satisfy my offspring; satisfy my cattle; satisfy my hosts; may my hosts not be thirsty.

For Indra, accompanied by the Vasus and the Rudras, thee! For Indra, accompanied by the Ādityas, thee! For Indra, the slayer of the adversary, thee! For the Śyena, the bearer of Soma, thee! For Agni, the bestower of the increase of wealth, thee!
O Soma, whatever light is yours in heaven, whatever on earth, and whatever in the broad mid-air—with that, create wide space for wealth for this sacrificer; speak in favor of the giver.
You are refreshing, subduers of Vṛtra, delighting in bounty, wives of immortality. O goddesses, being invited, lead this sacrifice to the gods; drink of the Soma.
Do not fear, do not tremble; take up strength, O Earth! Being firm, may you two stand fast; bestow strength. Evil is struck down, not Soma.
From the east, from the west, from the north, from the south—from all directions, let them run toward you! O Mother, look down; may we find our kin.
O most powerful god, you indeed have granted favor to the mortal; O Maghavan, there is no other than you who is a comforter, O Indra—I speak these words to you.
Flow for the Lord of Speech, purified by the hands from the stalks of the bull; as a god, flow for the gods whose portion you are.
Make our nourishments full of sweetness. O Soma, that invincible and watchful name of yours which exists—unto that name of yours, O Soma, to Soma, Svāhā! Svāhā! I follow along the wide mid-air.

Thou art consecrated by thy own self for all the powers of sense, celestial and terrestrial; may Tvaṣṭṛ fashion thee with the mind! Svāhā! To the auspicious Sun, thee! To the gods who drink the rays of light, thee! O divine portion, for whomsoever I invoke thee, let that be true! By the downward-flowing crushing blow, may he be struck down—phaṭ! For out-breathing, thee! For diffused breathing, thee!
You are taken with a support; O Maghavan, restrain [the senses], protect the Soma; guard our wealth, perform this sacrifice.
I place you between heaven and earth; I place you within the wide intermediate space. Rejoicing with the gods, both those below and those above, O Maghavan, take your delight in the Antaryāma cup!

Thou art consecrated by thy own self for all the faculties, celestial and terrestrial; may the mind fashion thee; Svāhā! To the auspicious Sun, thee! For the gods who drink the rays of light, thee! For the upward breath (udāna), thee!

Come hither, O drinker of the pure, and adorn yourself for us; a thousand are your teams, O possessor of all boons. To you is offered the exhilarating juice, of which, O God, you have the first draught. For Vāyu, you!

O Indra and Vāyu, these [Soma juices] have been pressed; come hither with refreshments, for the drops long for you both. You are taken with a support: I take you for Vāyu, for Indra and Vāyu. This is your resting place: I take you for the two who are in harmony.
O Mitra and Varuna, you who increase the Truth, this Soma has been pressed for you; hear my invocation here! You are taken with a support; I take you for Mitra and Varuna.

May we, the kings, rejoice together with our offspring through the oblation, O gods, as cattle do through pasture. O Mitra and Varuna, grant us for all days that cow who never falters. This is your womb; I set you down for the two seekers of Truth.

O Aśvins, with that whip of yours which is honey-sweet and full of true bounty, sprinkle the sacrifice. You are taken with a support; I take you for the two Aśvins. This is your resting place; I take you for the two lovers of sweetness.

As of old, as formerly, as always, as now—[I draw] him who sits upon the sacrificial grass, the finder of heaven, the supreme one; for the sake of milking the facing enclosure, the roaring, swift, victorious one, through whom you grow strong. You are taken with a support; for Śaṇḍa, you! This is your womb; protect heroism! Śaṇḍa is wiped away. May the gods, the drinkers of the bright [Soma], accept you! You are unassailable.

O hero, generating heroes, go around the sacrificer with the abundance of wealth; uniting with heaven and earth, O bright one, with your bright luster. Śaṇḍa is cast out. You are the station of Śukra.
O divine Soma, may we be the givers of unimpaired heroic power and the abundance of wealth. That is the first consecration, possessing all boons; that is the first Varuṇa, Mitra, and Agni.
He is the first Bṛhaspati, the wise one; offer the pressed [juice] to that Indra—svāhā!
May the oblations of honey be satisfied—those which are well-offered, well-pleased, and well-poured with *svāhā*. The *agnīdh* has sacrificed.

This Vena impels the daughters of Pṛśni, whose womb is light, in the measurement of the mid-air; at the meeting-place of the waters and the sun, the wise ones lick him with their prayers as if he were a young child.
You are taken with a support; I take you for Marka.
In whose invocations you two, with sharp minds, hasten with power to accept the inspired hymns; he who, possessing great manly vigor, has placed the arrow-shaft in his hand according to his will.
This is your source; protect the subjects. Marka has been wiped away. May the gods who drink from the *manthin* cup lead you forward. You are unassailable.

Producing offspring of good progeny, go around the sacrificer with the abundance of wealth. Joining with heaven and earth, O *manthin*, you are churned with your radiant glow. Marka is cast out. You are the station of the *manthin*.
O gods who are eleven in heaven, you who are eleven upon the earth, you who dwell in the waters, eleven by your greatness—O gods, may you graciously accept this sacrifice.

You are taken with a support; you are the Āgrayaṇa, the best of the Āgrayaṇas. Protect the sacrifice, protect the lord of the sacrifice. May Viṣṇu protect you with his power; protect Viṣṇu; protect the pressings.

Soma purifies himself; Soma purifies himself for this priesthood, for this nobility, for this sacrificer who presses the juice. He purifies himself for food and strength; he purifies himself for the waters and the plants; he purifies himself for heaven and earth; he purifies himself for well-being. I take you for all the gods. This is your womb; I take you for all the gods.

You are taken with a support; for Indra, the mighty and full of vigor, I take you who are worthy of praise. That which is your great vigor, O Indra—for that I take you; for Viṣṇu I take you. This is your seat; for the hymns I take you; for the gods I take you, the one who favors the gods; for the life of the sacrifice I take you.

I take you, who favor the gods, for Mitra and Varuṇa, for the long life of the sacrifice. I take you, who favor the gods, for Indra, for the long life of the sacrifice. I take you, who favor the gods, for Indra and Agni, for the long life of the sacrifice. I take you, who favor the gods, for Indra and Varuṇa, for the long life of the sacrifice. I take you, who favor the gods, for Indra and Bṛhaspati, for the long life of the sacrifice. I take you, who favor the gods, for Indra and Viṣṇu, for the long life of the sacrifice.
The gods have generated Agni Vaiśvānara—the head of heaven, the steward of earth, born in the cosmic order (ṛta)—the seer, the sovereign, the guest of men, as a vessel for their mouths.

You are taken with a support; you are the firm one, dwelling in firmness, the firmest of the firm, the most immovable of the immovable. This is your birthplace; for Vaiśvānara, I take you. With a firm mind and speech, I pour down the firm Soma. Then may Indra make our people free from rivals and of one mind.

Whatever drop of yours falls away, whatever stalk of yours, shaken by the pressing-stones, from the lap of the two bowls, or from the Adhvaryu, or from the filter—that I offer with my mind, consecrated by the *vaṣaṭ* call, *svāhā*. You are the upward path of the gods.

Granting splendor to my out-breath, flow pure for the sake of splendor! Granting splendor to my diffused breath, flow pure for the sake of splendor! Granting splendor to my up-breath, flow pure for the sake of splendor! Granting splendor to my speech, flow pure for the sake of splendor! Granting splendor to my will and skill, flow pure for the sake of splendor! Granting splendor to my hearing, flow pure for the sake of splendor! Granting splendor to my two eyes, flow pure for the sake of splendor!

Granting splendor to my self, flow pure for splendor; granting splendor to my vigor, flow pure for splendor; granting splendor to my life-span, flow pure for splendor; granting splendor to all my offspring, flow pure both of you for splendor.

Who are you? Which one are you? To whom do you belong? What is your name? We have meditated upon your name; we have satisfied you with Soma. Bhūr Bhuvaḥ Svaḥ! May I be rich in offspring through my children, rich in heroes through my men, and rich in nourishment through my possessions.

You are taken with a support; for Madhu, you! You are taken with a support; for Mādhava, you! You are taken with a support; for Śukra, you! You are taken with a support; for Śuci, you! You are taken with a support; for Nabhas, you! You are taken with a support; for Nabhasya, you! You are taken with a support; for Iṣ, you! You are taken with a support; for Ūrj, you! You are taken with a support; for Sahas, you! You are taken with a support; for Sahasya, you! You are taken with a support; for Tapas, you! You are taken with a support; for Tapasya, you! You are taken with a support; for Aṃhasaspati, you!
O Indra and Agni, come to the pressed juice, to the desirable cloud through our songs; drink of this, impelled by our prayer.
You are taken with a support; for Indra and Agni, you! This is your womb; for Indra and Agni, you!

Hither come those who kindle Agni and spread the sacrificial grass in due order—those whose friend is Indra the youthful. You are taken with a support; for Agni and Indra, you! This is your womb; for Agni and Indra, you!

O protectors of the people, all you gods, come hither; you who give, [come] to the pressed juice of the giver. You are taken with a support: for all the gods, I take you. This is your resting place: for all the gods, I take you.

O All-Gods, come hither; hear this my invocation. Sit down upon this sacred grass (barhis). You are taken with a support; I take you for the All-Gods. This is your resting place; I take you for the All-Gods.

O Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, drink the Soma here, just as you drank of the pressed juice at Śāryāta’s sacrifice. Under your guidance and in your protection, O Hero, the sages skilled in sacrifice seek to win your favor.
You are taken with a support; for Indra accompanied by the Maruts, you! This is your resting place; for Indra accompanied by the Maruts, you!

The bull accompanied by the Maruts, who has grown great, the one whose power is never failing, the divine ruler Indra, the all-conquering, the fierce, the giver of victory—him we invoke here for new protection.

You are taken with a support; for Indra accompanied by the Maruts, you! This is your resting place; for Indra accompanied by the Maruts, you! You are taken with a support; for the vigor of the Maruts, you!
O Indra, rejoicing together with the Maruts as your host, drink the Soma, O wise hero, slayer of Vṛtra! Slay the enemies, drive away the adversaries, and then grant us safety from every side.
You are taken with a support; for Indra accompanied by the Maruts, you! This is your birthplace; for Indra accompanied by the Maruts, you!
O Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, a bull for the fray, drink the Soma according to your wont for exhilaration. Pour the wave of sweetness into your belly; you are the king of the Soma-pressings.
You are taken with a support; for Indra accompanied by the Maruts, you! This is your birthplace; for Indra accompanied by the Maruts, you!

In the great [battle], Indra, like a man, comes to the aid of the people; moreover, doubly vast and undiminished in his powers, he has grown toward us for heroic deeds. Broad and wide, he has been made well-fashioned by the makers.
You are taken with a support; I take you for Mahendra. This is your womb; I take you for Mahendra.
Indra has grown great through the hymns of Vatsa, like Parjanya rich in rain by his own might.
You are taken with a support; for Mahendra you! This is your womb; for Mahendra you!
Upward indeed his rays bear him, that god who knows all beings, the Sun, so that everyone may behold him; Svāhā!
The brilliant face of the gods has risen—the eye of Mitra, Varuṇa, and Agni. Sūrya, the soul of all that moves and stands, has filled the heaven, the earth, and the mid-air. Svāhā!
O Agni, lead us by a good path to wealth, O God, you who know all ways. Drive away from us the sin that leads astray; we shall offer to you the most abundant homage. Svāhā!
May this Agni grant us wide space; may he go before us, shattering our adversaries. May he win prizes in the contest for booty; may he, exulting, conquer our enemies. Svāhā!

With form have I come unto your form; may Tutha, the all-knowing, distribute you. Go forth by the path of Truth, O you whose sacrificial fees are radiant! Behold the sun, behold the mid-air! Strive with those who sit in the assembly.
Today may I find a Brahmin who has a father and grandfathers, who is a seer and the descendant of seers, and who is worthy of a well-placed sacrificial fee. O gifts, go to the gods; enter the donor.

May Varuṇa give you to me for Agni; may I attain immortality. Be life to the giver, and joy to me, the receiver. May Varuṇa give you to me for Rudra; may I attain immortality. Be breath to the giver, and vigor to me, the receiver. May Varuṇa give you to me for Bṛhaspati; may I attain immortality. Be skin to the giver, and joy to me, the receiver. May Varuṇa give you to me for Yama; may I attain immortality. Be a horse to the giver, and vigor to me, the receiver.
Who gave? To whom did he give? Desire gave; it was given to desire. Desire is the giver; desire is the receiver. O Desire, this is yours.
Thou art taken with a support; for the Ādityas, thee! O Viṣṇu of wide stride, this is thy Soma; guard it, let them not deceive thee.
Never art thou barren, O Indra; thou never failest the worshipper. More and more, O Maghavan, thy bounty as a god is now poured forth.
For the Ādityas, you!
Never do you neglect; you protect both races of beings. O Āditya, your fourth libation is your power; immortality has taken its place in heaven. For the Ādityas, I take you.

The sacrifice goes toward the favor of the gods; O Ādityas, be gracious! May your benevolence turn hitherward, which is the best finder of wide space even from distress. For the Ādityas, you [are taken].

O Vivasvat Āditya, this is your draught of Soma; rejoice therein! O men, give credence to this word, when the husband and wife, bestowing blessings, enjoy what is desirable. A male son is born, he acquires wealth, and thereafter he prospers every day in his house with offspring.

O Savitṛ, grant us what is auspicious today, and what is auspicious tomorrow, and what is auspicious day by day. For, O God, through this prayer, may we become partakers of the auspicious and abundant dwelling.

You are taken with a support; you belong to Savitṛ; you are the bestower of delight. You are the bestower of delight; bestow delight upon me! Quicken the sacrifice, quicken the lord of the sacrifice for the sake of fortune. For the god Savitṛ, I take you.
You are taken with a support; you are a good refuge, well-established. Homage to Bṛhadukṣa! For all the gods, you are taken. This is your womb; for all the gods, you are taken.

You are taken with a support; O divine Soma, may I succeed in drawing these cups of your juice—the Indra-strengthening, accompanied by the wives—which belong to Bṛhaspati’s son. I am above, I am below; that which is the intermediate space has become my father. I have beheld the sun on both sides, and I [behold] that which is the supreme secret of the gods.

O Agni, accompanied by the wives [of the gods], in harmony with the god Tvaṣṭṛ, drink the Soma—svāhā! You are Prajāpati, the bull, the depositor of seed; place seed within me. May I obtain the seed-depositing power of you, the bull Prajāpati, the depositor of seed.

You are taken with a support; you are the tawny one, the yoker of the tawny steeds; for the two tawny steeds, I take you. You are the parched grains for the two tawny steeds, together with Soma, for Indra.

That portion of yours which wins horses, that which wins cattle—of that, which has had the *yajus* offered, the *soma* pressed, the *uktha* recited, and which has been invited, I, being invited, partake.

You are the expiation for sin committed against the gods; you are the expiation for sin committed against men; you are the expiation for sin committed against the ancestors; you are the expiation for sin committed by oneself; you are the expiation for every sin. You are the expiation for all that sin which I have committed knowingly and that which I have committed unknowingly.

We have united with splendor, with nourishment, and with our bodies, and with a gracious mind. May Tvaṣṭṛ, the bounteous giver, bestow wealth upon us; may he smooth over whatever in our bodies is injured.

O Indra, unite us with a favorable mind, with cattle, with wise patrons, O Maghavan, and with well-being; unite us with the sacred prayer (brahman) created by the gods, and with the benevolent favor of the gods worthy of sacrifice. Svāhā!

We have united with splendor, with nourishment, and with our bodies; we have united with a gracious mind. May Tvaṣṭṛ, the bounteous giver, bestow wealth upon us and smooth over whatever in our bodies is injured.
May Dhātṛ, Rāti, Savitṛ, Prajāpati, the god Agni the guardian of treasures, Tvaṣṭṛ, and Viṣṇu, bestowing harmony through progeny, grant wealth to the sacrificer—svāhā!
O gods, we have prepared easy paths for you who have come to this libation with favor; bearing and bringing the oblations, O Vasus, bestow riches upon us—svāhā!

O divine Agni, send those gods whom you have brought here according to their desire to their own dwelling place; having all eaten and drunk, may they abide in life, in the cosmic order, and in the light—svāhā!

For we have chosen you here, O Agni, as the Hotṛ-priest at this proceeding sacrifice. You have sacrificed successfully and performed the rites successfully; knowing the way, come to the sacrifice as one who knows. Svāhā!
O gods who know the way, having found the way, go upon the way. O Lord of the Mind, O God, place this sacrifice in the wind with the cry of Svāhā!

O sacrifice, go to the sacrifice; go to the lord of the sacrifice; go to your own source; svāhā! This is your sacrifice, O lord of the sacrifice, accompanied by the hymn of praise and possessing all heroes; enjoy it; svāhā!

May you not become a viper, may you not become a snake! For King Varuṇa has made a broad path for the sun to follow. He has provided feet to set down where there was no place to stand; he is the deliverer even from that which pierces the heart. Homage to Varuṇa! May the noose of Varuṇa pass me by.

The face of Agni has entered the waters; O Son of the Waters, protect the divine power. In every house, O Agni, you shall sacrifice the fuel; let your tongue rise up toward the clarified butter—Svāhā!

In the ocean is your heart, within the waters; may the plants and the waters enter into you. O Lord of Sacrifice, we shall honor you with well-spoken hymns and words of homage at the sacrifice, when the *svāhā* is uttered.
O divine Waters, this is your embryo; bear it well-pleased and well-sustained. O divine Soma, this is your place; bestow peace upon it and protect it all around.

O Avabhṛtha, O Nicumpuṇa, you are the gliding one, the Nicumpuṇa. Through the gods, I have washed away the sin committed against the gods; through mortals, the sin committed against mortals. O God, protect me from the harm of the far-roaring [enemy].
You are the kindling-stick of the gods.
Let the ten-month-old embryo move forth together with the afterbirth; just as this wind moves, just as the ocean moves, so let this ten-month-old one be born together with the afterbirth.
To her whose embryo is worthy of sacrifice, whose womb is golden, and whose limbs are uninjured—to her, I have brought him together with his mother; *svāhā*!

The wise Indu, the much-subduing one of manifold forms, has clothed himself in greatness within. May the worlds spread out along her—one-footed, two-footed, three-footed, four-footed, and eight-footed—svāhā!
O Maruts, great in splendor, that man in whose dwelling you drink from heaven is indeed the most well-guarded of people.
May Heaven and Earth and the broad Mid-world bedew this sacrifice of ours; may they fill us with nourishments.
Mount the chariot, O slayer of Vṛtra; your two bay horses have been yoked by our prayer. May the pressing-stone, with its roar, turn your mind toward us.
You are taken with a support; for Indra, the sixteenfold one, you are taken. This is your womb; for Indra, the sixteenfold one, you are placed.
Yoke, O Indra, your two long-maned, vigorous bay horses that fill out their girths; then, O Soma-drinker, come to listen to our songs.
You are taken with a support; for Indra, the sixteenfold, you! This is your womb; for Indra, the sixteenfold, you!
The two bay steeds carry Indra, whose power is unassailable, toward the praises of the seers and toward the sacrifice of human beings.
You are taken with a support; for Indra, the sixteenfold one, you are taken. This is your womb; for Indra, the sixteenfold one, you are placed.
Since there is no other born higher than he who has entered into all beings—Prajāpati, rejoicing in his offspring—he, the sixteenfold one, accompanies the three lights.

Indra the sovereign and Varuṇa the king—those two have made this your first portion. Following their consumption, I consume it; may the goddess Vāc, being pleased, be satisfied with the Soma. Together with the vital breath, Svāhā!
O Agni, purify yourself with skillful hands; bestow upon us splendor and heroic strength, granting me wealth and nourishment.
You are taken with a support; for Agni, you, for splendor! This is your womb; for Agni, you, for splendor! O Agni, radiant one, you are radiant among the gods; may I become radiant among men.

Rising up with vigor, having drunk [the Soma], you shook your jaws, O Indra, after drinking the Soma pressed in the vessel. You are taken with a support; for Indra, for his vigor! This is your womb; for Indra, for his vigor! O Indra, most powerful among the gods, may I become the most powerful among men.
His banners have become visible; his rays extend across the people, shining like blazing fires.

You are taken with a support; for Sūrya, the radiant, you! This is your womb; for Sūrya, the radiant, you! O Sūrya, most radiant one, you are the most radiant among the gods; may I be the most radiant among men.
Upward his rays bear that god Jātavedas, the Sun, so that everyone may behold him.

You are taken with a support; for Sūrya, the radiant, you! This is your womb; for Sūrya, the radiant, you! O Sūrya, most radiant one, you are the most radiant among the gods; may I become the most radiant among men.
May she who yields a thousandfold with her broad stream of milk flow for me; may wealth come back to me again.
O Iḍā, Rantī, Havyā, Kāmyā, Candrā, Jyotī, Aditi, Sarasvatī, Mahī, Viśrutī—these are your names, O inviolable one; announce me as a doer of good deeds to the gods.
O Indra, strike down our adversaries; cast those who attack us low. Whoever seeks to harm us, send him down into the deepest darkness.
You are taken with a support; for Indra, the dispeller of foes, you! This is your womb; for Indra, the dispeller of foes, you!

Let us invoke today, for our protection in the struggle for booty, the Lord of Speech, Viśvakarman, who is swift as thought; may he, the source of all well-being and the performer of righteous deeds, graciously accept all our invocations for our aid.
You are taken with a support; for Indra Viśvakarman, you! This is your resting place; for Indra Viśvakarman, you!
O Viśvakarman, by means of the strengthening oblation, you made Indra a protector who is invincible; to him the many tribes bowed down, so that he might be this formidable one, worthy of invocation.
You are taken with a support; for Indra Viśvakarman you. This is your resting place; for Indra Viśvakarman you.

You are taken with a support; I take you for Agni, whose meter is the Gāyatrī. I take you for Indra, whose meter is the Triṣṭubh. I take you for the All-Gods, whose meter is the Jagatī. The Anuṣṭubh is your song of praise.

I shake you at the flight-path of the Vr̥śīs; I shake you at the flight-path of the Kūkānanās; I shake you at the flight-path of the Bhandanas; I shake you at the flight-path of the most intoxicating [Soma-stems]; I shake you at the flight-path of the most honey-sweet [Soma-stems]. I shake you, the bright one, as the bright one, in the form of the day, in the rays of the sun.
