Upon the peak shines the great form of the bull; the bright one is the precursor of the bright, Soma is the precursor of Soma. O Soma, that invincible and watchful name of yours—into that I take you. To that name of yours, O Soma, to Soma, Svāhā!

O divine Soma, you are the yearning one; go to the beloved abode of Agni. O divine Soma, you are the self-controlled one; go to the beloved abode of Indra. O divine Soma, you are our friend; go to the beloved abode of all the gods.

Here is delight; here do ye rejoice; here is steadfastness, here self-steadfastness, Svāhā! Bestowing support upon the mother, he who supports the mother while sucking—may he maintain for us the increase of wealth, Svāhā!
The success of the sacrifice has come to us; we have reached the light and become immortal. We have ascended from earth to heaven; we have found the gods, the sun, and the light.

O Indra and Parvata, you who fight in the vanguard, strike down each and every one who would attack us; strike him down with the thunderbolt, strike him down! May it be a deep abyss for the one who flees afar, which he may seek to reach. O Hero, may the destroyer rend our enemies on all sides; may he rend them from every direction.
Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! May we be rich in offspring through our children, rich in heroes through our men, and rich in nourishment through our possessions.

Parameṣṭhin is designated when speech is uttered; Prajāpati when it has been spoken; Andha Accheta when [the Soma] is sought; Savitṛ during the winning of the prize; Viśvakarman during the consecration; and Pūṣan during the purchase of the Soma-cow.

Indra and the Maruts are when he has stood up for purchase; the Asura is when he is being bargained for; Mitra is when he has been purchased; Viṣṇu Śipiviṣṭa is when he has been seated upon the lap; Viṣṇu Narandhiṣ is when he is being carried forth.
Soma has arrived; Varuṇa is seated upon the throne-seat; Agni is at the Āgnīdhra fire-altar; Indra is at the oblation-holder; Atharvan is being brought down.

The All-Gods are deposited in the stalks; Viṣṇu, the protector of the consecrated, is being replenished; Yama is being pressed; Viṣṇu is being gathered; Vāyu is being purified; Śukra is purified; Śukra is mixed with milk; Manthin is mixed with barley-meal.

The Viśve Devas are [the Soma] drawn up into the cups; Asura is [the Soma] raised for the oblation; Rudra is [the Soma] being offered; Vāta is [the Soma] turned toward [the sacrificer]; Nṛcakṣas is [the Soma] looked upon; Bhakṣa is [the Soma] being consumed; the Pitṛs are the Nārāśamsas when [the vessels] have been set down.

The Sindhu is prepared for the final purificatory bath; the ocean is being brought down; the waters are overflowing. By whose power the regions were propped up, who by their heroic deeds are most manly and most mighty; they who rule unopposed through their strengths—O Viṣṇu and Varuṇa, come at the first invocation!

The sacrifice has gone to the gods and the heaven; from that may wealth come to me. The sacrifice has gone to men and the intermediate space; from that may wealth come to me. The sacrifice has gone to the ancestors and the earth; from that may wealth come to me. To whatever world the sacrifice has gone, from that may prosperity be mine.

The thirty-four threads which have been stretched out, they who sustain this sacrifice with their own inherent power—of them I join together what has been severed; Svāhā! Let the Gharma-offering go unto the gods.

The milking of the sacrifice has been extended in many places; it has spread across the sky in eight ways. O Sacrifice, milk forth for me great abundance in progeny; may I attain all life and the increase of wealth—svāhā!
Flow forth, O Soma, bringing gold, horses, and heroes; bring us strength consisting of cattle. Svāhā!

O God Savitṛ, impel the sacrifice; impel the lord of the sacrifice for his good fortune. May the divine Gandharva, the purifier of intentions, purify our intention; may the Lord of Speech make our strength palatable. Svāhā!

Thee, who dwellest in the firm, who dwellest among men, who dwellest in the mind—I have taken thee with a support; I take thee, acceptable to Indra. This is thy womb; for Indra, thee, the most acceptable. Thee, who dwellest in the waters, who dwellest in the clarified butter, who dwellest in the sky—I have taken thee with a support; I take thee, acceptable to Indra. This is thy womb; for Indra, thee, the most acceptable. Thee, who dwellest on earth, who dwellest in the intermediate space, who dwellest in heaven, who dwellest among the gods, who dwellest in the firmament—I have taken thee with a support; I take thee, acceptable to Indra. This is thy womb; for Indra, thee, the most acceptable.
The essence of the waters that rises upward, which is gathered within the sun—the most excellent essence of that essence of the waters, that I take for you.
You are taken with a support; I take you, acceptable to Indra. This is your womb; for Indra, you who are most acceptable.

The planets, the offerings of strength, bestowing thought upon the sage—of you, those with beautiful jaws, I have seized the food and the strength. You are taken with a support; I take you, acceptable to Indra. This is your womb; for Indra, I take you, most acceptable. You two are united; unite me with prosperity. You two are separated; separate me from evil.

Thou art Indra’s thunderbolt, the winner of booty; may this man win booty through thee. Now, at the impulse of booty, we celebrate with our speech the great Mother, named Aditi, in whom this entire world has entered; may the god Savitṛ impel for us the sacred law within her.

Within the waters is immortality, within the waters is healing; and in the praises of the waters, O horses, become winners of the prize. O divine Waters, that wave of yours which is victorious, humped, and a winner of the prize—with that, may this man win the prize.
The wind, or the mind, or the twenty-seven Gandharvas—they first yoked the horse; they placed speed in it.

Become swift as the wind, O steed, when you are harnessed; be present for glory like Indra’s own right-hand horse. May the Maruts, possessors of all wealth, harness you; may Tvaṣṭṛ bestow speed in your feet.

O vigorous steed, with that speed of yours which is placed in secret, which was bestowed upon the falcon and moved within the wind—with that power, O vigorous one, become strong for us and a winner of prizes; and be one who carries us across in the assembly.
O strong ones, winners of the prize, about to win the prize, smell the portion of Bṛhaspati.

By the impulse of God Savitṛ, of true impulse, may I ascend the highest heaven of Bṛhaspati. By the impulse of God Savitṛ, of true impulse, may I ascend the highest heaven of Indra. By the impulse of God Savitṛ, of true procreation, I have ascended the highest heaven of Bṛhaspati. By the impulse of God Savitṛ, of true procreation, I have ascended the highest heaven of Indra.
O Bṛhaspati, win the prize! Speak the word for Bṛhaspati; cause Bṛhaspati to win the prize! O Indra, win the prize! Speak the word for Indra; cause Indra to win the prize!

This was that true speech of yours by which you caused Bṛhaspati to win the prize; you have caused Bṛhaspati to win the prize—O trees, be unyoked! This was that true speech of yours by which you caused Indra to win the prize; you have caused Indra to win the prize—O trees, be unyoked!

By the impulse of God Savitṛ, whose impulsion is true, may I win the prize of Bṛhaspati, the winner of the prize. O prize-winning steeds, supporting the path and measuring out the stages, go to the goal!
This vigorous steed, bound by the neck, at the flanks, and in the mouth, hastens toward the whip. Dadhikrā, exerting his will, springs along, leaping over the joints of the paths. Svāhā!
And indeed, as he runs and hastens, the wind blows after him like the wing of a bird eager for prey; like a swooping falcon, Dadhikrāvan crosses over the shoulder with his might—*svāhā*.

May the Vājins be auspicious to us in our invocations, they who are swift as measured paces, well-praised in the assembly of the gods; crushing the serpent, the wolf, and the demons, may they utterly drive away diseases from us.

May all those coursers, who hear our invocation, hear our call—the swift ones of measured speed, winners of thousands, eager for gain at the winning of the prize, they who have won great wealth in battles.

In every contest for booty, O swift steeds, protect us—you who are wise, immortal, and knowers of the Eternal Order. Drink of this honeyed mead and rejoice; being satisfied, go by the paths traveled by the gods.
May the impulse of strength come to me; may Heaven and Earth, the two of all forms, come hither; may my father and mother both come to me, and may Soma come to me with immortality.
O vigorous ones, winners of the prize, who have run for the prize, smell the portion of Bṛhaspati while rubbing yourselves clean.

To Āpi, svāhā! To Svāpi, svāhā! To Āpija, svāhā! To Kratu, svāhā! To Vasu, svāhā! To the Lord of Day, svāhā! To the bewildered Day, svāhā! To the bewildered Vinamśin, svāhā! To Vinamśin Āntyāyana, svāhā! To Antya Bhauvana, svāhā! To the Lord of the World, svāhā! To the Overlord, svāhā!

May life be perfected through sacrifice; may breath be perfected through sacrifice; may sight be perfected through sacrifice; may hearing be perfected through sacrifice; may the back be perfected through sacrifice; may sacrifice itself be perfected through sacrifice. We have become the offspring of Prajāpati; we have gone to the light, O gods; we have become immortal.

May your Indra-power be with us; may our manly strength and will be with us; may splendors be yours. Homage to Mother Earth! Homage to Mother Earth! This is your sovereign power. You are the controller, the restrainer; you are firm, the supporter. For cultivation I take you, for security I take you, for wealth I take you, for prosperity I take you.
This impulse of strength first brought forth King Soma among the plants and in the waters; may they be sweet for us, and may we, as domestic priests, remain watchful in the kingdom. Svāhā!

The impulse of strength has taken its stand upon this heaven and all these worlds, O Sovereign. Knowing [the way], he causes him who is unwilling to give to give; may he bestow upon us wealth consisting of all-heroic sons. Svāhā!
Now has the impulse of strength come forth, encompassing all these worlds on every side; the wise King moves around the perimeter, increasing our progeny and prosperity—*svāhā*!
To the Ādityas, Viṣṇu, Sūrya, Brahmā, and Bṛhaspati, Svāhā!
Impel Aryaman, Bṛhaspati, and Indra to bestow gifts; impel Vāc, Viṣṇu, Sarasvatī, and the vigorous Savitṛ—svāhā!
O Agni, speak for us here; be well-disposed toward us. Bestow upon us, O winner of thousands, for you are the giver of wealth. Svāhā!
May Aryaman grant us [it], may Pūṣan, may Bṛhaspati; may the goddess Vāc grant it to us—svāhā!

At the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins, with the hands of Pūṣan, I place you within the restraint of Sarasvatī, the controller of speech. With the sovereignty of Bṛhaspati, I consecrate you, O [Name]!

Agni won the breath with the one-syllable [word]; may I win it back. The Aśvins won bipeds, human beings, with the two-syllable [word]; may I win them back. Viṣṇu won the three worlds with the three-syllable [word]; may I win them back. Soma won four-footed cattle with the four-syllable [word]; may I win them back.

Pūṣan won the five directions with the five-syllable [meter]; may I win them. Savitṛ won the six seasons with the six-syllable [meter]; may I win them. The Maruts won the seven domestic animals with the seven-syllable [meter]; may I win them. Bṛhaspati won the Gāyatrī with the eight-syllable [meter]; may I win it.

Mitra won the *trivṛt* stoma with the nine-syllable [meter]; may I win it. Varuṇa won the *virāj* with the ten-syllable [meter]; may I win it. Indra won the *triṣṭubh* with the eleven-syllable [meter]; may I win it. The Viśve Devas won the *jagatī* with the twelve-syllable [meter]; may I win it.

By means of thirteen syllables, the Vasus won the thirteenth *stoma*; may I win it. By means of fourteen syllables, the Rudras won the fourteenth *stoma*; may I win it. By means of fifteen syllables, the Ādityas won the fifteenth *stoma*; may I win it. By means of sixteen syllables, Aditi won the sixteenth *stoma*; may I win it. By means of seventeen syllables, Prajāpati won the seventeenth *stoma*; may I win it.

This is your portion, O Nirṛti; accept it, svāhā! To the gods whose leader is Agni, who sit in the east, svāhā! To the gods whose leader is Yama, who sit in the south, svāhā! To the gods whose leaders are the Viśvedevas, who sit in the west, svāhā! To the gods whose leaders are Mitra and Varuṇa—or whose leaders are the Maruts—who sit in the north, svāhā! To the gods whose leader is Soma, who sit above and offer worship, svāhā!

To those gods who have Agni as their leader, who sit in the east—to them, Svāhā! To those gods who have Yama as their leader, who sit in the south—to them, Svāhā! To those gods who have the Viśvedevas as their leaders, who sit in the west—to them, Svāhā! To those gods who have Mitra and Varuṇa as their leaders, or the Maruts as their leaders, who sit in the north—to them, Svāhā! To those gods who have Soma as their leader, who sit above and are worthy of worship—to them, Svāhā!
O Agni, overcome the hostile armies, casting away those who attack; invincible, crossing over the godless ones, bestow splendor upon the bearer of the sacrifice.

At the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins and the hands of Pūṣan, I offer you with the power of Upāṃśu; the Rākṣasa is slain, Svāhā! For the destruction of the Rākṣasas, I offer you. We have slain the Rākṣasa; we have slain so-and-so. He is slain!

May Savitṛ impel you among those who impel; Agni among the householders; Soma among the lords of the forest; Bṛhaspati for speech; Indra for preeminence; Rudra for cattle; Mitra as the truthful one; and Varuṇa among the lords of dharma.

O gods, consecrate this man who seeks the breath of life for great sovereignty, for great preeminence, for great lordship over the people, and for the power of Indra. This is the son of so-and-so, the son of so-and-so; for this people, he is your king. Soma is the king of us Brāhmaṇas.
The divine waters, rich in sweetness, full of vigor, and shining as sovereigns, have been taken up—those with which they anointed Mitra and Varuṇa, and with which they led Indra beyond his enemies.

You are the wave of Vṛṣan, the giver of sovereignty; grant sovereignty to me, svāhā! You are the wave of Vṛṣan, the giver of sovereignty; grant sovereignty to so-and-so! You are Vṛṣasena, the giver of sovereignty; grant sovereignty to me, svāhā! You are Vṛṣasena, the giver of sovereignty; grant sovereignty to so-and-so!

You are purposeful, givers of sovereignty; grant me sovereignty, svāhā! You are purposeful, givers of sovereignty; grant sovereignty to [Name]! You are powerful, givers of sovereignty; grant me sovereignty, svāhā! You are powerful, givers of sovereignty; grant sovereignty to [Name]! You are waters that flow around, givers of sovereignty; grant me sovereignty, svāhā! You are waters that flow around, givers of sovereignty; grant sovereignty to [Name]! You are the lord of the waters, giver of sovereignty; give me sovereignty, svāhā! You are the lord of the waters, giver of sovereignty; give sovereignty to [Name]! You are the embryo of the waters, giver of sovereignty; give me sovereignty, svāhā! You are the embryo of the waters, giver of sovereignty; give sovereignty to [Name]!

You are sun-skinned, givers of sovereignty; grant me sovereignty, svāhā! You are sun-skinned, givers of sovereignty; grant sovereignty to so-and-so. You are sun-bright, givers of sovereignty; grant me sovereignty, svāhā! You are sun-bright, givers of sovereignty; grant sovereignty to so-and-so. You are gladdening, givers of sovereignty; grant me sovereignty, svāhā! You are gladdening, givers of sovereignty; grant sovereignty to so-and-so. You dwell in the fold, givers of sovereignty; grant me sovereignty, svāhā! You dwell in the fold, givers of sovereignty; grant sovereignty to so-and-so. You are lowing, givers of sovereignty; grant me sovereignty, svāhā! You are lowing, givers of sovereignty; grant sovereignty to so-and-so. You are most powerful, givers of sovereignty; grant me sovereignty, svāhā! You are most powerful, givers of sovereignty; grant sovereignty to so-and-so. You are mighty, givers of sovereignty; grant me sovereignty, svāhā! You are mighty, givers of sovereignty; grant sovereignty to so-and-so. You support the people, givers of sovereignty; grant me sovereignty, svāhā! You support the people, givers of sovereignty; grant sovereignty to so-and-so. You support all, givers of sovereignty; grant me sovereignty, svāhā! You support all, givers of sovereignty; grant sovereignty to so-and-so. O Waters, you are self-ruling, givers of sovereignty; grant sovereignty to so-and-so. Let the honeyed ones be mixed with the honeyed, winning great dominion for the Kṣatriya. Sit down, unassailable, endowed with power, bestowing great dominion upon the Kṣatriya.

You are the splendor of Soma; may my splendor be like yours. Svāhā to Agni! Svāhā to Soma! Svāhā to Savitṛ! Svāhā to Sarasvatī! Svāhā to Pūṣan! Svāhā to Bṛhaspati! Svāhā to Indra! Svāhā to Ghoṣa! Svāhā to Śloka! Svāhā to Aṃśa! Svāhā to Bhaga! Svāhā to Aryaman!

You two are the purifiers, belonging to Viṣṇu. At the impulse of Savitṛ, I purify you with a flawless purifier, with the rays of the sun. You are unassailable, the kinsman of speech, born of austerity; you are the gift of Soma. Svāhā to the royal waters!

These waters, gladdening in their company, resplendent, unassailable, active, and clothed in their own power—Varuṇa has made his dwelling-place within them; he, the infant of the waters, is within those who are most motherly.

You are the caul of the Kṣatra; you are the amnion of the Kṣatra; you are the womb of the Kṣatra; you are the navel of the Kṣatra. You are Indra’s slayer of Vṛtra; you belong to Mitra; you belong to Varuṇa. Through you, may this man smite Vṛtra. You are a piercer; you are a breaker; you are a crusher. Protect him facing forward; protect him facing backward; protect him facing crosswise; protect him from all directions.

They have been made manifest. Agni, the lord of the household, has been made manifest. Indra, of far-reaching fame, has been made manifest. Mitra and Varuṇa, whose laws are firm, have been made manifest. Pūṣan, the knower of all, has been made manifest. Heaven and Earth, the sources of universal well-being, have been made manifest. Aditi, the wide-sheltering one, has been made manifest.
The biting serpents have been driven away. Ascend the eastern direction; may the Gāyatrī protect you, the Rathantara Sāman, the Trivṛt Stoma, the spring season, and the Brahman as your wealth.
Ascend the south; may the Triṣṭubh meter protect you, the Bṛhat Sāman, the Pañcadaśa Stoma, the Grīṣma season, and the Kṣatra as your wealth.
Ascend the western quarter; let the Jagatī metre protect you, the Vairūpa Sāman, the seventeenfold Stoma, the rainy season, and the people as your wealth.
Ascend to the north; may the Anuṣṭubh protect you, the Vairāja Sāman, the Ekaviṃśa Stoma, the autumn season, and the fruit as the wealth.

Climb upward; may the *paṅkti* meter protect you, the *śākvara* and *raivata* *sāmans*, the *triṇava* and *trayastrim̐śa* *stomas*, and the seasons of winter and the cool season; [grant] splendor and wealth. The head of Namuci has been cast down.
You are the splendor of Soma; may my splendor be like yours. Protect me from death. You are vigor, you are power, you are immortality.
O Indra, at the dawning of the golden-hued Uṣas, you and Sūrya have both arisen. Ascend the chariot-seat, O Varuṇa and Mitra; from there, behold both Aditi and Diti.
You are Mitra; you are Varuṇa.

I consecrate you with the splendor of Soma, with the brilliance of Agni, with the luster of Sūrya, and with the power of Indra. Be the lord of rulers among rulers; protect yourself against the missiles.

O gods, consecrate this man who has no rival for great sovereignty, for great preeminence, for great lordship over the people, and for the power of Indra. This is the son of so-and-so, the son of so-and-so; he is the king of this people. Soma is the king of us Brāhmaṇas.

From the back of the mountain, the bull, the ships move forth, flowing with their own moisture; they have turned downward after having been drawn upward, following the serpent of the deep as they flow along.
Thou art the wide stride of Viṣṇu; thou art the step of Viṣṇu; thou art the stride of Viṣṇu.

O Prajāpati, none other than you has encompassed all these forms. Whatever desire we have when we offer to you, may that be ours. This one is the father of that one; that one is the father of this one. May we be masters of riches! Svāhā! O Rudra, that which is your active, supreme name—in that [name] you are offered; you are sacrificed to; you are the fire! Svāhā!

Thou art the thunderbolt of Indra. By the command of Mitra and Varuṇa, the two directors, I yoke thee. For steadfastness thee, for self-sustenance thee—unharmed, white, through the impulse of the Maruts, conquer! We have attained [thee] with our mind; we have united with vital power.

O Indra, O vanquisher of the swift, may we not, through lack of devotion and through failure to offer prayers, suffer while unyoked before you. Mount the chariot which you, O wielder of the thunderbolt, shall ascend, O God, as you take up the reins for your own well-trained horses.

To Agni, the lord of the household, svāhā! To Soma, the lord of the forest, svāhā! To the vigor of the Maruts, svāhā! To the power of Indra, svāhā! O Earth, my mother, do not harm me, nor may I harm you.

The swan dwelling in purity, the Vasu dwelling in the atmosphere, the Hotṛ-priest dwelling on the altar, the guest dwelling in the house; dwelling among men, dwelling in the best of places, dwelling in Truth, dwelling in the sky; born of the waters, born of the kine, born of Truth, born of the mountains—the Great Truth.

So much is your life; bestow that life upon me. You are a yoke; you are splendor; bestow splendor upon me. You are vigor; bestow vigor upon me. I draw you both down toward the arms of Indra, the performer of heroic deeds.
Thou art pleasant; thou art a good seat. Thou art the womb of sovereignty. Sit upon the pleasant one; sit upon the good seat; sit upon the womb of sovereignty.
Varuṇa, whose law is ghee, has sat down in his dwellings for sovereign rule, he who is of excellent wisdom.

Thou art the conqueror; may these five directions be favorable to thee. Thou art the Brahman, thou art the Brahman; thou art Savitṛ, whose procreation is truth. Thou art Varuṇa, whose power is truth. Thou art Indra, whose power is the people. Thou art Rudra, the most gracious. O doer of much, maker of prosperity, maker of abundance! Thou art the thunderbolt of Indra; with that, prosper me.

May Agni Pṛthu, the lord of the sacred law, being pleased, accept the clarified butter—Svāhā! Having been consecrated with Svāhā, strive together with the rays of the sun for the preeminence among your kinsmen.

Impelled by Savitṛ the impeller, by Sarasvatī with speech, by Tvaṣṭṛ with forms, by Pūṣan with cattle, by Indra for us, by Bṛhaspati with sacred formulation, by Varuṇa with vigor, by Agni with splendor, by Soma the king, and by Viṣṇu—the tenth deity—I creep forward, being impelled.
Be prepared for the Aśvins; be prepared for Sarasvatī; be prepared for Indra, the Good Protector. Purified by the filter, Vāyu is Soma flowing forth; he is the worthy friend of Indra.

O Agni, surely you will provide for those who possess the grain, just as they reap it in due order, separating it out; bring here and there the food of those who offer worship with reverence upon the sacred grass.
You are taken with a support; for the Aśvins you, for Sarasvatī you, for Indra the Good Protector you!
O Aśvins, lords of splendor, drinking the Surā together with Namuci the Asura, you two aided Indra in his heroic deeds.

Like parents for their son, both Aśvins protected you, O Indra, with their poetic wisdom and wondrous deeds; when you drank the intoxicating Soma with your powers, Sarasvatī refreshed you, O Maghavan.
Harnessing his mind for the first time and fixing his thought upon the Truth, Savitṛ, having perceived the light of Agni, brought it forth from the earth.
With a disciplined mind, we [act] at the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with power for the sake of heaven.
Having yoked the gods who travel through the sun by means of his wisdom toward heaven, Savitṛ impels them as they are about to create the great light.

The inspired poets harness their mind and they harness their thoughts for the sake of the great, inspired, wise one. He alone, the knower of the ways, ordains the priestly functions; great indeed is the praise of the god Savitṛ.

I yoke for you both an ancient prayer with prostrations; let the hymn go forth like a path to the patron. May all the sons of immortality hear it, they who have taken up their stations in the celestial realms.
After whose departure all other gods have followed according to the majesty of that god with his power—he, the divine Savitṛ, the steed Etaśa, who measured out the earthly regions by his greatness.

O God Savitṛ, impel the sacrifice; impel the lord of the sacrifice for his portion. May the celestial Gandharva, the purifier of intentions, purify our intention; may the Lord of Speech make our speech sweet.

O God Savitṛ, lead this sacrifice of ours forward—this one that wins the gods, finds friends, conquers all, wins wealth, and wins the light of heaven. Accomplish the hymn with the verse; through the Gāyatra, [accomplish] the Rathantara and the Bṛhat, which follow the path of the Gāyatra. Svāhā!

At the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins and the hands of Pūṣan, I take thee. With the Gāyatrī metre, in the manner of Aṅgiras, from the seat of the earth, bring hither Agni Purīṣya in the manner of Aṅgiras, with the Triṣṭubh metre, in the manner of Aṅgiras.
You are the spade, you are the woman; with you may we be able to dig for Agni in his dwelling-place, according to the Jāgata metre, in the manner of Aṅgiras.
Having taken it in his hand, Savitṛ, bearing a golden spade and perceiving the light of Agni, bring it forth from the earth.
With the Anuṣṭubh metre, in the manner of Aṅgiras.
O swift steed, run forward along the widest expanse; your highest birth is in heaven, your navel is in the intermediate space, and your womb is upon the earth.
Yoke the donkey, O you two possessors of wealth, for this journey, as it carries Agni who is well-disposed toward us.
In every endeavor and in every contest for booty, we, as friends, invoke Indra, the most powerful one, for our protection.

Advancing, come hither; trampling down the unpraised, come as a source of bliss to the host of Rudra. Traverse the wide mid-air, creating security and fearlessness, together with Pūṣan as your companion.

From the common dwelling-place of the earth, bring hither Agni of the soil in the manner of Aṅgiras. We approach Agni of the soil in the manner of Aṅgiras. We shall bear Agni of the soil in the manner of Aṅgiras.
Agni has looked along the forefront of the dawns; the first Jātavedas has looked along the days. You have extended yourself along the many rays of the sun, and along heaven and earth.
Having come along the path, the steed shakes off all enemies; he seeks to perceive Agni with his eye in the great assembly place.
O steed, having stepped upon the earth, seek Agni with your luster; having searched through the ground, tell us where we may dig him up.
Heaven is your back, the earth your seat, the atmosphere your soul, and the ocean your womb. Having looked abroad with your eye, do you trample upon those who attack us.
Step forth for great good fortune from this place, O bestower of wealth, O vigorous one! May we abide in the favor of the Earth while we dig for Agni in her lap.

The wealth-giver, the prize-winning steed, has stepped forth toward this world, toward the well-prepared, auspicious place upon the earth. From there, ascending to the highest heaven, let us dig up Agni of the beautiful countenance.
I sprinkle you with my mind and with ghee, you who dwell facing all beings—broad, vast with horizontal vigor, most expansive, impetuous, and visible through your foods.

I offer oblations from every side to him who faces us; may he accept it with a mind free from malice. Agni, possessing the beauty of a youth and a desirable form, flickers with his body so that one cannot touch him.
Agni, the sage and lord of booty, has stepped around the oblations, bestowing jewels upon the donor.
O Agni, O powerful one, we place you around us as a fortress—you, the inspired sage, of bold appearance, day by day the slayer of those who deal treacherously.

O Agni, you are born from the heavens; you, O seeker of flame, are born from the waters and from the stone; you are born from the forests and from the plants; you, O Lord of men, are born pure among men.

At the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins, with the hands of Pūṣan, from the seat of the earth, I dig for Agni Purīṣya in the manner of the Aṅgirases. You, O Agni, who are full of light, fair of aspect, shining with imperishable radiance—auspicious to creatures and non-injurious—we dig for you, Agni Purīṣya, from the seat of the earth in the manner of the Aṅgirases.
You are the back of the waters, the womb of Agni, swelling around the ocean. Growing great upon the lotus leaf, spread yourself out with the measure and the breadth of heaven.
You two are a refuge and you two are a shield; both of you are flawless and vast. Envelop yourselves in wide space, and preserve Agni Purīṣya.
Dwell together, you two who find the light of heaven, united in breast and in self, bearing within yourselves Agni, the luminous and imperishable.

You are the one who dwells in the soil, the sustainer of all; Atharvan was the first to churn you forth, O Agni. From the lotus, O Agni, Atharvan churned you forth from the head of the entire world, he the priest.
The seer Dadhyañc, the son of Atharvan, kindled you—that slayer of Vṛtra, the shatterer of forts.
The Pāthya, the bull, has kindled you, the greatest slayer of Dasyus, the winner of wealth in every battle.

Sit down, O Hotṛ, in your own place, being wise; establish the sacrifice in the womb of good action. As one who pleases the gods, worship the gods with the oblation; O Agni, bestow great vitality upon the sacrificer.

The Hotṛ, knowing his place, has sat down upon the seat of the Hotṛ—resplendent, shining, and most skillful. Agni, whose wisdom protects the inviolable vows, the most excellent, the bringer of thousands, with his pure tongue.
Sit down upon the great [altar]; shine forth, O best invoker of the gods! O Agni, worthy of sacrifice, praised one, emit your ruddy, beautiful smoke.
Release the divine waters, rich in sweetness, for the health of all creatures; from their place of origin, let the plants rise up, bearing goodly fruit.
May Vāyu Mātariśvan restore for you the heart that was torn asunder when you lay supine; O God, you who move among the gods with their vital breath—O God, may the *vaṣaṭ* call be unto you!
Well-born together with light, he has taken his seat in the heavenly realm as a shelter and a protection; O Agni, rich in radiance, clothe yourself in your garment of every form.
Arise, O you of fair sacrifice, and come to us with divine thought; shining brightly with great light so that we may behold you, O Agni, come hither with our excellent praises.
Stand up erect for our protection like the god Savitṛ; standing erect as the winner of booty when we, with ointments and with singers, call upon you from all sides.

Born as an embryo of the two worlds, O Agni, you are beautiful, distributed among the plants; a brilliant infant, you have gone forth from your mothers, crying aloud beyond the darkness and the nights.
Be firm, O strong-limbed one; be swift, O steed, O courser! Be broad and well-seated, you who carry the loose earth of Agni.
Be auspicious toward the human subjects, O Aṅgiras; do not scorch the heaven and earth, nor the intermediate space, nor the trees.

Let the vigorous steed go forth, neighing loudly, the braying donkey, the flyer; bearing Agni of the soil, may he not fall before his full span of life. Bearing the bull Agni, the potent one, the child of the waters, the oceanic.
O Agni, come hither for the feast.

The Law is truth, the Law is truth. We bring Agni Purīṣya, as did Aṅgiras. O plants, rejoice at this auspicious Agni as he approaches you here. Driving away all famines and diseases, may he sit down; strike away from us evil intent.
O plants, rich in flowers and bearing good fruit, receive him; this germ of yours, born in due season, has taken his seat in the ancient dwelling-place.

Flashing forth with your broad radiance, drive away our enemies, the Rākṣasas, and diseases. May I abide in the protection of the great Agni, who provides excellent refuge, under the guidance of him who is easily invoked.
O Waters, you are indeed sources of bliss; grant us strength for our great joy and for our vision.
Whatever most auspicious essence you possess, grant us a share of it here, like longing mothers.
Therefore, let us come quickly to you, for whose abode you quicken us; O Waters, give us life.
Mitra, having united the earth and the ground together with light, I unite you—the well-born Jātavedas—for the health of all creatures.
Having united with the earth, the Rudras kindled a great light; their unceasing, bright radiance shines among the gods.
May Sinīvālī, having mixed the clay with the Vasus and Rudras—the wise ones—and having made it soft with her two hands, fashion it into a workable form.
Sinīvālī, with beautiful braided hair, wearing a fine head-ornament and lovely earrings—may she, O Aditi, place the fire-pan into your hands for my sake.
May Aditi fashion the fire-pan with her power, her two arms, and her wisdom; may she bear Agni within her womb as a mother carries her son in her lap.
You are the head of Makha.

May the Vasus fashion you with the Gāyatrī metre, like Aṅgiras; you are firm. You are the earth. Bestow upon me offspring, abundance of wealth, mastery over cattle, heroic vigor, and kinsmen for the sacrificer.

May the Rudras fashion you with the Triṣṭubh metre, like Aṅgiras; you are firm, you are the intermediate space. Bestow upon me offspring, abundance of wealth, lordship over cattle, heroic vigor, and kinsmen for the sacrificer.

May the Ādityas fashion you with the Jāgata metre, like Aṅgiras; you are firm, you are the sky. Bestow upon me offspring, abundance of wealth, lordship over cattle, heroic vigor, and kinsmen for the sacrificer.

May all the gods, belonging to all men, fashion you with the Anuṣṭubh metre, like Aṅgiras. You are firm; you are the quarters. Bestow upon me offspring, abundance of wealth, lordship over cattle, heroic vigor, and kinsmen for the sacrificer.
"O Aditi, [this is] your resting place; may Aditi grasp your cavity. Having fashioned this great earthen pan as a womb for Agni, Aditi gave it to her sons, saying, 'Let him cook [the oblation]'."

May the Vasus fumigate you with the Gāyatrī metre, after the manner of Aṅgiras. May the Rudras fumigate you with the Triṣṭubh metre, after the manner of Aṅgiras. May the Ādityas fumigate you with the Jagatī metre, after the manner of Aṅgiras. May all the gods belonging to Vaiśvānara fumigate you with the Anuṣṭubh metre, after the manner of Aṅgiras. May Indra fumigate you; may Varuṇa fumigate you; may Viṣṇu fumigate you.

May Aditi, the goddess accompanied by all the gods, dig the pit for you in the lap of the earth, in the manner of Aṅgiras. May the wives of the gods, the goddesses accompanied by all the gods, place you, O pan, in the lap of the earth, in the manner of Aṅgiras. May the Dhiṣaṇās, the goddesses accompanied by all the gods, kindle you, O pan, in the lap of the earth, in the manner of Aṅgiras. May the Varūtrīs, the goddesses accompanied by all the gods, cook you, O pan, in the lap of the earth, in the manner of Aṅgiras. May the Gnas, the goddesses accompanied by all the gods, bake you, O pan, in the lap of the earth, in the manner of Aṅgiras. May the divine women with unbroken wings, accompanied by all the gods, bake you, O pan, in the lap of the earth, in the manner of Aṅgiras.
The aid of the divine Mitra, the sustainer of the people, is winning; his splendor possesses most wonderful renown.
May the god Savitṛ, with beautiful hands, beautiful fingers, and beautiful arms, dig thee up with his power; unshaking upon the earth, fill the regions and the quarters.
Having arisen, you shall become great; arise, standing firm! O Mitra, I entrust this fire-pan to you so that it may not be broken; may it not shatter.

May the Vasus fashion you with the Gāyatrī metre, in the manner of Aṅgiras. May the Rudras fashion you with the Triṣṭubh metre, in the manner of Aṅgiras. May the Ādityas fashion you with the Jagatī metre, in the manner of Aṅgiras. May all the gods belonging to Vaiśvānara fashion you with the Anuṣṭubh metre, in the manner of Aṅgiras.

To Ākūti, to Agni Prayuja, Svāhā! To Manas, to Medhā, to Agni Prayuja, Svāhā! To Citta, to Vijñāta, to Agni Prayuja, Svāhā! To Vācas, to Vidhṛti, to Agni Prayuja, Svāhā! To Prajāpati, to Manu, Svāhā! To Agni Vaiśvānara, Svāhā!
May every mortal choose the friendship of the divine leader; everyone strives for wealth, may he choose glory so that he may prosper—*svāhā*!
Do not fear, do not be harmed; O Mother, be courageous and act with valor! You and Agni shall accomplish this task together.

Be firm, O Goddess Earth; for our well-being, you have been made by the power of the Asuras through the self-sustaining law (svadhā). May this oblation be acceptable to the gods; rise up uninjured in this sacrifice.
He who has wood for food and butter for his libation, the ancient, desirable Hotṛ-priest, the wonderful son of strength.
From the higher distance, come down to the lower ones; protect those where I am.
From that furthest distance, O you whose horses are ruddy, come here! O Agni, friend of many, dwelling in the soil, do you overcome our adversaries.
O Agni, whatever logs of wood we place before you, may all that be ghee for you; accept it, O youngest one.
Whatever the upajihvikā eats, whatever the ant crawls over—let all that be ghee for you; enjoy it, O youngest one!
Bringing fuel day after day without fail, like fodder for a horse that stands ready, may we rejoice with the increase of wealth and nourishment; O Agni, may we, your neighbors, not come to harm.

At the navel of the earth, while the fire is kindled, we invoke for the sake of great increase of wealth Agni—the one who gladdens with food, the one worthy of great hymns, the worshipful, the victor, and the conqueror in battles.
Those armies that are rushing forward, those that pierce and those that are fierce in their hosts, as well as those who are thieves and those who are robbers—these I place within your mouth, O Agni.
With your two fangs, O Blessed One, [devour] the night-pirates; with your teeth, the thieves; with your jaws, the robbers—chew them up well-chewed!
Those among men who are defilers, thieves, and robbers in the forest, those who are malevolent in the thickets—these I place within your two jaws to crush.
Whoever acts with hostility toward us, and whoever is a person who hates us, whoever reviles us and seeks to harm us—reduce all of them to ashes!
Sharpened is my sacred word, sharpened is my vigor and strength; sharpened is the victorious ruling power of him for whom I am the domestic priest.
I have extended their arms upward, and their luster, and also their strength; with my sacred word (*brahman*), I destroy the enemies and I raise up my own people.
O Lord of food, grant us food that is free from disease and full of vigor; further prolong the life of the giver, and bestow strength upon our bipeds and quadrupeds.

Visible like a golden ornament, he has shone forth widely; radiant for the sake of glory, he has attained an invincible lifespan. Agni became immortal through his vital powers when the prolific Heaven brought him forth.
Night and Dawn, of one mind yet different forms, moving together, suckle the single infant. Between heaven and earth the golden disk shines; the gods, bestowers of wealth, have sustained Agni.

The Seer puts on all forms; he has brought forth what is auspicious for bipeds and quadrupeds. Savitar, the one to be chosen, has looked out upon the firmament; he shines along the departure of the Dawn.

You are Suparṇa, the Garuḍa; the Trivṛt-stoma is your head, the Gāyatra your eye, the Bṛhat and Rathantara your wings, the Stoma your body, the meters your limbs, and the Yajus your name. The Sāman Vāmadevya is your torso, the Yajñāyajñīya your tail, and the Dhiṣṇya hearths your hooves. You are Suparṇa, the Garuḍa; go to the sky, fly to the light!

Thou art the stride of Viṣṇu, the slayer of rivals; ascend the Gāyatrī metre; stride along the earth! Thou art the stride of Viṣṇu, the slayer of the arrogant; ascend the Triṣṭubh metre; stride along the intermediate space! Thou art the stride of Viṣṇu, the slayer of the hostile; ascend the Jagatī metre; stride along the sky! Thou art the stride of Viṣṇu, the slayer of those who act as enemies; ascend the Anuṣṭubh metre; stride along the quarters!

Agni has cried out like the thundering sky, licking the earth and anointing the plants. As soon as he was born, once kindled, he looked abroad; he shines with his splendor between the two worlds, heaven and earth.
O Agni, you who turn back toward us, turn back toward me with life-span, with luster, with progeny, with wealth, with gain, with wisdom, with riches, and with nourishment.
O Agni Aṅgiras, may there be a hundred turnings for you, and a thousand approaches for you. Then, by the nourishment of nourishment, bring back to us what we have lost; bring back to us our wealth.
Return again with vigor, O Agni, return with food and long life; protect us again from distress.
Return with wealth, O Agni; swell with a stream that provides all-nourishing food from every side.
I have brought you hither; you have come within. Stand firm, unshakable. Let all the people desire you; let not the kingdom fall away from you.
O Varuṇa, loosen the uppermost bond from us, untie the lowest, and release the middle one. Then, O Āditya, under your law, may we be sinless before Aditi.

In the forefront of the dawns, the great one has stood upright; emerging from the darkness, he has come with light. Agni, with his radiant luster and beautiful limbs, having been born, has filled all dwellings.

The Haṃsa dwelling in the pure realm, the Vasu dwelling in the mid-air, the Hotṛ dwelling on the sacrificial altar, the guest dwelling in the remote home; dwelling among men, dwelling in the best of places, dwelling in Truth, dwelling in the firmament; born of the waters, born of the kine, born of Truth, born of the mountains—He is the Eternal Order.
Vast.
Sit down upon the lap of this mother, O Agni, you who know all ways; do not scorch her with heat or with flame, but shine forth within her with pure light.
O Agni, with your luster, be within the fire-pan in its own place; heating it with your flame, O Jātavedas, be auspicious.
Having become auspicious for me, O Agni, sit down as one who is auspicious; having made all the quarters auspicious, sit here in your own womb.

Agni was first born from the sky; from this [earth] was Jātavedas born a second time; a third time he was born in the waters, he whose mind is manly. The pious man, kindling him, praises him as the eternal one.
We know your three forms, O Agni, in three ways; we know your stations distributed in many places. We know your supreme name which is hidden in secret; we know that fountain from which you have come.

In the ocean, within the waters, the manly-minded one kindled thee; O Agni, the beholder of men kindled thee in the udder of heaven. Standing in the third realm, in the lap of the waters, the mighty ones increased thee.
Agni has cried out like the thundering sky, licking the earth, anointing the plants; as soon as he was born, being kindled, he looked abroad, and with his radiance he shines between the two worlds.

Magnificent bestower of glories, supporter of riches, inspirer of prayers, and guardian of Soma; the Vasu, the Son of Strength, the King in the waters, shines forth, kindled at the forefront of the dawns.
The banner of the universe, the germ of the world, at his birth filled the two worlds; even the firm rock he split asunder when departing, when the five peoples sacrificed to Agni.
The loving, purifying, wise, and active Agni, the immortal, has been established among mortals. Bearing his ruddy smoke, he rises up, striving to reach the sky with his bright radiance.

Visible like a golden ornament, he has shone far and wide; shining for the sake of glory with a life-span difficult to surpass, Agni became immortal through his vital powers when the prolific Heaven brought him forth.
O Agni of auspicious luster, whoever today prepares for you a cake rich in ghee, O God—lead him further toward greater wealth, toward the favor bestowed by the gods, O youngest one.

O Agni, grant him a share in glorious deeds; at every hymn being recited, grant him a share. May he be dear to Sūrya, may he be dear to Agni; may he excel through what has been born and through what is yet to be born.
O Agni, day after day, the sacrificers have placed all desirable treasures within you. Seeking wealth through you, the yearning ones have opened the cow-filled stall.

Agni, the benevolent friend of men, Vaiśvānara, the guardian of Soma, has been praised by the seers. We invoke the two gods, Heaven and Earth, who are free from hatred; O gods, bestow upon us wealth accompanied by heroic sons.
Honor Agni with fuel; awaken the guest with clarified butter; offer the oblations into him.
May all the gods, O Agni, bear you upward with their thoughts; be thou gracious to us, thou who art fair of aspect and rich in light.
O Agni, come forward as one possessed of light with your auspicious flames; shining with great beams of radiance, do not harm the offspring with your body.

Agni has cried out like the thundering sky, licking the earth and anointing the plants. As soon as he was born, being kindled, he looked abroad; he shines with his splendor between the two worlds, heaven and earth.
Far-famed is this Agni of Bharata, who shines forth with great luster like the sun; he who has stood firm against the Pūru in battles, our auspicious divine guest, has shone brightly.
O divine Waters, receive this ash; place it in a pleasant and fragrant world. Let wives with noble husbands bow down before it; bear it within the waters like a mother her son.
O Agni, your seat is in the waters; you penetrate the plants; being in the womb, you are born again.
You are the embryo of the plants, the embryo of the trees; O Agni, you are the embryo of every living being, the embryo of the waters.
Having propitiated the womb with ashes, O Agni, and having united yourself with the waters and the earth, you, together with your mothers, have returned as one possessed of light.
Having returned again to your seat, O Agni, you lie upon the waters and the earth within this [world], most auspicious in her lap, as if in the womb of a mother.
Return again with vigor, O Agni, return with food and long life; protect us again from distress.
Return with wealth, O Agni; swell with a stream that provides for all from every side.

O youngest one, O self-ruling lord, grant me understanding of this word of mine, which is most bountiful and offered to you. One person reviles, while another praises; I, your worshipper, praise your body, O Agni.
O wise sage, Maghavan, Lord of wealth, giver of riches, drive away from us those who hate us.
Svāhā to Viśvakarman!

May the Ādityas, Rudras, and Vasus kindle you again; may the Brahmins, O leader of wealth, [kindle you] again with sacrifices. May you cause your body to grow with clarified butter; may the desires of the sacrificer come true.
Depart, go away, and creep far from here—those who are here, both the ancient ones and the recent! Yama has granted this dwelling on earth; the ancestors have prepared this world for him.

You are consciousness; you are the upholder of desire. May your upholding of desire be in me. You are the ashes of Agni; you are the soil of Agni. You are piled up, you are piled around, you are piled upward; stand firm!
This is that Agni in whom Indra, longing for him, placed the pressed Soma within his belly; having won thousandfold booty like a swift steed, you are praised, O Jātavedas.

O Agni, that splendor of yours which is in heaven, on earth, in the plants, and in the waters, O worshipful one—by which you have spread across the wide mid-air—that light of yours is brilliant, surging, and beholds men.

O Agni, you go toward the flood of heaven; you have spoken to the gods who are worthy of worship. To those waters which are in the luminous realm beyond the sun, and those which stand below it, [you go].
May the fires that dwell in the soil, being of one accord with those on the slopes, accept the sacrifice—being free from malice, they shall grant great, disease-free refreshments.

O Agni, bestow upon the one who invokes you the *iḍā*—the gift of many cattle, most enduring. May there be to us a son, a progeny that continues the lineage; O Agni, may that benevolence of yours be with us.
This is your seasonal womb, from which once born you shone forth; knowing it, O Agni, ascend it, and then increase our wealth.
You are consciousness; by that deity, sit firm like Aṅgiras. You are the surrounding consciousness; by that deity, sit firm like Aṅgiras.
Fill the world, fill the gap; then sit down firm. Indra, Agni, and Bṛhaspati have established you in this womb.
These dappled cows, yielding milk for the preparation, mix the Soma; they are the subjects at the birth of the gods, in the three luminous realms of heaven.
All songs have magnified Indra, who is as vast as the ocean—the best of charioteers among charioteers, the true lord and master of spoils.
May you two always agree together, being well-disposed toward one another, radiant, and of good mind, dwelling together for the sake of food and strength.
I have brought together your minds, your vows, and your thoughts. O Agni Purīṣya, be our protector; bestow food and vigor upon the sacrificer.
O Agni, you are the one dwelling in the soil, possessed of wealth and abundance; having made all directions auspicious, sit here upon your place of birth.
Be of one mind with us, of one intent, and stainless; do not harm the sacrifice nor the lord of the sacrifice, O Jātavedas; be auspicious to us today.
As a mother carries her son, the Earth has borne Agni Purīṣya in her own womb, the fire-pan; may Prajāpati Viśvakarman, in harmony with all the gods and the seasons, release him from it.

Seek him who does not breathe [the sacrifice], who does not offer sacrifice; follow the track of the thief, of the robber! Seek someone other than us—that shall be your path. O Goddess Nirṛti, let there be homage to you!
Homage be to you, O Nirṛti of piercing splendor! Untie this iron bond. In agreement with Yama and Yamī, cause him to ascend to the highest firmament.
I offer this oblation to your terrible aspect for the release from these bonds—O you whom people joyfully call "the Earth," yet I recognize you everywhere as Nirṛti.
The noose which the goddess Nirṛti bound upon your necks so that it could not be untied—that I loosen for you from the midst of your life; then, being released, eat this food.
Homage to Bhūti, by whom this was made.
The abode and gatherer of riches, he beholds all forms with his powers; like the god Savitṛ whose laws are true, he stands like Indra at the meeting-place of the paths.
The seers yoke the ploughs; the wise ones stretch out the yokes separately, seeking favor among the gods.
Harness the ploughs, stretch out the yokes; sow the seed here in the prepared womb. May our song and our prompt obedience be fruitful together; may the sickle come closer to the ripened grain.
May the ploughs furrow the earth auspiciously; may the plowmen proceed auspiciously with their draft-animals. O Śuna and Sīra, being gratified by our oblation, make the plants bear fine fruit for us.
Let Sītā be anointed with ghee and honey, approved by all the gods and the Maruts; full of vigor, swelling with milk—O Sītā, turn toward us with your milk!
The plough, sharp-edged, very kind, with a handle for holding the Soma-stalks—this he sows: cattle and sheep, and a fat, swelling cow; and a wagon for carrying a chariot, complete with its seat.
O yielder of desires, milk forth desire for Mitra and Varuṇa, for Indra, for the two Aśvins, for Pūṣan, for all creatures, and for the plants.
Be released, O inviolable ones; we have gone to the further shore of this darkness, we have attained the light.

In harmony with the waters and the living beings; in harmony with the dawn and the ruddy cows; in agreement with the Aśvins through their wondrous deeds; in harmony with Sūrya and his steed Etaśa; in harmony with Vaiśvānara, with the sacrificial food and clarified butter—Svāhā!
Those herbs which were born first, three ages before the gods—I now take heed of them: the hundred and seven abodes of the brown ones.
A hundred, O Mother, are your abodes, and a thousand are your growths; therefore, you who possess a hundred powers, make this [child] of mine free from disease.
Rejoice in the plants—those that bear flowers and those that bring forth fruit; like victorious mares, may these healing herbs carry us across to safety.
"O Plants, you mothers; as such, O goddesses, I address you: may I win back the horse, the cow, the garment, and your very self, O man."
The holy fig tree is your place of rest; the leaf has been made your dwelling. You shall indeed be sharers in cattle, if you win back the man.
Where the plants have gathered together like kings in an assembly, he is called the wise physician, the slayer of demons and the dispeller of disease.
I have gathered all the plants—those rich in horses, rich in Soma, full of vigor, and full of strength—for his well-being and freedom from harm.
The swelling powers of the plants rush forth like cows from the stall, seeking to win wealth for you, O man, and their very self.
Healing is your mother by name, and you yourselves are healers; you are winged furrows, for you heal whatever is diseased.
They have passed beyond all obstacles; like a thief entering a pen, they have driven out the plants and whatever bodily defect there was.
When I, seeking strength, take these plants in my hand, the self of the wasting disease perishes, as if before the seizer of life.
O plants, as you creep from limb to limb and joint to joint, drive away the consumption from there, like a fierce man who sits in the midst [of his army].
Fly away, O consumption, together with the blue jay, the woodpecker; vanish together with the rush of the wind, together with the whirlwind.
Let one among you protect another; let each assist the other. All of you, being in full accord, further this speech of mine.
Those plants that bear fruit and those that are fruitless, those that bloom and those that do not—impelled by Bṛhaspati, may they release us from distress.
May they release me from the curse of the oath, and also from that of Varuṇa, and also from Yama’s fetter, and from every offense against the gods.
Descending from the sky, the plants spoke: "The living man whom we shall reach, that person shall not come to harm."
Of those many plants whose king is Soma, which possess a hundredfold vision—you are the most excellent among them; [I take you] for the fulfillment of desire, for peace of heart.
O plants whose king is Soma, which are spread across the earth, impelled by Bṛhaspati, bestow your power upon this woman.
Those creepers which hear this and those which have gone far away—let all of them, having come together, bestow their power upon her.
May the one who digs you not be harmed, nor he for whom I dig you; may all our bipeds and quadrupeds be free from disease.
The plants conversed together with Soma the king: "O King, we shall bring across that man for whom a Brahmin performs [this rite]."
You are the destroyer of phlegm and of hemorrhoids that have grown thick; furthermore, you are the eradicator of a hundred consumptive diseases.
The Gandharvas dug you up; Indra dug you up; Bṛhaspati dug you up. O herb, King Soma, the wise one, was released from consumption by means of you.
Overcome my enemies; overcome those who attack us; overcome every evil, O victorious herb!
Long-lived be the one who digs you up, O herb, and he for whom I dig you; and so may you, having become long-lived yourself, grow forth with a hundred shoots.
O herb, you are the highest; trees are your attendants. May he who assails us be our attendant.

May he not harm us—he who is the progenitor of the earth, or he who, possessing true dharma, pervaded the sky, and who first brought forth the moon-like waters. To which god shall we offer worship with our oblation?
Turn toward us, O Earth, with the sacrifice and with milk; Agni, impelled, has ascended your omentum.
O Agni, that which is yours, the bright, that which is radiant, that which is purified, and that which is worthy of sacrifice—that we bring to the gods.
I have taken from here nourishment and vigor, the womb of Cosmic Order, the stream of the Great One. May it enter into my cattle and my limbs; I cast away exhaustion, lack of food, and disease.
O Agni, yours is renown and vital strength; your flames shine brightly, O Lord of Radiance. With your great light and power, O Sage, you bestow praiseworthy booty upon the donor.
With purifying luster, with bright luster, with undiminished luster, you rise up with your radiance. Moving between your two mothers as their son, you protect them; you fill both heaven and earth.

O Son of Strength, Jātavedas, rejoice with our excellent praises and our prayers, for you have been established as our benefactor. In you they have gathered manifold foods—those of many forms, with wondrous aids, born of noble lineage.
O Agni, ruling over all, spread yourself out with living beings; bestow wealth upon us, O Immortal One! You shine forth with a form worthy to be beheld; you fulfill our winning wisdom.
The wise ordainer of the sacrifice, who rules over great wealth—you bestow upon him a fortunate gift of beauty, great nourishment, and winning riches.

The people have placed before them for their welfare Agni, the observer of cosmic order, the mighty one visible to all; you, the divine one with ears that hear, most far-reaching, through song do human generations invoke.
Swell up; let virile strength come to you from every side, O Soma; be present at the gathering of booty.
May your milks come together, and let your strengths and manly powers that overcome the adversary unite. Swelling for the sake of immortality, O Soma, bestow upon us the highest glories in heaven.
Swell up, O most exhilarating Soma, with all your stalks; be our most glorious friend for our prosperity.
May Vatsa draw your mind hither, O Agni, even from the most distant dwelling, with a song that yearns for you.
To you, O best of the Angirases, all those people, each with their own good dwellings, have turned for the sake of their desire, O Agni.
Agni, as desire for all that has been and is to be, shines forth as the sole sovereign in his beloved abodes.
I take Agni first in me for the increase of wealth, for good progeny, and for heroic vigor; may the deities attend upon me.
You are the back of the waters, the womb of Agni, swelling around the ocean; growing great upon the lotus-leaf, spread yourself out with the measure and the breadth of heaven.
Brahman, first born in the east, Vena has revealed from the radiant horizon; he has disclosed its highest stations in the depths, and the womb of both the existent and the non-existent.
In the beginning, Hiraṇyagarbha arose; once born, he was the sole lord of all that exists. He supported this earth and yonder sky. To what god shall we offer worship with our oblation?
The drop has fallen upon the earth and upon heaven, upon this womb and that which was before; I offer the drop as it moves along toward the common womb, following the seven officiating priests.
Homage be to the serpents, whichever ones are upon the earth; to those in the intermediate space and those in heaven—to those serpents, homage!
Homage to those serpents who are the arrows of the sorcerers, or those who dwell in the trees, or those who lie in holes.
Homage to those serpents who are in the bright realm of heaven, or who are in the rays of the sun, or whose dwelling has been established in the waters.
Assume your power like a wide-spreading net; go forth like a king with his powerful elephant. Rushing along your swift net, you are an archer; pierce the demons with your most scorching shafts.

Your swift-moving flames fall; touch them with boldness as you blaze forth. O Agni, with your sacrificial ladle, cast out your heats like winged birds; unbound, scatter your firebrands in every direction.
Send forth your spies; be the swiftest one, an undeceivable guardian for this people. Whether he who plots evil against us be far away or near, O Agni, let no affliction from you prevail over us.
Arise, O Agni! Spread yourself out against them; burn down our enemies, O you of the sharp weapon! Whosoever has directed hostility toward us, O kindled one, burn him down like dry brushwood.
Stand upright; pierce them from above us; O Agni, make manifest thy divine powers. Slacken the firm [bonds] of those impelled by demons; crush the enemies, whether kin or stranger.
I settle you with the splendor of Agni.
Agni is the head of heaven, the summit, the lord of this earth; he quickens the seeds of the waters.
I set you down with the vital power of Indra.

Leader of the sacrifice and of the mid-world, where you accompany [us] with your auspicious teams of horses; you have established your head in heaven, winning the light, and you have made your tongue, O Agni, the bearer of the oblation.
Firm art thou, a supporting foundation, spread out by Viśvakarman; let not the ocean overwhelm thee, nor the Suparṇa; being unshakable, make firm the earth.
May Prajāpati seat you upon the back of the waters, on the breast of the ocean; you who are spacious and wide-extending, spread yourself out—you are the Earth.
You are Bhūḥ, you are the Earth, you are Aditi, the all-sustaining, the upholder of the entire world. Support the earth, make the earth firm; do not harm the earth.

For all out-breathing, in-breathing, diffused breathing, and upward breathing; for stability and for movement—may Agni protect you with great well-being and most peaceful shelter. By that deity, sit firm like Aṅgiras.
Growing from joint to joint, from every single node, even so, O *dūrvā* grass, extend yourself for us by a hundred and a thousandfold.
O divine brick, you who spread yourself with a hundred and grow forth with a thousand—unto you we shall offer worship with an oblation.
O Agni, those splendors of yours which extend across the sky with rays into the sun—with all of them, grant us radiance today for the sake of our people.
O gods, whatever splendors you possess in the sun, and whatever splendors are in the cows and in the horses—with all those splendors, O Indra and Agni, and O Bṛhaspati, bestow splendor upon us.

Virāj has sustained the light; Svarāj has sustained the light. May Prajāpati settle thee, the luminous one, upon the back of the earth. Bestow universal light for the sake of universal out-breathing, in-breathing, and diffused breathing. Agni is thy overlord; by that deity, sit firm like Aṅgiras.

Madhu and Mādhava are the two spring seasons. You are the internal bond of Agni. May Heaven and Earth be in harmony; may the waters and plants be in harmony; may the fires be in harmony. With one mind and a common vow, let those fires that dwell between these two, Heaven and Earth, during the two spring seasons, enter into you as the gods entered Indra, being well-disposed toward you. By that deity, in the manner of Aṅgiras, sit firm in your places.
You are Aṣāḍhā, the overcoming one; overcome the enemies, overcome those who attack us. You possess a thousandfold power; as such, quicken me.
The winds blow honey for the one who follows the cosmic order; the rivers flow with honey; may the plants be sweet for us.
May the night be honey-sweet, and may the dawn be honey-sweet; may the earthly realm be honey-sweet, and may our father, heaven, be honey-sweet for us.
May the Lord of the Forest be full of sweetness for us; may Sūrya be full of sweetness; may the cows be sweet for us.
Sit in the depth of the waters; let not the sun scorch you, nor Agni Vaiśvānara. Behold the offspring with unsevered wings; may the divine rain attend you.

The bull, lord of the waters, has flowed through the three oceans and the heavenly realms, clothing himself in the soil-bricks of the well-made world; go there, where those who went before have departed.
May Heaven and Earth, the broad ground, mix this sacrifice for us; may they fill us with nourishments.
Behold the deeds of Viṣṇu, through which he has made his vows manifest; he is the close companion and friend of Indra.
You are firm, O Jātavedas; from these wombs you were first born as a supporter. Knowing the way, may you carry the oblation to the gods by means of the Gāyatrī, the Triṣṭubh, and the Anuṣṭubh meters.
Rejoice for the sake of nourishment, wealth, power, splendor, vigor, and progeny! You are the sovereign ruler; you are the self-ruling lord. May the two springs of Sarasvatī protect you.
O Agni, yoke those horses of yours, O God, which are well-trained and carry you readily according to your will.
Yoke, O Agni, like a charioteer, your horses that best summon the gods; sit down as the ancient Hotṛ-priest.
The streams flow rightly, like milch-cows, purified within by the heart and the mind; I behold the streams of clarified butter, and in the midst of the fire stands the golden reed.
For the Ṛc you, for radiance you, for luster you, for light you! This has become the strength of the entire world and of Agni Vaiśvānara.
Agni is radiant with light; the golden disk is brilliant with splendor. You are the giver of thousands; for the sake of a thousand, I take you.
Anoint the solar embryo with milk, the image of a thousand, possessing all forms. Avoid it with your heat; do not harm it. Granting it a hundred-year lifespan, may you be built up.

The impulse of the wind, the navel of Varuṇa, the horse born in the midst of the flood—do not harm that infant of the rivers, the tawny one whose foundation is the mountain, O Agni, in the highest heaven.
I praise with salutations Agni—the unceasing, ruddy, and restless drop—known from of old; may he, fashioning himself according to his joints and the seasons, not harm the cow, Aditi, the radiant one.
The guardian of Tvaṣṭṛ, the navel of Varuṇa, the ewe born from beyond the realm of space—the great, thousandfold creative power of the Asura—O Agni, do not harm her in the highest heaven.
That fire which was born from the heat of Agni, from the earth, or from the sky—that by which Viśvakarman generated all creatures—may Agni’s wrath spare you from that.
The brilliant face of the gods has risen, the eye of Mitra, Varuṇa, and Agni. Sūrya has filled heaven, earth, and the mid-space; he is the soul of all that moves and stands still.
Do not harm this two-footed animal, O thousand-eyed one, as you are being built for the sacrifice. Accept the Mayu as the sacrificial victim, O Agni; building up your bodies with it, take your seat.
May the heat of passion reach the demon; may the heat of passion reach him whom we hate.
Do not harm this one-hoofed animal, the neighing steed among the prize-winning steeds. I assign to you the wild ox; building up your bodies with that, settle down.
Let your heat reach the fair-complexioned one; let your heat reach him whom we hate.

O Agni, do not harm this Aditi, who yields clarified butter for the sake of humanity, who flows in a thousand streams and a hundred channels, spreading forth in the midst of the ocean, in the highest heaven.
I assign to you the wild gavaya; fashioning your bodies with it, sit down. Let your heat reach the gavaya; let your heat reach him whom we hate.
This woolly one, the navel of Varuṇa, the skin of animals, biped and quadruped—the first birthplace of Tvaṣṭṛ’s progeny—O Agni, do not harm it in the highest heaven.
I assign to you the wild camel; piling yourself with it, settle down in your bodies. Let your heat reach the camel; let your heat reach him whom we hate.

For the unborn was born from the heat of Agni; he beheld his progenitor in the beginning. By him the gods attained divinity in the beginning; by him the worthy ones ascended to the height. I assign the wild *śarabha* to you; building up your bodies with it, sit down. Let your heat reach the *śarabha*; let your heat reach him whom we hate.
O youngest one, protect the men who offer oblations; hear our songs, and guard our offspring as well as yourself.

I settle you in the surge of the waters; I settle you in the heaving of the waters; I settle you in the froth of the waters; I settle you in the light of the waters; I settle you in the course of the waters. I settle you in the wave as your seat; I settle you in the ocean as your seat; I settle you in the flood as your seat; I settle you in the dwelling of the waters; I settle you in the abode of the waters; I settle you in the resting place of the waters; I settle you in the station of the waters; I settle you in the womb of the waters; I settle you in the soil of the waters; I settle you in the domain of the waters. I settle you with the Gāyatrī metre; I settle you with the Triṣṭubh metre; I settle you with the Jagatī metre; I settle you with the Anuṣṭubh metre; I settle you with the Paṅkti metre.

This is the eastern region of the world. Its breath is Bhauvanāya. Spring is its breath. The Gāyatrī is of spring. From the Gāyatrī comes the Gāyatra [chant]. From the Gāyatra comes the Upāṃśu [cup]. From the Upāṃśu comes the Trivṛt [stoma]. From the Trivṛt comes the Rathantara [sāman]. Vasiṣṭha is the seer. With thee, taken by Prajāpati, I take hold of the breath for the sake of all creatures.

This southern direction is Viśvakarman; his mind is Vaiśvakarmaṇa; summer is mental; the Triṣṭubh meter belongs to summer; from the Triṣṭubh comes the Svara-sāman; from the Svara comes the Antaryāma cup; from the Antaryāma comes the Pañcadaśa stoma; from the Pañcadaśa comes the Bṛhat sāman; Bharadvāja is the seer. With thee, taken by Prajāpati, I take hold of the mind for the sake of offspring.

This one behind is Viśvavyacās; his eye is Vaiśvavyacasian. The rains have the eye as their deity; the Jagatī meter belongs to the rains; from the Jagatī comes the Ṛksamā; from the Ṛksamā comes the Śukra cup; from the Śukra comes the Saptadaśa stoma; from the Saptadaśa comes the Vairūpa sāman. Jamadagni is the seer. With thee, taken by Prajāpati, I take the eye for all creatures.

This [season] is the northern quarter; its season is the winter solstice (*saumya*); the autumn is the domain of the ear (*śrautrī*); the *anuṣṭubh* meter belongs to the autumn; from the *anuṣṭubh* comes the *aiḍa* chant; from the *aiḍa* comes the *manthin* cup; from the *manthin* comes the twenty-one-fold stoma; from the twenty-one-fold comes the *vairāja* chant; Viśvāmitra is the seer. With thee, taken by Prajāpati, I take up the sense of hearing for the sake of offspring.

This [season] above is the mind (*mati*). Speech (*vāc*) is measured by it; winter (*hemanta*) is to be expressed by speech. The *paṅkti* [meter] belongs to winter; from the *paṅkti* comes that which has a *nidhana*; from that which has a *nidhana* comes the *āgrayaṇa* [graha]; from the *āgrayaṇa* come the *triṇava* and *trayastrim̐śa* [stomas]; from the *triṇava* and *trayastrim̐śa* come the *śākvara* and *raivata* [sāmans]. Viśvakarman is the seer (*ṛṣi*). With thee, taken by Prajāpati, I take speech for my offspring. Fill the world, fill the gap, and sit thou firm. Indra, Agni, and Bṛhaspati have seated thee in this womb.
These dappled cows, yielding milk for the libation, mix the Soma; they are the clans at the birth of the gods, in the three luminous realms of heaven.
All songs have magnified Indra, who is as expansive as the ocean—the best of charioteers among charioteers, the true lord and master of spoils.

Firmly established, with a firm source, you are firm; sit firmly upon your firm womb in the proper manner, delighting in the first signal of the fire-pan. May the Aśvins, the two Adhvaryus, settle you here.
Nest-like, rich in clarity, and all-encompassing, sit upon the pleasant seat of the earth. May the Rudras and Vasus sing praises to you; cause these prayers to swell for our good fortune.
May the two Aśvins, the Adhvaryu priests, settle you here.

Sit here, O Son of Dakṣa, with your own skillful powers, for the great joy and favor of the gods. Be as kind as a father to his son; enter into us with a body that is easy of access and most gracious.
May the Aśvins, the two Adhvaryu priests, settle you here.
You are the soil of the earth, whose name is Apas; may all the gods acclaim you. Seated here upon the back of the hymn, rich in clarified butter, grant us offspring through the sacrificial ladle.
May the Aśvins, the two Adhvaryu priests, settle you here.

I set thee on the back of Aditi, the supporter of the intermediate space, the prop of the quarters, the sovereign lady of the worlds; thou art the wave, the drop of the waters; Viśvakarman is thy seer.
May the two Aśvins, the Adhvaryu priests, settle you here.

Śukra and Śuci are the two summer seasons of Agni; you are their internal bond. May Heaven and Earth be prepared; may the waters and plants be prepared; may the fires, being of one mind, be prepared separately for the sake of preeminence, sharing a common vow. Those fires which are of one mind between these two, Heaven and Earth, preparing themselves for the two summer seasons—may they enter [you] together as the gods entered Indra. With that deity, sit firm like Aṅgiras! May you two sit firm!

In harmony with the seasons, in harmony with the ritual distributions, in harmony with the gods, in harmony with the gods who provide the dwelling—may the two Aśvins, the Adhvaryu priests, settle you here for Agni Vaiśvānara.

In harmony with the seasons, in harmony with the ritual distributions, in harmony with the Vasus, in harmony with the gods who provide a dwelling—may the two Aśvins, the Adhvaryu priests, settle you here for Agni Vaiśvānara.

In harmony with the seasons, in harmony with the ritual distributions, in harmony with the Rudras, in harmony with the gods who provide vital strength—may the two Aśvins, the Adhvaryu priests, settle you here for Agni Vaiśvānara.

In harmony with the seasons, in harmony with the ordinances, in harmony with the Ādityas, in harmony with the gods who protect our vital breaths—may the two Aśvins, the Adhvaryu priests, settle you here for Agni Vaiśvānara.

In harmony with the seasons, in harmony with the ordinances, in harmony with all the gods, in harmony with the gods who provide vital strength—may the two Aśvins, the Adhvaryu priests, settle you here for Agni Vaiśvānara.

Protect my out-breath; protect my in-breath; protect my diffused breath. Shine forth widely for my sight; make my hearing resonant with praise. Swell the waters; quicken the plants. Protect the bipeds; guard the quadrupeds. Send down rain from heaven.

The head is vigor; Prajāpati is the metre. Dominion is vigor; the joy-giving is the metre. The support is vigor; the overlord is the metre. Viśvakarman is vigor; the highest lord is the metre. The ram is vigor; the wide-striding is the metre. The bull is vigor; the broad is the metre. Man is vigor; the wearying is the metre. The tiger is vigor; the unassailable is the metre. The lion is vigor; the covering is the metre. The four-year-old ox is vigor; the *bṛhatī* is the metre. The steer is vigor; the *kakubh* is the metre. The bull is vigor; the *sato-bṛhatī* is the metre.

The ox is the age; *paṅkti* is the metre. The milch-cow is the age; *jagatī* is the metre. The two-year-old steer is the age; *triṣṭubh* is the metre. The three-year-old steer is the age; *virāj* is the metre. The four-year-old steer is the age; *gāyatrī* is the metre. The five-year-old steer is the age; *uṣṇih* is the metre. The six-year-old steer is the age; *anuṣṭubh* is the metre. Fill the space, fill the gap; then sit down, you who are firm. Indra, Agni, and Bṛhaspati have seated you in this womb.
These dappled cows, yielding milk for the preparation, mix the Soma; they are the clans at the birth of the gods, in the three luminous realms of heaven.
All songs have magnified Indra, who is as expansive as the ocean—the best of charioteers among charioteers, the true lord and master of spoils.
O Indra and Agni, do you two make firm this unshaking brick; with its back, it presses against heaven and earth and the intermediate space.
May Viśvakarman settle you upon the back of the atmosphere—broad and expansive; uphold the atmosphere, make the atmosphere firm; do not injure the atmosphere.
For all out-breathing, in-breathing, diffused breathing, and up-breathing; for stability and for movement.
May Vāyu protect you with great well-being and most peaceful shelter; through that deity, sit firm like Aṅgiras.

You are the Queen, the eastern direction; you are the Virāj, the southern direction; you are the Samrāj, the western direction; you are the Svarāj, the northern direction; you are the Sovereign Lady, the great (bṛhatī) direction.
May Viśvakarman settle you, the luminous one, upon the back of the intermediate space.
Bestow universal light for all out-breath, in-breath, and diffused breath.
Vāyu is your overlord; by that deity, sit firm like Aṅgiras.

Nabhas and Nabhasya are the two rainy seasons. You are the internal cohesion of Agni. May Heaven and Earth be in harmony; may the waters and plants be in harmony; may the fires be in harmony. With one mind and common vows, let those fires which dwell between these two, Heaven and Earth, during the two rainy seasons, enter into you all together, just as the gods entered Indra. By that deity, in the manner of Aṅgiras, sit firm in your places.

Iṣa and Ūrja, the two autumnal seasons—you are the internal bond of Agni. May Heaven and Earth be in harmony; may the waters and plants be in harmony; may the fires, being of one mind, be in harmony for the sake of preeminence, each according to its vow. Those fires which are of one mind between these two, Heaven and Earth, during the two autumnal seasons—may they enter into you, as the gods entered Indra, harmonizing themselves. With that deity, sit firm like Aṅgiras! May you two sit firm!

Protect my life-span; protect my out-breath; protect my in-breath; protect my diffused breath; protect my sight; protect my hearing; nourish my speech; invigorate my mind; protect my self; bestow light upon me.
