The Mā-chandas metre; the Pramā-chandas metre; the Pratimā-chandas metre; the Amṛtivayasa-chandas metre; the Paṅkti-chandas metre; the Uṣṇih-chandas metre; the Bṛhatī-chandas metre; the Anuṣṭubh-chandas metre; the Virāj-chandas metre; the Gāyatrī-chandas metre; the Triṣṭubh-chandas metre; the Jagatī-chandas metre.

The earth is meter; the intermediate space is meter; the sky is meter; the years are meter; the stars are meter; speech is meter; the mind is meter; agriculture is meter; gold is meter; the cow is meter; the goat is meter; the horse is meter.

Agni is a deity; Vāta is a deity; Sūrya is a deity; Candramas is a deity; the Vasus are deities; the Rudras are deities; the Ādityas are deities; the Maruts are deities; the Viśvedevas are deities; Bṛhaspati is a deity; Indra is a deity; Varuṇa is a deity.
You are the head, you are the sovereign; you are firm, the supporter, the sustainer, the earth. For long life I take you, for splendor I take you, for agriculture I take you, for security I take you.
You are the controller, the ruler; you are the controller, the restrainer; you are the firm one, the supporter. For food you, for strength you, for wealth you, for prosperity you!
Fill the world, fill the gap; then sit down, you who are firm. Indra, Agni, and Bṛhaspati have seated you in this womb.
These dappled cows, yielding milk for the sacrifice, mix the Soma; they are the clans at the birth of the gods, in the three luminous realms of heaven.
All songs have magnified Indra, who is as expansive as the ocean—the best of charioteers among charioteers, the true lord and master of spoils.

The Swift is the Trivṛt; the Radiant is the Pañcadaśa; the Void is the Saptadaśa; the Supporter is the Ekaviṃśa; the Rush is the Aṣṭādaśa; the Heat is the Navadaśa; the Overturning is the Savim̐śa; the Splendor is the Dvāviṃśa; the Gathering is the Trayoviṃśa; the Womb is the Caturviṃśa; the Embryos are the Pañcaviṃśa; the Vital Force is the Triṇava; the Will is the Ekatrim̐śa; the Foundation is the Trayastriṃśa; the Summit of Bradhna is the Catustriṃśa; the Firmament is the Ṣaṭtriṃśa; the Turning is the Aṣṭācatvāriṃśa; the Sustainer is the Catuṣṭoma.

Thou art the portion of Agni; the overlordship of Dīkṣā; the Brahman is protected; the Trivṛt Stoma. Thou art the portion of Indra; the overlordship of Viṣṇu; the Kṣatra is protected; the Pañcadaśa Stoma. Thou art the portion of the Nṛcakṣases; the overlordship of Dhātṛ; the organ of generation is protected; the Saptadaśa Stoma. Thou art the portion of Mitra; the overlordship of Varuṇa; the rain from heaven and the wind are protected; the Ekaviṃśa Stoma.

You are the portion of the Vasus; the sovereignty of the Rudras; four-footed creatures have been won; the twenty-fourfold hymn-form (*stoma*). You are the portion of the Ādityas; the sovereignty of the Maruts; embryos have been won; the twenty-fivefold hymn-form. You are the portion of Aditi; the sovereignty of Pūṣan; vigor has been won; the twenty-sevenfold hymn-form. You are the portion of the god Savitṛ; the sovereignty of Bṛhaspati; the convergent quarters have been won; the fourfold hymn-form.

You are the portion of barley; the overlordship of non-barley; offspring are won; the forty-fourfold hymn-form (*stoma*). You are the portion of the *Ṛbhus*; the overlordship of the All-gods (*Viśve Devāḥ*); existence is won; the thirty-threefold hymn-form.

Saha and Sahasya are the two winter seasons; you are the internal bond of Agni. May Heaven and Earth be in harmony; may the waters and plants be in harmony; may the fires be in harmony. With one mind, for the sake of preeminence, let those fires that dwell between these two, Heaven and Earth, being of one purpose during the two winter seasons, enter into you just as the gods entered Indra. By that deity, in the manner of Aṅgiras, sit firm in your places!

With one [verse] they praised; creatures were produced; Prajāpati was the overlord. With three [verses] they praised; the Brahman was created; Brahmaṇaspati was the overlord. With five [verses] they praised; beings were created; the Lord of Beings (Bhūtānām patiḥ) was the overlord. With seven [verses] they praised; the seven seers (Sapta Ṛṣayaḥ) were created; Dhātṛ was the overlord.

With nine [verses] they praised; the Fathers were created; Aditi was the sovereign lady. With eleven [verses] they praised; the seasons were created; the seasonal deities were the sovereign lords. With thirteen [verses] they praised; the months were created; the Year was the sovereign lord. With fifteen [verses] they praised; the Kṣatriya power was created; Indra was the sovereign lord. With seventeen [verses] they praised; the domestic animals were created; Bṛhaspati was the sovereign lord.

They praised with nine and ten; the Śūdra and the Ārya were created; Day and Night were the presiding lords. They praised with twenty-one; the one-hoofed animals were created; Varuṇa was the presiding lord. They praised with twenty-three; the small animals were created; Pūṣan was the presiding lord. They praised with twenty-five; the wild animals were created; Vāyu was the presiding lord. They praised with twenty-seven; Heaven and Earth went apart; the Vasus, Rudras, and Ādityas followed after them; they were the presiding lords.

They praised with twenty-nine; the trees were created; Soma was the overlord. They praised with thirty-one; creatures were created; the Yavas and Ayavas were the overlords. They praised with thirty-three; all beings became tranquil; Prajāpati Parameṣṭhin was the overlord. Fill the space, fill the gap, and then sit down, you who are firm. Indra, Agni, and Bṛhaspati have seated you in this womb.
These dappled cows, yielding milk for the preparation of the oblation, mix the Soma; they are the clans at the birth of the gods, in the three luminous realms of heaven.
All songs have magnified Indra, who is as expansive as the ocean—the best of charioteers among charioteers, the true lord and master of spoils.
O Agni, Jātavedas, drive away our born enemies and repel those yet unborn. Speak for us with a gracious mind and without anger; may we abide in your triple-layered protection, O Source of Prosperity.
O Jātavedas, drive away our enemies who have already been born; repel those yet unborn. Speak for us with a benevolent mind; may we be victorious, and drive away our enemies.

The sixteenfold hymn-form is vigor, the wealth; the forty-fourfold hymn-form is luster, the wealth. You are the soil of Agni, whose name is Apas; may all the gods acclaim you. Seated here upon the back of the hymn, rich in ghee, grant us wealth accompanied by progeny through sacrifice.

Eva is the metre; Varivas is the metre; Śambhū is the metre; Paribhū is the metre; Ācchat is the metre; Manas is the metre; Vyacas is the metre; Sindhu is the metre; Samudra is the metre; Sarira is the metre; Kakubh is the metre; Trikakubh is the metre; Kāvya is the metre; Aṅkupam is the metre; Akṣarapaṅkti is the metre; Padapaṅkti is the metre; Viṣṭārapaṅkti is the metre; Kṣurobhrāja is the metre.

Ācchat is a metre; pracchat is a metre; saṃyat is a metre; viyat is a metre; bṛhat is a metre; rathantara is a metre; nikāya is a metre; vivadha is a metre; gira is a metre; bhrajas is a metre; saṃstúbh is a metre; anuṣṭúbh is a metre; evá is a metre; varivá is a metre; vayas is a metre; vayaskṛt is a metre; viṣpardhás is a metre; viśālam is a metre; chadíḥ is a metre; dūrohaṇam is a metre; tandram is a metre; aṅkāṅkam is a metre.

With the ray, quicken truth for the sake of truth; with the forward-moving, quicken dharma for the sake of dharma; with the following, quicken heaven for the sake of heaven; with the junction, quicken the intermediate space for the sake of the intermediate space; with the counterpart, quicken earth for the sake of earth; with the support, quicken rain for the sake of rain; with the forward-extended, quicken day for the sake of day; with the following, quicken night for the sake of night; with the yearning, quicken the Vasus for the sake of the Vasus; with the precursor, quicken the Ādityas for the sake of the Ādityas.

With the thread, through the increase of wealth, quicken the increase of wealth; with the gliding [soma], through what is heard, quicken what is heard; with the portion for the cattle, through the plants, quicken the plants; with the highest [portion], through the bodies, quicken the bodies; with the bestower of vigor, through what has been studied, quicken what has not been studied; with the victorious, through splendor, quicken splendor.

You are the beginning; I take you for the beginning. You are the following; I take you for the following. You are the attainment; I take you for the attainment. You are splendor; I take you for splendor.

Thou art the threefold; for the threefold, thee! Thou art the forward-turning; for the forward-turning, thee! Thou art the wide-turning; for the wide-turning, thee! Thou art the together-turning; for the together-turning, thee! Thou art the stepping-up; for the stepping-up, thee! Thou art the stepping-together; for the stepping-together, thee! Thou art the stepping-out; for the stepping-out, thee! Thou art the stepping-forth; for the stepping-forth, thee! O Lord, quicken the strength of strength!

Thou art the Queen, the eastern quarter; the Vasus are thy gods and overlords; Agni is the warder-off of missiles. May the Trivṛt Stoma support thee on the earth; may the Ājya Uktha stabilize thee for steadiness; may the Rathantara Sāman establish thee in the atmosphere. May the first-born Ṛṣis among the gods extend thee with the measure and breadth of heaven; and may this Vidhartṛ and the Adhipati, all acting in concert, seat thee and the sacrificer upon the back of the firmament, in the world of heaven.

You are Virāj, the southern quarter; the Rudras are your gods as overlords, Indra is the warder-off of missiles. May the fifteenfold Stoma support you on earth; may the Pragātha hymn establish you for steadiness; may the Bṛhat Sāman provide stability in the intermediate space. May the Ṛṣis, the first-born among the gods, extend you with the measure and the breadth of heaven. And may this Vidhartṛ and the Adhipati, all acting in concert, settle you and the sacrificer upon the back of the firmament, in the world of heaven.

You are the sovereign; the western quarter is yours. The Ādityas are your overlords; Varuṇa is the warder-off of missiles. May the seventeenfold hymn support you upon the earth; may the Marutvatīya litany establish you for steadfastness; may the Vairūpa Sāman provide you with a firm foundation. In the intermediate space, may the first-born seers among the gods extend you with the measure and breadth of heaven. Both this Ordainer and the Overlord—may they all, being in agreement, seat the sacrificer upon the back of the firmament, in the world of heaven.

The North is your own realm; the Maruts are your divine overlords; Soma is the warder-off of weapons. May the twenty-one-fold hymn (stoma) support you on earth; may the Niṣkevalya litany (uktha) establish you for steadfastness; may the Vairāja chant (sāman) provide stability in the intermediate space. May the Rishis, the first-born among the gods, extend you with the measure and breadth of heaven, along with this Dispenser and the Overlord. May they all, being in agreement, seat you and the sacrificer upon the back of the firmament, in the world of heaven.

Thou art the sovereign, the lofty quarter; the All-gods are thy overlords, Bṛhaspati is the repeller of missiles. May the Triṇava and Trayastriṃśa hymns support thee upon the earth; may the Vaiśvadeva and Āgnimāruta liturgies establish thee for steadiness; may the Śākvara and Raivata chants provide stability in the atmosphere. May the Rishis, first-born among the gods, extend thee with the measure and breadth of heaven. Both the Ordainer and this Overlord, all in harmony, shall seat the sacrificer upon the back of the firmament, in the world of light.
This one in front is Harikeśa Sūryaraśmi; Rathagṛtsa and Rathaujas are his leaders of the army and the village chieftains.

Puñjikasthalā and Kratusthalā are the two Apsarases; fanged beasts are their missile, and man-made slaughter is their weapon. Homage be to them! May they protect us; may they be gracious to us. Whomsoever we hate, and whoever hates us—him we place within their jaws.
This is the southern quarter; Viśvakarman is its lord, and Rathasvana and Rathecitra are its Senānī and Grāmaṇī.

Menakā and Sahajanyā are the two Apsarases; the Yātudhānas are their missile, and the Rākṣasas are their weapon. Homage be to them! May they protect us; may they be gracious to us. Whomever we hate and whoever hates us—him we place within their jaws.
This Viśvavyacas is behind him; his Rathaprota and Asamaratha are the leaders of the army and the village chieftains.

Pramlocantī and Anumlocantī are the two Apsarases; the tiger is their weapon, the serpent their missile. Homage be to them! May they protect us; may they be gracious to us. Whomsoever we hate and whosoever hates us—him we place within their jaws.
This one from the north is Saṃyadvasu; his two leaders of the army and the village chieftains are Tārkṣya and Ariṣṭanemi.

Viśvācī and Ghṛtācī are the two Apsarases; the waters are their weapon, and the wind is their missile. Homage be to them! May they protect us; may they be gracious to us. Whomsoever we hate and whosoever hates us—him we place within their jaws.
This one above is Arvāgvasu; his two leaders of the host and the clan, Senajit and Suṣeṇa, are [his attendants].

Urvaśī and Pūrvacitti are the two Apsarases; Avasphūrjan is their weapon, and Vidyut is their missile. Homage be to them! May they protect us; may they be gracious to us. Whomsoever we hate, and whoever hates us—him we place within their jaws.
Agni is the head of heaven, the summit, the lord of this earth; he quickens the seeds of the waters.
This Agni is the lord of thousandfold and hundredfold strength; he is the sage, the head of riches.
O Agni, Atharvan churned you forth from the lotus, from the head of the entire universe, as the one who offers the sacrifice.

You are the leader of the sacrifice and of the mid-world, where you accompany us with your auspicious teams of horses; you place your head in heaven, winning the light, and you have made your tongue, O Agni, the bearer of the oblation.
Agni has been awakened by the fuel of the people, facing the Dawn as she approaches like a milch-cow. Like great birds rising up toward a branch, his rays stream forth toward the firmament.

We have spoken a word of praise to the sage worthy of sacrifice, to the bull, the vigorous one. Gaviṣṭhira, with reverence, has fixed his far-reaching hymn upon Agni, like a golden ornament in the sky.

This one was established here as the first by the creators—the Hotṛ-priest, most skilled in sacrifice, to be praised at the rites; him whom Apnavāna and the Bhṛgus caused to shine forth, the wonderful and pervasive one, among the trees for every clan.

The watchful guardian of the people, Agni, the highly skillful, has been born for new-found prosperity. With his face anointed with ghee, he, the pure one, shines brilliantly and loftily, touching the heavens, for the sake of the Bharatas.
O Agni, the Aṅgirases found you hidden in secret, dwelling in every forest; being churned, you are born with great power, and they call you, O Aṅgiras, the son of strength.
O friends, bring together for you all your nourishment and your hymn of praise directed toward Agni, the most exalted among the peoples, the son of strength, the possessor of power.
O bull-like Agni, you gather for yourself all the wealth of the enemy; kindled at the place of *iḍ*, bring us riches.
O Agni, most rich in wonderful fame, the people among the tribes invoke you—the one with flaming hair, beloved by many—to carry their oblations.
With this homage, I invoke for you Agni, the Son of Strength—the beloved, most wise steward of the sacrifice, the immortal messenger of all.
The immortal messenger of all, the immortal messenger of all—he yokes his two ruddy steeds that provide nourishment for everyone; well-invoked, let him speed forth.
He has sped forth, well-invoked; he has sped forth, well-invoked. The sacrifice is accompanied by excellent prayer and well-performed; it is the divine bounty of the Vasus for the people.
O Agni, lord of wealth consisting of cattle, son of strength, O Jātavedas, bestow upon us great renown.
Blazing here, the wise seer Agni, worthy of praise with our song—O you of many aspects, shine forth wealth upon us!
O King Agni, by yourself, both at night and at the break of dawn, O you with sharp fangs, burn against the Rākṣasas.
May our Agni, when invoked, be auspicious; may the gift be auspicious, O fortunate one, and may the sacrifice be auspicious; and may our praises also be auspicious.
May there be auspicious praises; make your mind auspicious for the conquest of Vṛtra, by which you may prevail in battles.
With which [strength] you are like a steadfast one, enduring in battles; extend far the [bowstrings] of those who are arrogant. May we conquer through your assistances.
I think of that Agni who is the Vasu, to whom the milch-cows go home, to whom the swift horses go home, and to whom the constant prize-winners go home; bring nourishment to those who praise you!

That Agni is the Vasu whom I praise, unto whom the milch-cows come together, the swift-running steeds come together, and the well-born patrons come together; bring nourishment to those who sing thy praises!
O you who are bright with light, you cook both ladles of clarified butter in your mouth; therefore, O Lord of Power, fill us up during our hymns and bring nourishment to your praisers.
O Agni, may we today succeed through our hymns in attaining that which is auspicious, like a horse, like a sacred rite, and touching the heart; may we accomplish this for you with our offerings.
For indeed, O Agni, you have become the charioteer of auspicious will, of effective and righteous power, and of the lofty cosmic order.
Through these our hymns, O Agni, turn toward us with all your gracious countenances, as the light turns toward the sun.

I honor Agni as the Hotṛ, the bountiful Vasu, the Son of Strength, Jātavedas—the wise one, like a sage, Jātavedas—who, a god with a well-performed sacrifice, with his flame directed toward the gods, desires the radiant splendor of the clarified butter, as the oblation of ghee is poured forth with his glowing luster.
O Agni, be our closest friend, our protector, and our auspicious guardian.
Agni is the Vasu, of Vasu-like fame; come hither and bestow upon us most resplendent wealth.
Thee, O most radiant one, shining forth, we now implore for the welfare of our friends.

In that sky where the seers, kindling the fire through their austerity, performed the sacrificial session while bringing forth the light—heaven—therein I have established Agni, whom men call the one for whom the sacred grass is strewn.
May we follow him, O gods, with our wives, our sons, our brothers, and our gold; grasping the firmament in the world of the righteous, upon the third ridge in the luminous realm of heaven.

This Agni, the lord of the virtuous, the wise one who seeks the high place, has ascended to the middle of speech; established upon the back of the earth and flashing brightly, let him cast beneath his feet those who are our adversaries.
May this Agni, the most heroic, the bestower of vigor, shining with a thousandfold splendor and never failing, blaze forth; resplendent in the midst of the flood, proceed toward the celestial abodes.
Depart together, go forth together; O Agni, prepare the paths that lead to the gods. Making your parents young again, weave this thread back into you.
Awake, O Agni; be watchful! May you and this sacrificer unite their offerings and pious works. In this highest common dwelling-place, may all the gods and the sacrificers sit together.
O Agni, by that path by which you carry away a thousand, and by which [you carry] all one's possessions, by that lead this sacrifice of ours to heaven, so that it may go among the gods.
This is your seasonal womb, from which once born you shone forth; knowing it, O Agni, ascend it, and then increase our wealth.

Tapa and Tapasya are the two dewy seasons. You are the internal bond of Agni; may Heaven and Earth be in harmony, may the waters and plants be in harmony, and may the fires, being of one mind for the sake of preeminence, be in harmony as those who share a common vow. May these fires, being of one mind between Heaven and Earth during these two dewy seasons, enter [the fire] together in harmony, just as the gods entered Indra. With that deity, sit firm like Aṅgiras.

May Parameṣṭhin settle you, the luminous one, upon the back of the sky—for the sake of universal out-breathing, in-breathing, diffused breathing, and upward breathing; for stability and for movement. Sūrya is your overlord; by that deity, sit firm like Aṅgiras.
Fill the world, fill the gap; then sit down, you who are firm. Indra, Agni, and Bṛhaspati have seated you in this womb.
These dappled cows, yielding milk for the libation, mix the Soma; they are the clans at the birth of the gods, in the three luminous realms of heaven.
All songs have magnified Indra, who is as vast as the ocean; the best of charioteers among charioteers, the true lord and master of spoils.
Like a horse pricking its nose at pasture, when he has stepped forth from the great enclosure, then the wind blows after his flame; and so, thy path becomes black.
I set you down in the seat of life, in the shade of the well, in the heart of the ocean. You who possess rays and are radiant, you who shine upon the sky, upon the earth, and across the wide mid-air.
May Parameṣṭhin settle you upon the back of the sky—broad and expansive. Support the sky; make the sky firm; do not harm the sky.
For all out-breathing, in-breathing, diffused breathing, and up-breathing; for stability and for movement.
May Sūrya protect you with great well-being and most peaceful shelter; with that deity, sit firm like Aṅgiras.
You are the measure of a thousand; you are the counterpart of a thousand; you are the standard of a thousand; you are a thousandfold; for a thousand, I take you.
Homage to you, O Rudra, to your wrath, and also homage to your arrow; and homage to your two arms.
O Rudra, that auspicious form of yours which is not terrible and does not appear as evil—with that most peaceful form, O Lord of the Mountain, look upon us with favor.
O Lord of the Mountain, that arrow which you carry in your hand to discharge—O Protector of the Mountain, make it auspicious; do not harm the person or the world.
We address you with auspicious speech, O Lord of the Mountain, so that our entire world may be free from disease and well-disposed toward us.
The first divine physician, the supreme advocate, has spoken; he crushes all serpents and all sorceresses, and drives them far away downward.
We implore the wrath of him who is copper-colored, ruddy, and brown, the most auspicious one, and of those thousands of Rudras who dwell around him in every direction.
He who creeps along, blue-necked and deep red—him the cowherds have seen, him the water-carriers have seen; seen, may he be gracious to us.
Homage be to the blue-necked one, the thousand-eyed, the bountiful; and also to those who are his attendants, to them I have paid homage.
Unstring the bowstring from both ends of your bow; O Blessed One, cast away those arrows that are in your hand.
The bow of the one with matted hair is strungless, and his arrow is barbless; his arrows have perished, and his quiver has become harmless.
O most bountiful one, with that missile which was in your hand and that bow which you possessed—with that, protect us on all sides from disease.
May the missile of your bow avoid us on every side; and as for that quiver of yours, O Hero, place it far away from us.
Having drawn your bow, O thousand-eyed one, wielder of a hundred quivers, having blunted the points of your arrows, be auspicious and well-disposed toward us.
Homage to your weapon, which is unstrung yet bold; homage also to both your arms and to your bow.
Do not harm our great ones, nor our small ones; do not harm our growing ones, nor our grown ones. Do not slay our father, nor our mother; O Rudra, do not injure our dear bodies.

Do not harm us in our children or grandchildren, nor in our life-span; do not harm us in our cattle or our horses. O Rudra, do not slay our heroic men in your anger; bearing oblations, we invoke you always.

Homage to Hiraṇyabāhu, the leader of armies and lord of the quarters; homage, homage! Homage to the trees with golden hair, the lord of cattle; homage, homage! Homage to the one tawny as young grass, the radiant one, the lord of paths; homage, homage! Homage to the golden-haired one wearing the sacred thread, the lord of prosperity; homage!

Homage to Babhluśa, the hunter; homage to the Lord of foods! Homage to the weapon of Bhava; homage to the Lord of moving beings! Homage to Rudra, the archer; homage to the Lord of fields! Homage to Sūta, the unslayable; homage to the Lord of forests!

Homage to Rohita, the carpenter, the lord of trees; homage, homage to Bhuvantya, the maker of space, the lord of plants; homage, homage to Mantrin, the merchant, the lord of thickets; homage, homage to Uccairghoṣa, the one who causes shouting, the lord of foot-soldiers.

Homage to him who runs with his entire body, to the Lord of living beings, homage, homage! Homage to the victorious one, the piercer, to the Lord of those who pierce, homage, homage! Homage to the quiver-bearer, the towering one, to the Lord of thieves, homage, homage! Homage to the gliding one, the prowler, to the Lord of the forests, homage!

Homage to the deceiver, to the overreacher, to the lord of thieves, homage! Homage to the one who carries a quiver and a bow, to the lord of robbers, homage! Homage to those who bear spears, to those who seek to kill, to the lord of plunderers, homage! Homage to those who carry swords, to those who roam at night, to the lord of cut-throats, homage!

Homage to the one with the crown-protrusion, who wanders the mountains, the lord of the Kuluñcas; homage, homage to you, the archers with arrows! Homage to you as you string your bows and fix your arrows; homage to you as you draw them back and release them! Homage to you! Homage to you!

Homage to you who release [arrows] and homage to you who pierce; homage to you who sleep and homage to you who wake; homage to you who lie down and homage to you who sit; homage to you who stand and homage to you who run.

Homage to the assemblies and to you, the lords of the assemblies; homage, homage to the horses and to you, the masters of the horses; homage to the piercing ones and to you, the ones who pierce through; homage to the fierce troops and to you, the crushing ones.

Homage to you, the hosts and to you, the lords of hosts; homage to you, the troops and to you, the lords of troops; homage to you, the clever ones and to you, the lords of the clever; homage to you, the multiformed and to you, the omniformed.

Homage to the armies and homage to you who lead the armies; homage to the charioteers and homage to you who are without chariots; homage to the attendants and homage to you who gather the troops; homage to the great ones and homage to you who are small.

Homage to you, the carpenters and the chariot-makers; homage to you, the potters and the leather-workers; homage to you, the Niṣādas and the Puñjiṣṭhas; homage to you, the dog-keepers and the hunters.
Homage to the dogs and to the masters of the dogs; homage, homage to Bhava and to Rudra; homage to Śarva and to Paśupati; homage to the blue-necked one and to the white-throated one.

Homage to the one with matted hair and to the one with shorn hair; homage to the thousand-eyed one and to the wielder of the hundred bows; homage to the mountain-dweller and to Śipiviṣṭa; homage to the most bountiful one and to the possessor of arrows.
Homage to the short and to the dwarf; homage to the large and to the most extensive; homage to the aged and to the growing; homage to the foremost and to the first.

Homage to the swift and to the fleet-footed; homage to the rapid and to the hasty; homage to the one of the waves and to the one of the rivers; homage to the one of the streams and to the one of the islands.
Homage to the eldest and to the youngest; homage to the first-born and to the last-born; homage to the middlemost and to the unassuming; homage to the lowest and to the foundational.

Homage to the one who is gentle and to the one who wards off [evil], homage to the one who belongs to Yama and to the one who brings security; homage to the one who is worthy of praise and to the one who dwells in the end, homage to the one who belongs to the cultivated field and to the one who belongs to the threshing floor.
Homage to Vanya and to Kakshnya; homage to Shrava and to Pratisrava; homage to Ashushena and to Ashuratha; homage to Shura and to Avabhedin.

Homage to the one with the helmet and to the one with the armor; homage to the one clad in mail and to the one who provides protection; homage to the famous one and to him whose army is renowned; homage to the one who sounds the drum and to the one who strikes it.

Homage to the bold and to the one who reaches out; homage to the one who carries a quiver and to the one who possesses a bow-case; homage to the one with sharp arrows and to the one armed with weapons; homage to the one with excellent weapons and to the one with a good bow.

Homage to the one of the stream and to the one of the path; homage to the one of the ditch and to the one of the canal; homage to the one of the rivulet and to the one of the lake; homage to the one of the river and to the one of the pool.

Homage to the one who is in the well and to the one who is in the pit; homage to the one who is in the lightning-streak and to the one who is in the heat; homage to the one who is in the cloud and to the one who is in the lightning; homage to the one who is in the rain and to the one who is in the drought.
Homage to Vātya and to Reṣmya; homage to Vāstavya and to Vāstupa; homage to Soma and to Rudra; homage to Tāmra and to Aruṇa.

Homage to Śaṅgu and to Paśupati; homage to the Fierce and to the Terrible; homage to the One who strikes nearby and to the One who strikes from afar; homage to the Slayer and to the More-Slaying; homage to the trees with golden hair; homage to Tāra!
Homage to Śambhu and to Mayobhuva; homage to Śaṅkara and to Mayaskara; homage to Śiva and to Śivatara.

Homage to the one who has reached the further shore and to the one who has not yet reached it; homage to the one who carries across and to the one who brings forth; homage to the one on the bathing place and to the one on the riverbank; homage to the one in the young grass and to the one in the foam.
Homage to Sikatya and to Pravāhya; homage to Kiṃśila and to Kṣayaṇa; homage to Kapardin and to Pulasti; homage to Iriṇya and to Prapathya.

Homage to him who is on the journey and to him who is in the herd; homage to him who is on the couch and to him who is in the house; homage to him who is in the heart and to him who is in the dwelling; homage to him who is on the path and to him who dwells in the abyss.

Homage to the one who is dry and to the one who is green; homage to the one who belongs to the dust and to the one who belongs to the mist; homage to the one who is to be dissolved and to the one who is to be wiped away; homage to the one who is wide and to the one who is expansive.

Homage to Parṇa and to Parṇaśada; homage to him who raises up and to him who strikes down; homage to him who tears out and to him who tears away; homage to you, the makers of arrows and the makers of bows; homage, homage to you, the Kirikas, the hearts of the gods; homage to those who sift, homage to those who destroy, homage to those who have not been driven away.
O wearer of the mantle, Lord of the food, O Daridra, blue-and-red one: do not fear for these offspring, do not harm these cattle; let nothing whatsoever cause us distress.

We offer these prayers to Rudra, the powerful one with matted hair, the lord of heroes, so that there may be well-being for our bipeds and quadrupeds, and so that everything in this village may be nourished and free from disease.
O Rudra, that auspicious form of yours which is auspicious and healing at all times, the auspicious healer of disease for the cry [of pain], with that, be gracious to us so that we may live.

May the missile of Rudra pass us by, and may the ill-will of the impetuous one who seeks to harm us avoid us. O Bounteous One, relax thy firm [bow] for the sake of our patrons; O Giver of Boons, be gracious unto our children and progeny.
O most bountiful, most auspicious one, be gracious and well-disposed toward us! Having laid aside your weapon upon the highest tree and wearing a skin garment, come hither bearing your Pināka bow.
O scattered one, O blood-red one, homage be to you, O Blessed One! May those thousand missiles of yours strike down someone other than us.
Thousand upon thousands are the weapons in your arms; O Blessed One, as their master, turn their points away from us.
Those thousands of Rudras who are upon the earth—for them, at a distance of a thousand yojanas, we unstring our bows.
In this great ocean, in the intermediate space, you are present; we unstring the bows of those who are a thousand yojanas away.
The blue-necked, white-throated Rudras who have taken refuge in heaven—far away, at a distance of a thousand yojanas, we unstring their bows.
The blue-necked ones, the white-throated ones, the Śarvas who roam upon the earth below—their bows we unstring at a distance of a thousand yojanas.
Those birds that dwell in the trees, tawny as young grass, with dark-blue necks and ruddy-brown bodies—we unstring their bows at a distance of a thousand leagues.
Those who are the lords of beings, with shaven heads or matted locks—may we unstring their bows at a distance of a thousand yojanas.
Those who are the guardians of the paths, the increasers of prosperity, the warriors for life—for them we unbend our bows at a distance of a thousand leagues.
Those who wander among the sacred fords, carrying spears in their hands and wearing quivers—we unstring their bows at a distance of a thousand yojanas.
Those who pierce others while they are drinking from vessels—them we stretch out like bowstrings at a distance of a thousand yojanas.
As many Rudras as there are, and even more, who are stationed in all directions—may we unstring their bows at a distance of a thousand yojanas.

Homage be to the Rudras who are in heaven, whose arrows are rain! To them—ten to the east, ten to the south, ten to the west, ten to the north, and ten above—be homage! May they protect us; may they be gracious to us. Whomsoever we hate, and whoever hates us, him we place within their jaws.

Homage be to the Rudras who are in the intermediate space, whose arrows are the wind! To them—ten toward the east, ten to the south, ten to the west, ten to the north, and ten upward—let there be homage! May they protect us; may they be gracious to us! Whomsoever we hate and whosoever hates us, him we place within their jaws.

Homage be to the Rudras who are upon the earth, whose arrows are food! To them—ten in the east, ten in the south, ten in the west, ten in the north, and ten above—be homage! May they protect us; may they be gracious to us. Whomsoever we hate, and whosoever hates us—him we place within their jaws.
The strength resting in the stone, in the mountain—the milk gathered from the waters, the plants, and the trees—O Maruts, bestowing it together, grant us that nourishment and strength.
In the stone is your hunger; in me is your strength; let your heat reach him whom we hate.

O Agni, may these bricks of mine be milch-cows: one and ten, ten and a hundred, a hundred and a thousand, a thousand and ten thousand, ten thousand and a hundred thousand, a hundred thousand and a You are the seasons, increasers of the cosmic order; you abide in the seasons, increasers of the cosmic order. Dropping ghee, dropping honey, named Virāj, you are the wish-fulfilling cows that never diminish.
O Agni, we envelop you with the Avakā plant from the ocean; be purifying and auspicious for us.
O Agni, we envelop you with the womb of the cold; be purifying and auspicious for us.

Come to the earth, come to the reed, descend into the rivers, O Agni! You are the bile of the waters; O female frog, come hither with them, and make this sacrifice of ours pure-colored and auspicious.
This is the gathering place of the waters, the dwelling of the ocean. May your missiles burn others than us; O Purifier, be auspicious unto us.
O Agni, Purifier, with your radiant and delightful tongue, O God, bring the gods hither and worship them.
O purifying, radiant Agni, bring the gods here to us, to our sacrifice and our oblation.

With his purifying, discerning grace, he has shone upon the earth like the radiance of the dawn; like one who prevails on his journey, he is the joy of Etaśa, the ageless one who, like a thirsty man in the heat, has never grown old.
Homage to your consuming flame, homage be to your radiance! May your missiles scorch others than us; O Purifier, be auspicious unto us.
Veṭ! To him who sits among men, veṭ! To him who sits in the waters, veṭ! To him who sits on the sacrificial grass, veṭ! To him who sits in the forest, veṭ! To him who finds the light of heaven, veṭ!

Those gods who among the gods are worthy of sacrifice, who sit partaking of their year-long share; though they do not eat the oblation, may they themselves drink of the honey and the ghee at this sacrifice.

Those gods who attained godhead among the gods, who are the precursors of this sacred formulation (brahman), without whom no domain whatsoever is purified—neither on the heights of heaven nor upon the ridges of earth do they abide.
Giver of breath, giver of downward breath, giver of pervasive breath, giver of luster, giver of wide space: let your missiles burn others than us; O Purifier, be auspicious unto us!
May Agni with his sharp flame consume every devourer; may Agni win wealth for us.
The seer who, as the Hotṛ-priest, sat down offering all these worlds as an oblation—our father—he, seeking wealth through his prayer and providing the first covering, entered into the lower regions.
What was the foundation, what was the starting point, and how was it? From what did Viśvakarman, the all-seeing, generating the earth, spread out the sky by his greatness?
With eyes on every side and a face on every side, with arms on every side and feet on every side, the one God, generating heaven and earth, fans them together with his arms and wings.
What was the wood, and what was that tree, from which they fashioned heaven and earth? O wise ones, ask this with your mind: upon what did he stand while supporting the worlds?

O Viśvakarman, those abodes of yours which are highest, which are lowest, and these which are intermediate—teach them to your friends at this oblation, O self-dependent one; worship yourself, increasing in your own body.
O Viśvakarman, strengthened by the oblation, sacrifice yourself to both the earth and the heaven. Let other rivals around us be confounded; here let the bountiful patron be ours.

Let us invoke today, for our protection in the struggle for booty, the Lord of Speech, Viśvakarman, who is swift as thought; may he, the source of all well-being and the performer of righteous deeds, graciously accept all our invocations for our aid.

O Viśvakarman, by means of the strengthening oblation, you made Indra a protector who cannot be slain; to him the many tribes bowed down, so that he might be this formidable one, worthy of invocation.

The Father of the eye, wise in his mind, generated these two [worlds] as they bowed down like clarified butter; when their eastern limits were made firm, then indeed Heaven and Earth spread themselves out.
Viśvakarman, the far-seeing, the creator and ordainer, the highest manifestation; their sacrifices rejoice together with nourishment where they say there is one beyond the seven seers.
He who is our father and progenitor, who is the ordainer and knows all abodes and all beings—he alone is the sole namer of the gods; toward him all other worlds go for instruction.
The ancient seers, like singers in great number, sought wealth from him; they who, seated in the unmanifested and manifested realm, brought these beings into existence.
That which is beyond heaven, beyond this earth, beyond the gods and the Asuras—what was that first embryo which the waters received, wherein the ancient gods beheld one another?
The waters first received that embryo wherein all the gods came together; it was fixed upon the navel of the Unborn, in which all existing worlds abide.
You do not perceive him who generated these [worlds]; something else has come between you. Enveloped by mist and idle chatter, the reciters of hymns wander about, seeking only their own sustenance.

For Viśvakarman was born as a god; then he became a Gandharva for the second time; as a third, he became the father who generated the plants, and he distributed the embryo of the waters in many places.
Swift, sharpening his weapons like a terrifying bull, the striker, the agitator of the peoples; the roaring, unblinking, sole hero, Indra has conquered a hundred armies at once.

With him who is all-shaking, unblinking, victorious, eager for battle, difficult to overthrow, and bold—with that Indra, O men, conquer and prevail in combat, with the bull who holds arrows in his hand.

He, the controller, with his bow in hand and his quiver, is the one who brings together the hosts for battle; Indra is the conqueror of the joined forces, the drinker of Soma, strong of arm, possessing a formidable bow, and a shooter with well-aimed arrows.
O Bṛhaspati, fly around with your chariot, slaying the Rākṣasas and driving away our enemies; shattering the armies and crushing them in battle, be the protector of our chariots as you conquer.
O Indra, discoverer of strength, elder, preeminent hero, powerful, vigorous, victorious, fierce, surpassing hero, surpassing warrior, born of might, winner of cattle—mount your victorious chariot!

The breaker of the enclosure, the winner of cattle, with arms like thunderbolts, conquering the race and crushing [the foe] with his might—O kinsmen, follow this Indra with valor; O friends, rally together after him!
Piercing through the cow-pens with might, the pitiless hero Indra, of a hundredfold wrath, unshakable, subduer of armies, and invincible—may he protect our troops in the battles.
May Indra be their leader; may Bṛhaspati, the sacrificial fee, the sacrifice, and Soma go before them. May the Maruts march at the head of the divine armies as they shatter and conquer.
The fierce roar of the gods has arisen—the host of Indra the bull, of King Varuṇa, of the Ādityas, and of the Maruts; the shout of the high-minded ones who shake the world as they conquer.
O Maghavan, rouse up our weapons; rouse up the spirits of my warriors. O slayer of Vṛtra, rouse up the vigor of the steeds; let the shouts of the victorious chariots go forth.
May Indra be on our side when the banners meet; may those arrows which are ours be victorious. May our heroes be superior; O gods, protect us in our invocations.
Bewildering the minds of these men, seize their limbs, O Apvā; go forth! Advance against them and burn them with sorrows in their hearts; let the enemies be possessed by blinding darkness.
Released, fly away, O arrow, sharpened by sacred prayer; go to the enemies, fall upon them, and leave not one of them remaining.
O ghosts, may you be victorious; may Indra, the lord of men, grant you protection. May your arms be formidable so that you shall be invincible.
O Maruts, that army of our adversaries which approaches us, vying with us in its might—hide it in a lawless darkness, so that these men shall not recognize one another.
Where arrows fly together like boys with hair-locks, there may Indra, Bṛhaspati, and Aditi grant protection; may they grant protection for all days.
I cover your vital organs with armor; may King Soma clothe you with immortality. May Varuṇa make for you a space wider than the wide; may the gods rejoice after you as you conquer.
Lead him upward, O Agni, you who are invoked with clarified butter; unite him with the increase of wealth and make him abundant with progeny.
O Indra, lead this man further forward; may he be the master of his kinsmen. Endow him with splendor; may he be a giver of portions to the gods.
O Agni, do thou cause that man to prosper in whose house we prepare the oblation; for him may the gods speak in favor, as well as this Brahmaṇaspati.
May all the gods, O Agni, lift you up with their thoughts; may you, who are very auspicious, fair-faced, and rich in light, be gracious to us.

May the five divine quarters protect the sacrifice, O goddesses, driving away ignorance and ill-will; bestowing upon the lord of the sacrifice an abundance of wealth, the sacrifice has been established upon an abundance of wealth.

Upon the kindled fire, the one being magnified, winged with hymns, worthy of praise, and grasped—the gods, having taken hold of the heated *gharma*, performed the sacrifice when they offered the sacrifice with vital strength.

For the divine upholder, the lover [of the gods], the god-glorying one, the well-minded one with a hundredfold streams; having encompassed the sacrifice, the gods came; the gods stood as *adhvaryu*s for the gods.
The oblation is prepared; let the immolator sacrifice it for the sake of peace. Where the fourth sacrifice proceeds with the offering, there may the prayers and our blessings be graciously accepted.
Savitar, with golden hair and sunbeams, has raised his eternal light in the east; at his impulse, the wise Pūṣan goes forth, the guardian who beholds all beings.

This celestial chariot sits in the midst of heaven, having filled the two worlds and the intermediate space. It gazes upon all the ghee-dripping regions that extend between the eastern and western horizons.

The bull, the ocean, the ruddy one, the fair-winged bird, has entered the womb of the ancient father. Placed in the midst of heaven, the dappled stone has strode forth; he guards the two ends of the realm.
All songs have magnified Indra, who is as vast as the ocean—the best of charioteers among charioteers, the true lord and master of spoils.
May the invoker of the gods bring [them] to the sacrifice; may the invoker of favor bring [it] to the sacrifice. May Agni, the god, worship the gods and bring them to the sacrifice.
At the impulse of the thunderbolt, Indra has seized me with the upward-grasp; then, by the downward-grasp, he has cast my rivals beneath me.
The gods have increased the sacred word (brahman), both the uplifting and the suppressing; then may Indra and Agni scatter my rivals in all directions.
Advance toward the vault of heaven with Agni, bearing the fire-pan in your hands; having gone to the back of the sky, the light of heaven, join yourselves with the gods.
Go forth, O Agni, knowing the way, along the eastern quarter; be here the foremost fire of fires. Shining brightly, illumine all the directions; bestow strength upon our bipeds and our quadrupeds.
From the earth I have ascended to the intermediate space; from the intermediate space I have ascended to heaven. From the back of the firmament of heaven, I have gone to the light of *svar*.
Going to heaven, they look not back; they ascend to the sky and to the two worlds, they who, being well-knowing, have extended the sacrifice that flows in every direction.

O Agni, go forth as the first of those seeking the gods, the eye of both gods and mortals. May the sacrificers, desiring to offer sacrifice and being in harmony with the Bhr̥gus, go safely to the heavenly light.
Night and Dawn, like-minded yet diverse in form, moving together, suckle the one infant. The golden disk shines between heaven and earth; the gods, bestowers of wealth, have sustained Agni.

O Agni, thousand-eyed, hundred-headed, a hundred are your out-breaths, a thousand your diffused breaths. You are the lord of thousandfold wealth; for that sake we pay homage to you, for the sake of strength—svāhā!
You are the fair-winged Garuḍa; sit upon the back of the earth. Fill the mid-air with your radiance, prop up the sky with your light, and make firm the quarters with your splendor.
Being invoked, O Agni of beautiful countenance, sit properly in your place from the east; in this subsequent recitation, may all the gods and the sacrificer sit together.
Of that desirable Savitṛ, I choose the wondrous, all-beneficent favor, which Kaṇva milked from him—the swelling, great cow, with her thousand streams of milk.

Let us worship you in your highest birth, O Agni; let us worship with hymns in your lower dwelling-place. From whatever womb you have arisen, that I worship; into you, when well-kindled, they have offered oblations.
O Agni, shine forth for us, well-inflamed with your unextinguished flame, O youngest one; unto you all sacrificial strengths ever approach.
O Agni, may we today succeed through our offerings in this hymn—like a horse, like a noble resolve—that touches the heart. May we prosper for you with our praises.

I offer consciousness with mind and clarified butter, so that the gods, who increase the cosmic order and are eager for the oblation, may come here. To the Lord of all existence, to Viśvakarman, I offer every day an invincible oblation.

Seven are your fuel-sticks, O Agni, seven your tongues, seven the seers, and seven your beloved abodes. Through seven officiating priests they worship you in seven ways; fill the seven wombs with clarified butter—*svāhā*!
Śukrajyotis, Citrajyotis, Satyajyotis, and Jyotiṣmat; Śukra, Ṛtapā, and Atyamhas.
Such-like and otherwise-like, similar and corresponding; measured and well-measured, they bear the burden together.
And Order, and Truth, and the Firm, and the Supporter; and the Sustainer, and the Ordainer, and the Upholders.
Ṛtajit, Satyajit, Senajit, Suṣeṇa, Antimitra, and Dūreamitra constitute the host.
Such as you are, of such a kind, come hither to us—equal and corresponding ones; O Maruts, being measured and well-measured, united in bearing, come today to this sacrifice of ours.
The self-strong, the devourer, the inflamer, and the householder; the playful, the powerful, and the victorious.
Ugra and Bhīma and Dhvānta and Dhuni, Sāsahvān and Abhiyugvan and Vikṣipa—svāhā!
The divine hosts, the Maruts, became followers of Indra; just as the divine hosts, the Maruts, became followers of Indra, so may both the divine and human hosts become followers of this sacrificer.
O Agni, suckle at this breast, full of vigor and swelling with water, in the midst of the flood; enjoy the honeyed fountain, O Courser, and enter your oceanic dwelling.
Ghee has been mixed; ghee is his womb; he rests in ghee; ghee is his abode. According to your wont, bring [the gods] here; rejoice; O Bull, carry the oblation consecrated with Svāhā!

From the ocean a wave rich in sweetness has arisen; through the *upāṃśu* [cup], it has attained immortality. That which is the secret name of clarified butter is the tongue of the gods and the navel of immortality.
Let us proclaim our names; let us offer oblations of clarified butter at this sacrifice with acts of homage. May the Brahman hear the hymn being recited; the four-horned bull has bellowed this.
He has four horns, three feet, two heads, and seven hands; bound in three ways, the bull bellows loudly; the great god has entered into mortals.

The gods discovered the threefold beneficial clarified butter hidden by the Paṇis within the cow; Indra produced one part, Sūrya produced one, and from Vena they fashioned one by their own inherent power.
These [streams] flow from the ocean within the heart; having a hundred paths, they cannot be perceived by an enemy. I behold the streams of clarified butter; in their midst stands the golden reed.
The streams flow rightly, like milch-kine, being purified within by the heart and the mind; these waves of clarified butter rush forth like deer fleeing from a swift hunter.
Like swift birds on the path of the ocean, the mighty streams of clarified butter fly forth, overtaking the wind; like a ruddy steed, they break through the barriers, swelling with their waves.
Like beautiful women smiling as they go to a gathering, the streams of clarified butter have approached Agni with kindling-sticks; finding pleasure in them, Jātavedas desires them.

Like a maiden adorning herself for the bridal procession, I gaze upon the ointments as they are being applied; where Soma is pressed and where the sacrifice is performed, there the streams of clarified butter flow forth in purification.
Flow toward our excellent praise in the contest for cattle; bestow auspicious riches upon us! Lead this sacrifice of ours to the gods; the streams of clarified butter flow, sweet with honey.

Upon your abode the entire world is supported: within the ocean, within the heart, and within life. May we attain that honeyed wave of yours, which has been brought to the assembly at the face of the waters.
May my strength and my procreation, my departure and my pervasion, my meditation and my will, my tone and my fame, my renown and my hearing, my light and my heaven be perfected through sacrifice.

May my out-breath and my in-breath, my diffused breath and my life-force, my consciousness and my intention, my speech and my mind, my sight and my hearing, my skill and my strength, be perfected through sacrifice.

May my vital energy and my strength, my self and my body, my shelter and my armor, my limbs and my bones, my joints and my physical forms, and my life-span and my old age, be perfected through sacrifice.

May my preeminence and my sovereignty, my indignation and my wrath, my impetuosity and my water, my greatness and my breadth, my width and my height, my length and my growth, and my increase be perfected through sacrifice.

May truth and my faith, and my world and my wealth, and my universe and my greatness, and my play and my joy, and what has been born and what is yet to be born, and my well-spoken hymn and my good deed—may these all be perfected through sacrifice.

May my *ṛta* and my *amṛta*, my freedom from disease and my freedom from illness, my vitality and my long life, my absence of enemies and my fearlessness, my happiness and my bed, my good wives and my auspicious day, be made perfect through sacrifice.

May my controller and my upholder, my security and my steadfastness, my universe and my greatness, my consciousness and my knowledge, my procreation and my productivity, my plow and my resting place, prosper through sacrifice.

May welfare for me and joy for me, and what is dear to me and my desire, and my wish and good-mindedness for me, and fortune for me and wealth for me, and prosperity for me and excellence for me, and preeminence for me and glory for me—may these be perfected through sacrifice.

May my nourishment and my pleasant speech, my milk and my sap, my clarified butter and my honey, my shared meal and my shared drink, my agriculture and my rain, and my victory and my triumph through breaking forth—may these all be perfected through sacrifice.

May my wealth and my riches, my prosperity and my growth, my pervasiveness and my power, my fullness and my greater fullness, my grain and my imperishability, my food and my freedom from hunger, be perfected through sacrifice.

May my wealth and what is to be known, my past and my future, my good course and my auspicious path, my prosperity and my power, my accomplishment and my means of accomplishment, my intellect and my noble insight, be perfected through sacrifice.
May my rice and my barley, my beans and my sesame, my mung beans and my lentils, my millet and my panicum, my fine grains and my wild rice, my wheat and my lentils, be perfected through sacrifice.
May my stone and my clay, my hills and my mountains, my sands and my trees, my gold and my iron, my tin and my copper, my lead and my pewter be perfected through sacrifice.

May my fire and my waters, my plants and my herbs, my crops ripened by cultivation and my crops ripened without cultivation, my domestic animals and my wild animals, my wealth and my acquisition, my past prosperity and my future fortune, be perfected through sacrifice.
May my wealth and my dwelling, my ritual action and my power, my purpose and my approach, my desire and my course, be perfected through sacrifice.
May Agni and Indra for me, Soma and Indra for me, Savitṛ and Indra for me, Sarasvatī and Indra for me, Pūṣan and Indra for me, Bṛhaspati and Indra for me—may they be perfected through sacrifice.

May Mitra and Indra for me, Varuna and Indra for me, Dhatar and Indra for me, Tvashtar and Indra for me, the Maruts and Indra for me, and all the gods and Indra for me, be perfected through sacrifice.

May the earth and Indra for me, and the atmosphere and Indra for me, and the sky and Indra for me, and the years and Indra for me, and the lunar mansions and Indra for me, and the quarters and Indra for me—may they all be perfected through sacrifice.

May my *am̐śu* and my *raśmi*, my *adābhya* and my *adhipati*, my *upām̐śu* and my *antaryāma*, my *aindravāyava* and my *maitrāvaruṇa*, my *āśvina* and my *pratiprasthāna*, my *śukra* and my *manthī*—may they be perfected through sacrifice.

May my Āgrayaṇa and my Vaiśvadeva, my Dhruva and my Vaiśvānara, my Aindrāgna and my Mahāvaiśvadeva, my Marutvatīyas and my Niṣkevalya, my Sāvitra and my Sārasvata, my Patnīvata and my Hāriyojana be perfected through sacrifice.

May my *sruva*-ladles and my *camasa*-cups, my *vāyavya*-vessels and my *droṇakalaśa*-vessel, my pressing-stones and my two pressing-boards, my *pūtabhṛt* and my *ādhavanīya* vessels, my altar and my sacrificial grass, my purificatory bath and my cry of "Svāhā"—may these all be perfected through sacrifice.

May Agni and my Gharma, and Arka and my Sūrya, and Prāṇa and my Aśvamedha, and Pṛthivī and my Aditi, and Diti and my Dyau, and my fingers, the Śakvarīs, and the quarters be perfected through sacrifice.
May my vow and my seasons, my austerity and my year, my day and night, my thighs and knees, and my Bṛhat and Rathantara [sāmans] be perfected through sacrifice.

And one for me, and three for me, and three for me, and five for me, and five for me, and seven for me, and seven for me, and nine for me, and nine for me, and eleven for me, and eleven for me, and thirteen for me, and thirteen for me, and fifteen for me, and fifteen for me, and seventeen for me, and seventeen for me, and nineteen for me, and nineteen for me, and twenty-one for me, and twenty-one for me, and twenty-three for me, and twenty-three for me, and twenty-five for me, and twenty-five for me, and twenty-seven for me, and twenty-seven for me, and twenty-nine for me, and twenty-nine for me, and thirty-one for me, and thirty-one for me, and thirty-three for me, and thirty-three for me—may they be made perfect through sacrifice.

May my four and my eight, and my eight and my twelve, and my twelve and my sixteen, and my sixteen and my twenty, and my twenty and my twenty-four, and my twenty-four and my twenty-eight, and my twenty-eight and my thirty-two, and my thirty-two and my thirty-six, and my thirty-six and my forty, and my forty and my forty-four, and my forty-four and my forty-eight—may they be perfected through sacrifice.

May my three-year-old male goat and my three-year-old female goat, my bull two years old and my cow two years old, my five-year-old male goat and my five-year-old female goat, my three-year-old steer and my three-year-old heifer, and my four-year-old bull and my four-year-old cow, be made perfect through sacrifice.
May my draft-ox and my heifer, my bull and my cow, my stud-bull and my barren cow, my draught-ox and my milch-cow prosper through the sacrifice.

Hail to strength! Hail to impulsion! Hail to the after-born! Hail to will! Hail to Vasu! Hail to the lord of the day! Hail to the day! Hail to the bewildered one! Hail to the bewildered one belonging to Vainamśin! Hail to Ainvamśin belonging to Āntyāyana! Hail to Āntya belonging to Bhauvana! Hail to the lord of the world! Hail to the sovereign lord! Hail to Prajāpati! This is thy delight, O Mitra; thou art the controller, the restrainer. For vigor thee! For rain thee! For the sovereignty over creatures thee!

May life be perfected through sacrifice; may breath be perfected through sacrifice; may sight be perfected through sacrifice; may hearing be perfected through sacrifice; may speech be perfected through sacrifice; may mind be perfected through sacrifice; may the self be perfected through sacrifice; may the Brahman be perfected through sacrifice; may light be perfected through sacrifice; may heaven be perfected through sacrifice; may the *pṛṣṭha* be perfected through sacrifice; may sacrifice itself be perfected through sacrifice. The *stoma*, the *yajus*, the *ṛc*, and the *sāman*; the *bṛhat* and the *rathantara*; we have gone to heaven, O gods; we have become immortal; we have become the offspring of Prajāpati. Veṭ! Svāhā!
Now, at the impulse of strength, we celebrate with our speech the great Mother, named Aditi, in whom this entire world has entered; may the god Savitar impel for us the sacred law within her.
May all the Maruts come today with every aid; may all the fires be well-kindled. May all the gods come to us with their protection; may all wealth and strength be ours.
May Vāja protect us from the seven directions or from the four distant realms; may Vāja protect us here in the winning of wealth along with all the gods.
May Vāja impel our gift today; may Vāja arrange the gods according to the seasons. For Vāja has begotten me with all heroes; as lord of Vāja, may I conquer all quarters.
May Vāja be before us and also in our midst; may Vāja strengthen the gods with our oblation. For Vāja has made me possessed of all heroes; may I become a lord of Vāja in all directions.
I unite myself with the milk of the earth; I unite myself with the waters and the plants. Thus may I, O Agni, win the prize of strength.
Place milk in the earth, milk in the plants, milk in heaven, and milk in the intermediate space; may the quarters of the sky be full of milk for me.
At the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins, with the hands of Pūṣan, with the restraint of Sarasvatī, the controller of speech, I consecrate you with the sovereign power of Agni.

Agni, the upholder of cosmic order, whose abode is truth, is the Gandharva; his Apsarases are the plants, named Delights. May he protect this our spiritual power and political power. To him, Svāhā! Vāṭ! To them, Svāhā!

The Sun, the possessor of all songs, is the Gandharva; his Apsarases are named Āyus. May he protect this our spiritual power (brahman) and our ruling power (kṣatra). To him, Svāhā! Vāṭ! To them, Svāhā!

Suṣumṇa, the sun-rayed, the moon, is the Gandharva; his Apsarases are named Bhekurayas. May he protect this our spiritual power (brahman) and our ruling power (kṣatra). To him, Svāhā! Vāṭ! To them, Svāhā!
The swift, all-pervading Vāta is the Gandharva; his Apsarases are named Ūrjas. May he protect this our spiritual power (brahman) and our ruling power (kṣatra). To him, Svāhā! Vāṭ! To them, Svāhā!

Bhujyu Suparṇa, the sacrifice, is the Gandharva; his Apsarases are named Stāvās. May he protect this our spiritual power (brahman) and our sovereign power (kṣatra). To him, Svāhā! Vāṭ! To them, Svāhā!

Prajāpati Viśvakarman is the Gandharva; his Apsarases are the Ṛk and Sāman verses, named Eṣṭayas. May he protect this our spiritual power (brahman) and our ruling power (kṣatra). To him, Svāhā! Vāṭ! To them, Svāhā!
O Lord of the world, O Prajāpati, you whose dwellings are above us or here on earth, grant great protection to this sacred power (brahman) and to this ruling power (kṣatra); Svāhā!

You are the ocean, possessed of breath, the giver of moisture; bringing bliss and prosperity, blow upon me! Svāhā! You are the Marut, the host of the Maruts; bringing bliss and prosperity, blow upon me! Svāhā! You are the seeker of aid, the worshipful one; bringing bliss and prosperity, blow upon me! Svāhā!
O Agni, those splendors of yours which extend across the sky with rays reaching the sun—with all of them, grant us radiance today for the sake of our people.
O gods, those splendors of yours which are in the sun, and those splendors which are in the cows and in the horses—with all of those, O Indra and Agni, and O Bṛhaspati, bestow splendor upon us.
Bestow luster upon our brahmins; grant us luster among the kings; grant us luster among the commoners and the śūdras; bestow luster upon me through luster.

That I ask of you, adoring you with a sacred prayer; that the sacrificer desires from you through his oblations. O Varuṇa, be present here without anger; O you of wide renown, do not steal away our life.
Svar na gharmah svāhā! Svar na arkah svāhā! Svar na śukrah svāhā! Svar na jyotih svāhā! Svar na sūryah svāhā!
I yoke Agni with power and with ghee—the celestial, well-winged, great bird in vigor. With him may we go to the summit of the radiant realm, ascending to the sky, to the highest vault.

These two ageless wings of yours, O Agni, like those of a bird, with which you drive away the Rākṣasas—with those may we fly to the world of the doers of good deeds, where the first-born, ancient seers have gone.
The Moon is skillful, a falcon, true to the cosmic order, a golden-winged bird, swift and active. Seated firmly in the great assembly, let there be homage to you; do not harm me.
You are the head of heaven, the navel of the earth, the strength of the waters and the plants; you are all-life, wide-extending protection, and homage to the path.

You stand supported upon the head of the universe; your heart is in the ocean, your life-force is in the waters. Give us water, burst open the reservoir! From heaven, from Parjanya, from the intermediate space, and from the earth—from those places, favor us with rain.
The sacrifice has been offered by the Bhṛgus; it is full of blessings through the Vasus. From that sacrifice, well-offered and well-pleased, may you bring us wealth here.
May Agni, the beloved one, invoked with oblations, fulfill our sacrifice; may this offering be well-savored by the gods. Homage!

Whatever has flowed forth from intention, or has been gathered from the heart or the mind, or from the eye—follow after that as a beacon toward the world of those who have performed good deeds, where the first-born, ancient seers have gone.
I entrust this to you in common abode, O Jātavedas, that treasure which you have brought here; the lord of the sacrifice shall follow you here—recognize him in the highest heaven.

Know this in the highest heaven, O gods who share a common dwelling: recognize his form when he arrives by the paths traveled by the gods; make manifest for him the merit of his sacrifices and pious works.
Awake, O Agni! Be watchful! May you and this sacrificer unite their offerings and pious works. Upon this highest common seat, may all the gods and the sacrificers sit together.
O Agni, by that path by which you carry a thousand, by which you carry all wealth, lead this sacrifice of ours to heaven to go among the gods.
With the sacrificial grass, the enclosing sticks, the ladle, the altar, and the sacred straw—with this *ṛc*, lead this sacrifice of ours to heaven, so that it may go among the gods.

Whatever has been given, whatever has been received from others, whatever pious works have been performed, and whatever sacrificial fees have been bestowed—may Agni Vaiśvakarman place all that for us among the gods in heaven.
Where the streams of honey and of clarified butter do not fail—may Agni Vaiśvakarman place that heavenly light for us among the gods.
I am Agni, by birth Jātavedas; clarified butter is my eye, immortality is in my mouth. I am the threefold light, the measurer of the mid-region, the unaging heat; "oblation" is my name.
I am named the *ṛc*s, I am named the *yajus*es, I am named the *sāman*s. Those fires that belong to the people of the east upon this earth—you are the highest among them; impel us toward long life.
O Indra, we turn you toward us for the slaying of Vṛtra, for strength, and for victory in battle.
O Indra, much-invoked, you crushed Kuṇāru, who dwelt together with his wife yet was handless; O Indra, with your might, you struck down the footless Vṛtra as he grew arrogant and hostile.
O Indra, strike down our adversaries; cast those who attack us low. Whoever seeks to harm us, send him down into the deepest darkness.

Like a fearsome wild beast, roaming and dwelling in the mountains, you have come from the furthest distance. Sharpening your bolt and making your weapon keen, O Indra, strike down the enemies and drive away those who oppose us.
May Vaiśvānara come to us for our protection from afar; may Agni approach our well-spoken hymns.
Questioned in heaven, questioned on earth, Agni has entered all plants; Vaiśvānara Agni, questioned with power, may he protect us from harm by day and by night.

May we obtain your desire, O Agni, through your protection; may we obtain wealth, O Lord of Wealth, with noble heroes. May we obtain booty, seeking booty; may we obtain your undecaying and ageless splendor.
We have indeed fulfilled your desire today, having approached you with uplifted hands and with homage. O Agni, as a sage, worship the gods with a most sacrificial mind and with an unfailing thought.
May Agni, the concealer of the dwelling, Indra, the god Bṛhaspati the priest, and all the gods, being of one mind, protect our sacrifice for the sake of prosperity.
O youngest one, protect the men who offer oblations; hear our songs; and guard our offspring as well as ourselves.

I unite you, who are sweet, with what is sweet; you, who are sharp, with what is sharp; you, who are immortal, with what is immortal; you, who are honey-sweet, with what is honey-sweet—[I unite you] together with Soma.
Thou art Soma; be prepared for the two Aśvins; be prepared for Sarasvatī; be prepared for Indra the Good Protector.
Pour out the pressed juice all around—the Soma which is the supreme oblation, the manly one that has flowed within the waters; he has pressed the Soma with the stones.
Purified by the wind with a strainer, Soma has flowed westward; he is the worthy companion and friend of Indra.
Purified by the filter of the wind, Soma has flowed forth westward, the fitting friend of Indra.
The daughter of the Sun purifies your flowing Soma with her eternal, continuous fleece.

The Brahman, the Kṣatra, brilliance, and sensory power flow forth; Soma, pressed and poured out with the surā, is for intoxication. O God, satisfy the deities with your bright splendor; bestow food upon the sacrificer with your essence.
Surely, just as those who possess barley reap it in due order, separating it out, so do thou bring here the food of those who offer their homage upon the sacred grass.
You are taken with a support; I take you for the Aśvins, for Sarasvatī, and for Indra the Good Protector.
This is your womb; for brilliance you, for heroism you, for strength you.
For many indeed are the seats established for you by the gods; do not mingle together in the highest heaven! You are the spirited Surā, and this is Soma; do not harm me as you enter your own womb.
You are taken with a support: yours is the splendor of the Aśvins, the vigor of Sarasvatī, and the strength of Indra. This is your birthplace; for delight you, for bliss you, for majesty you.

You are splendor; bestow splendor upon me. You are vigor; bestow vigor upon me. You are strength; bestow strength upon me. You are vital power; bestow vital power upon me. You are wrath; bestow wrath upon me. You are conquest; bestow conquest upon me.
May she who protects against the tiger, the cholera, and both the wolf—the falcon, the winged bird, and the lion—protect this man from distress.
When the son, joyfully sucking, has crushed his mother—O Agni, by this I become free from that debt; my parents have not been harmed by me.
You are mingled; mingle me with what is auspicious. You are separated; separate me from evil.
The gods performed the sacrifice as a healing remedy, with the two Aśvins as physicians; Sarasvatī, the physician with her speech, bestowed vital powers upon Indra.

The young shoots are the form of the initiation; the sprouts are the form of the introductory offering; the parched grains are the form of the purchase of Soma; the honey is the form of the Soma-stalks.
The *māsara* is the form of hospitality; the *nagnahu* is the form of the *mahāvīra* vessel; and this *surā* pressed for three nights is the form of the *upasad* rites.
The form of Soma, once purchased, is poured out as the fermenting liquor; it is milked by the Aśvins as a medicine—Indra’s portion for Indra, and Sarasvatī’s.
The stool is the form of the royal throne; the cauldron for holding the *surā* is the form of the altar. The space between is the form of the *uttaravedi*; the *kārotara* is the physician.

The altar is fully attained through the altar; the sacrificial grass, through the sacrificial grass; the power of the senses, through the sacrificial post; the sacrificial post is attained through the sacrificial post; and the consecrated fire, through the fire.
The Havirdhāna shed is for the Aśvins, the Āgnīdhra shed is for Sarasvatī; for Indra the Sadas has been prepared, and the Gārhapatya fire is for the wives of the gods.

Through the *praisha* formulas he obtains the *praishas*, through the *āprī* hymns the *āprīs* of the sacrifice; through the *prayāja* offerings he obtains the *anuyājas*, and through the *vaṣaṭ* calls the oblations.
Through animals he obtains animals; through sacrificial cakes, the oblations; through the meters, the *sāmidhenī* verses; and through the *yājyā* verses, the *vaṣaṭ* calls.
Parched grains, groats, flour, parched barley, milk, curd, the form of Soma, the oblation, the clotted curd, the whey, and honey.
The jujube fruit is the form of parched grains; wheat is the form of the scattered grain offering; the jujube berry is the form of roasted flour; and wild millet is the form of the gruel.
The form of milk is barley; the form of curd is jujube fruits; the form of Soma is whey; the form of the Saumya offering is the clotted curds (āmikṣā).

"Ā śrāvaya" (Make it heard) refers to the *stotriya* verses; "pratyāśrāvaḥ" (The response) is the *anurūpa*; "yajā" (Sacrifice) has the form of the *dhāyyā* verses; and the *pragāthas* are the "yeyajāmahāḥ."

Through the half-verses one attains the form of the *ukthas*; through the word-divisions (*pada*), the *nivid*s; through the *praṇava*s, the form of the *śastra*s; and through the milk, the *soma* is obtained.
The morning pressing was obtained from the Aśvins; the midday pressing for Indra from Indra; and the third pressing, for the Viśvedevas, from Sarasvatī.

Through the Vāyavya cups one obtains the Vāyavyas; through the Sata, the Droṇakalaśa; through the two Kumbhīs, the two Ambhṛṇas; when [the Soma] is pressed, one obtains the Sthālīs through the Sthālīs.
By the Yajus-formulas the Grahas are attained; by the Grahas the Stomas and Viṣṭutis; by the meters the Ukthas and Śastras; and by the Sāman the Avabhṛtha bath is attained.

Through the *iḍā* invocations he obtains the portions; through the *sūktavāka*, the blessings; through the *śamyu* formula, the *patnīsaṃyāja* offerings; and through the *samiṣṭayajus*, the completion of the sacrifice.
Through the vow one attains consecration; through consecration one attains the sacrificial fee; the sacrificial fee attains faith; and through faith, truth is attained.
Such is the full form of the sacrifice as it was performed by the gods and by Brahmā; all of that one obtains when the Sautrāmaṇī is offered within the sacrifice.

With reverence, the mighty ones impel the sacrifice, rich in Soma, seated upon the sacred grass, and abounding in heroes; offering Soma to the deities in heaven, may we, the sacrificers with beautiful hymns, rejoice in Indra.
That essence of yours which is gathered in the plants, the vigor of Soma, the pressed juice of Surā—with that, gladden the sacrificer with exhilaration, Sarasvatī, the Aśvins, Indra, and Agni.
That which Sarasvatī extracted from the Asura Namuci for the sake of Indra’s power—this very bright, honeyed, sparkling drop, King Soma, I consume here.
Whatever of this pressed, flavorful juice was sipped here by Indra with his powers—that Soma-king I now consume here with a gracious mind.

To the fathers who partake of the *svadhā*, *svadhā*! Adoration! To the grandfathers who partake of the *svadhā*, *svadhā*! Adoration! To the great-grandfathers who partake of the *svadhā*, *svadhā*! Adoration! The fathers have eaten; the fathers have rejoiced; the fathers have been satisfied. O fathers, be purified!
May the Soma-loving ancestors purify me; may the grandfathers purify me; may the great-grandfathers purify me with the hundred-year-old purifier.
May the grandfathers, worthy of Soma, purify me; may the great-grandfathers purify me. Through the purifier that grants a hundred-year life, may I attain a full span of life.
O Agni, purify our lives; bring us strength and nourishment; drive misfortune far away.
May the divine beings purify me; may they purify my thoughts with their minds. May all beings purify me; O Jātavedas, do thou purify me.
O God Agni, shining with brilliance, purify me with the bright purifier, according to the power of your wisdom.
O Agni, may that purifier of yours which is spread out within the flame purify my sacred formulation (brahman).
May he who is the purifier, the all-seeing Pavamāna, cleanse me today with his filter; may he who is the priest purify me.
O God Savitṛ, with both [means]—with the filter and with the impulse—purify me on every side.
The purifying goddess, belonging to all the gods, has come—she in whom these many forms with smooth backs reside. Rejoicing with her at our common feasts, may we be masters of riches.
Those ancestors who are equal and of one mind in the realm of Yama—for them let there be a world, *svadhā*, obeisance, and may the sacrifice be prepared among the gods.
Those living beings who are equal and of one mind among the living, who belong to me—may their prosperity be ordained for me in this world for a hundred years.
I have heard of two paths for the fathers—those of the gods and those of mortals. Along these two, all this that moves comes together, whatever lies between the father and the mother.

May this oblation be productive for me, with ten heroic sons and a complete retinue, for my well-being. May it grant me self, progeny, cattle, the world, and fearlessness. May Agni make my offspring abundant; bestow food, milk, and seed upon us.
May the lower, the higher, and the middle Soma-loving Fathers arise—those who have gone to the life-breath, who are harmless and knowers of the *ṛta*; may those Fathers protect us in our invocations.

The Aṅgirases are our fathers, the Navagvas, the Atharvans, and the Bhṛgus, who are worthy of the Soma; may we abide in the good-will of those worthy of sacrifice, and likewise in their auspicious favor.
Our ancient fathers, worthy of Soma, the Vasiṣṭhas who followed after the drinking of Soma—with them may Yama, rejoicing, desiring the offerings, eat at his pleasure along with those who desire him.
