O Soma, you are preeminent in wisdom; you lead us along the straightest path. Under your guidance, O Indu, our wise fathers obtained their share of treasure among the gods.

For our ancient fathers, O Soma, performed their sacred rites for you, O Pavamāna, as wise ones. Winning [the prize], unassailed, open up the enclosures; be a liberal patron to us with heroes and horses.
O Soma, being in harmony with the ancestors, you have extended yourself across heaven and earth. To you, O Indu, we pay homage with this oblation; may we become masters of riches.

O Fathers who sit upon the sacrificial grass, come hither with your aid; we have prepared these oblations for you, so please accept them. Come to us with most gracious protection, and then bestow upon us well-being, health, and freedom from harm.

I have found the benevolent fathers, and the descendant, and the wide stride of Viṣṇu. Those who sit upon the sacrificial grass and partake of the pressed food with their own portion—may they be the most frequent visitors here.
The Soma-loving ancestors have been invited to their dear offerings placed upon the sacred grass; may they come, may they hear us here, may they speak for us, and may they protect us.
May the Soma-loving Fathers, consumed by the fire, come to us by the paths traveled by the gods; rejoicing with the *svadhā* offering at this sacrifice, may they speak for us and protect us.
O Agniṣvātta Pitṛs, come here; sit each in his proper seat, O excellent leaders. Eat the oblations presented upon the sacred grass, and then bestow wealth consisting of all heroic sons.

Those who are consumed by fire and those who are not consumed by fire, who rejoice in the midst of heaven through their own inherent power (*svadhā*), for them Svarāj shall fashion this life-force (*asunīti*) and this body according to his will.

We invoke the Agniṣvātta ancestors who observe the seasons, who have attained the Soma-drink through the Nārāśaṃsa verses; may those wise ones be favorable to us when invoked, and may we be masters of riches.

Sitting down to the south, with knees bent, may you all, O Viśvedevas, favor this sacrifice. Do not harm us, O Fathers, for anything whatsoever; whatever offense we may have committed against you through our human nature.
Seated in the lap of the ruddy ones, bestow wealth upon the mortal who offers oblations; O Fathers, grant a portion of that treasure to his sons, and bestow vigor upon them here.
O Agni, carrier of the *kavyas*, whatever wealth you yourself deem worthy, cause that to be celebrated among the gods through our songs as a glorious companion for us.
The Agni who is the bearer of the *kavya* offerings, may he worship the ancestors who increase the cosmic order; may he announce the oblations to both the gods and the ancestors.

O Agni, being praised as the bearer of the *kavyas*, you have carried the oblations, having made them fragrant; you have presented them to the fathers, and they have eaten them with the *svadhā* call. Eat, O God, these offered oblations.

Those ancestors who are here and those who are not here, those whom we know and those whom we do not know—you know how many they are, O Jātavedas; accept this well-performed sacrifice with the *svadhā* offerings.
Let this homage be paid today to the fathers—those who went before and those who followed after, those who have settled in the earthly realm, or those who are now among the well-fortified clans.
And so, O Agni, as our ancient fathers of old, aspiring toward *ṛta*, went toward the pure light, chanting their hymns; cleaving the earth, they uncovered the ruddy dawns.
Desiring you, we set you down; desiring you, we kindle you. Desiring them, bring the desiring ancestors here to eat the oblation.
With the foam of the waters, O Indra, you struck off the head of Namuci, when you conquered all rival hosts.

King Soma, the pressed nectar, has abandoned death by means of the *ṛjīṣa*. Through the Cosmic Order (*ṛta*), he attained truth, sensory power, the drinking-vessel, and the bright juice. This milk of the plant is the sensory power of Indra, the nectar, the honey.

The curlew of the Aṅgirasas drank the milk from the waters by means of his inspired thought. By the Eternal Law, he drank the truth, the power of Indra, the bright draught of the soma-juice—this milk, the immortal honey, which is the very power of Indra.

The swan dwelling in the pure realm drank the Soma from the waters with a sacred verse. By means of cosmic order, he drank the truth, the sensory power, the bright draught of the plant; this is Indra’s sensory power, the milk, the nectar, the honey.

From food he drew forth the essence; with the sacred word (*brahman*), Prajāpati drank the ruling power (*kṣatra*), the milk, and the Soma. Through cosmic order (*ṛta*) comes truth, the sensory power, the drink, the bright juice of the plant—this milk, the immortal honey, is the very sense-power of Indra.
Entering the womb, he casts off semen and urine; the embryo, enveloped by the fetal membrane, casts off the outer membrane at birth.
By means of the cosmic order (ṛta), truth, power, the digestive fire, the bright essence of the soma-plant, this milk—the power of Indra, the immortal nectar—is prepared.
Having observed forms, Prajāpati distinguished between truth and falsehood; Prajāpati placed lack of faith in falsehood and faith in truth.
By means of Cosmic Order comes Truth, the potent power, the ripening, the bright essence of the plant-juice; this is Indra’s vital power, the milk, the nectar, the honey.
By means of the Veda, Prajāpati drank apart from form; he drank both the pressed and the unpressed.
By means of cosmic order, truth, and sensory power, this is the digestive draught, the bright essence of the soma-plant; it is Indra’s vital power, this milk, the nectar, the honey.
Having seen the flowing essence, Prajāpati drank the bright with the bright—the milk, the Soma.
By means of cosmic order comes truth, the power of the senses, the digestion of the food, the bright essence—this milk, the immortal honey, is the very power of Indra.
With lead as the warp, with the mind of the wise as the loom, the seers weave with woolen thread; the Aśvins, Savitṛ, and Sarasvatī fashion the sacrifice, while Varuṇa heals the form of Indra.

The three deities, acting in harmony through their powers, bestowed that immortal form upon him: his body hairs became like young grass, his hair like sprouts in many ways, and his skin and flesh became like parched grain.

Then the Aśvins, the physicians whose path is red, and Sarasvatī weave a beautiful form within; they place bone and marrow with the *māsara* mixture through the *kārotara* filter, upon the skin of cows.
Sarasvatī weaves with her mind a skillful treasure for the two Nāsatyas—a body beautiful to behold; like a red juice from fermented liquor, the wise one has fashioned it as a shuttle upon a loom.

Through milk they produce semen, the immortal generative power; through Sura they produce seed from urine. Driving away ignorance and ill-will, they cast far away the undigested food, the wind, and all that is foul.

Indra the Good Protector has generated truth with his heart; Savitṛ has produced it with the sacrificial cake. Varuṇa, acting as a physician, heals the liver and the lungs; he does not diminish the gall-bladder and the kidneys, nor the bile, by means of the Vāyavya oblations.

The entrails are the cauldrons overflowing with honey; the intestines are the vessels like a well-milking cow. The spleen, by its powers, is like the wing of a hawk; the navel is the throne-seat, and the belly is like a mother.

The jar is the rectum, the progenitor by his powers, in which, at the beginning, the embryo was within the womb; the bladder is manifest as a fountain with a hundred streams, and like a jar it yields the *svadhā*-offering for the fathers.

The mouth is his face; truth is his head; by truth the tongue is the filter; the Aśvins and Sarasvatī are its lips. The bladder is his anus; the physician is his tail; the testicles are his penis, swift with heat.

From the two Aśvins, the eye; from the two cups, the nectar; from the goat, brilliance; and from the cooked oblation—eyelashes fashioned with wheat and jujube fruits—they clothe themselves in white and black, like a garment of beauty.

Like a ram upon its nose for heroic power, the immortal path of breath is formed by the two cups; Sarasvatī, with her invocations, has generated the diffused breath (*vyāna*), the nasal passages, the sacrificial grass, and the jujube fruits.

The bull is the form of Indra for the sake of strength; from his two ears comes immortal hearing. His mane is like barley upon the head; from his mouth was born the honey of the bees, as sweet as the jujube fruit.

There is no hair on the wolf’s body nor on its lap; there is no beard on its face, nor the fur of a tiger. There are no hairs on its head for glory, but the tuft of hair is for splendor; it possesses the fur of a lion, brilliance, and sensory powers.

The Aśvins, as physicians, restored the limbs to the self; Sarasvatī joined the self together with the limbs. Assuming the form of Indra, a hundredfold lifespan, and immortal light through the moon, they established [him].
Sarasvatī, the consort, bears within her womb the well-fashioned embryo for the Aśvins; Varuṇa, the king in the waters, generates Indra for glory with the essence of the waters and with the Sāman.

The luster of cattle, the potent oblation, the foaming liquor with milk, the honey of the bees—this immortal Soma-drop has been milked by the two physicians, the Aśvins, and by Sarasvatī, for both the pressed and the unpressed.
You are the womb of the kṣatra; you are the navel of the kṣatra. May it not harm you; may you not harm me.
Varuṇa, whose vow is truth and who is wise in will, has sat down in his dwellings for the sake of sovereign rule.
Protect me from death; protect me from ignorance.

At the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins, with the hands of Pūṣan—I sprinkle you for splendor and Vedic luster with the healing power of the Aśvins; I sprinkle you for heroism, for the eating of food, with the healing power of Sarasvatī; I sprinkle you for strength, for prosperity, and for glory with the sensory power of Indra.
Who are you? Which one are you? For what purpose are you? For whom are you? O you of beautiful renown, O auspicious one, O king of truth!
My head is glory, my face is fame; my hair and beard are splendor. My breath is the King, my sight is the Immortal, my hearing is the Sovereign.
My tongue is auspiciousness, my speech is greatness, my mind is fury, and my wrath is self-ruling splendor; my joys and delights are my fingers, my limbs are my allies, and my power is my friend.
My arms are strength and power; my hands are action and vigor; my chest is the self and the ruling power.
My ribs are the kingdom; my belly, shoulders, neck, and hips; my thighs, forearms, and knees are the subjects; and all my limbs are the people on every side.

My navel is consciousness; my mind is the anus, the seat of honor. My testicles are joy and delight; my generative organ is fortune and prosperity. Through my shanks and feet, I am Dharma, established as the king of the people.

I establish myself in the ruling power, I establish myself in the kingdom; I establish myself in the horses, I establish myself in the cattle; I establish myself in the limbs, I establish myself in the self; I establish myself in the vital breaths, I establish myself in the ruling power, I establish myself in prosperity; I establish myself in heaven and earth.
The three groups of gods, the eleven, and the thirty-three, the bounteous ones, with Bṛhaspati as their domestic priest, at the impulse of the god Savitṛ—may the gods protect me along with the gods.

May the first [verses] by means of the second, the second by the third, the third by Truth, Truth by Sacrifice, Sacrifice by the Yajus-formulas, the Yajus-formulas by the Sāmans, the Sāmans by the Ṛcs, the Ṛcs by the Puronuvākyās, the Puronuvākyās by the Yājyās, the Yājyās by the Vaṣaṭ-calls, and the Vaṣaṭ-calls by the oblations—may these fulfill my desires! Bhūḥ Svāhā!
The body hairs are my exertion; the skin is my bending, my coming hither; the flesh is my approaching; the wealth is my bone; the marrow is my bowing.
O gods, whatever offense against the gods we have committed, O deities, may Agni release me from that sin and from all distress.
Whether by day or by night we have committed sins, may Vāyu release me from that sin and from all distress.
Whether we have committed these sins while awake or while dreaming, may Sūrya release me from that sin and from all distress.

Whatever sin we have committed in the village, whatever in the forest, whatever in the assembly, whatever in the senses; whatever toward a Śūdra, whatever toward an Ārya, whatever sin we have committed under the law of a single person—of that, you are the expiation.

When we swear by the waters, by the inviolable ones, or by Varuṇa, from that, O Varuṇa, release us. O Avabhṛtha, O Nicumpuṇa, you are the gliding one, the Nicumpuṇa. Through the gods, cleanse away the sin committed against the gods; through mortals, cleanse away the sin committed against mortals. O God, protect us from the harm of the far-reaching enemy.

In the ocean is your heart, within the waters; may the plants and the waters enter into you together. May the waters and the plants be friendly toward us; may they be unfriendly to him who hates us and whom we hate.
Like one released from a trap, like one who has sweated and bathed free from dirt, like clarified butter purified by a strainer—may the waters cleanse me from mental sin.
Beholding the higher light beyond the darkness, we have gone from the gods to the god Sūrya, the supreme light.
I have followed after the waters today; we have united with their essence. O Agni, rich in milk, I have come hither; endow me with splendor, with progeny, and with wealth.

You are fuel; may we prosper. You are kindling; you are splendor; bestow splendor upon me. The earth turns together, as do Dawn and Sūrya, and this entire living world. May I become the light of Vaiśvānara; may I attain manifold desires. Bhūḥ! Svāhā!
I place the fuel-stick upon you, O Agni, Lord of Vows; I undertake both the vow and faith; consecrated, I kindle you.
May I attain that holy world where Brahman and Kshatra move together in harmony, where the gods dwell along with Agni.
May I know that holy world where Indra and Vāyu move together in harmony, where there is no more exhaustion.
Let joint be joined with joint by you, and limb with limb; may your fragrance protect the Soma, and your unshakable sap for exhilaration.
They pour it out, they sprinkle all around, they pour it up, and they purify it; for the sake of the intoxication of the tawny *surā*, one says "what? and another says "what?"
O Indra, at dawn, accept our offering accompanied by parched grain, groats, and cakes, and attended by hymns of praise.
Sing forth a great song for Indra, O Maruts, the most effective slayer of Vṛtra, by whom the upholders of Ṛta generated light—the god who is ever-watchful for the sake of the gods.
O Adhvaryu, bring the Soma pressed with stones onto the filter; purify it for Indra to drink.
He who is the lord of beings, upon whom the worlds are supported, he who rules over the great—by him I take hold of you; I take hold of you within me.

You are taken with a support: for the Aśvins you, for Sarasvatī you, for Indra you, the Good Protector. This is your resting place: for the Aśvins you, for Sarasvatī you, for Indra you, the Good Protector.

You are the protector of my out-breath and the protector of my in-breath; you are the protector of my sight and the protector of my hearing. You are the universal healer of my speech and the dissolver of my mind.
Of that which was prepared by the Aśvins, prepared by Sarasvatī, and prepared by Indra the good protector—invited, I partake of you who have been invited.
Kindled at the face of the dawns, O Indra, increasing through the preceding light, he of the thunderbolt-armed hands struck Vṛtra with the thirty-three gods; he threw open the doors.

The hero Narāśaṃsa, measuring out [the sacrifice], Tanūnapāt, who conforms to the station of the sacrifice—the wise one, rich in fatness, anointing himself with milk and honey, bright with gold, performs the sacrifice.

Praised by the gods, the one with bay horses, the helper, being invoked with the oblation and exulting; may he, the breaker of forts, the shatterer of cow-pens, whose arm wields the thunderbolt, come to our sacrifice, taking pleasure in it.

May Indra, the lord of the bay horses, taking pleasure in the sacrificial grass, sit down facing the east upon the earth’s appointed place—broad-expanding, spreading out the pleasant seat, in harmony with the Ādityas and the Vasus.

May the swift, hollowed doors, like wives with noble husbands, hasten toward Indra, the bull. May the divine doors open wide on all sides, stretching themselves forth with their greatness for the sake of the hero, so that we may possess heroic sons.

Dawn and Night, the lofty and vast, the milk-giving and well-yielding, weave together the extended thread with their beautiful form—the two radiant ones, worthy of sacrifice, honoring the divine Indra among the gods.

Measuring out divine ordinances for many men, the two first Hotṛ-priests of fair speech [the Aśvins] establish Indra at the head of the sacrifice; increasing the eastern light with the oblation, they sustain it with honey.

The three goddesses, increasing through the oblation and delighting Indra like wives with their husbands—Sarasvatī, the divine Iḍā, and Bhāratī who overcomes all—with their milk [maintain] the unbroken thread.

May Tvaṣṭṛ, the unboiled yet most brilliant one, bestowing strength upon Indra the bull for the sake of glory, anoint the many [oblations]—he, the bull of abundant seed, worshipping the bull, may he unite the gods at the head of the sacrifice.

The Lord of the Forest, released though not by snares, anointing himself by his own power like a divine immolator, filling Indra’s belly with oblations, shall sweeten the sacrifice with honey and clarified butter.
Toward the drop, Indra, the hero, acting like a bull, the conqueror of the swift, may the immortal gods, rejoicing with a mind that sprinkles clarity, delight in the Svāhā! The drops.

May Indra come to us for our protection; praised here, may the hero be our companion at the feast. May he, whose many powers have increased, nourish his sovereign dominion like the sky, so that it may be all-surpassing.

May Indra, the fierce lord of men with the thunderbolt in his arm, come to our aid from afar or from nearby to grant us protection; may he, the conqueror in battles, overcome those who attack us with his most powerful [helpers].

May Indra come toward us with his bay horses, turning hitherward for our protection and for bounty. May the wielder of the thunderbolt, the bounteous and exuberant one, stand by this sacrifice of ours in the struggle for booty.
Indra the protector, Indra the helper, the hero Indra who is easily invoked at every call—I invoke Śakra, Indra who is invoked by many; may the bounteous Indra bestow well-being upon us.

May Indra, the good protector, the possessor of wealth, with his aids, be gracious to us—he who possesses all knowledge. May he drive away our enemies and grant us fearlessness; may we be masters of heroic vigor.
May we abide in the favor of that worshipful one, and in his auspicious goodwill. May he, Indra, the good protector and the self-reliant, drive our enemies far away from us.
Come, O Indra, with your pleasant bay horses whose tails are like peacock feathers; let no one hold you back as fowlers catch a bird—pass them by like a traveler through the desert.
Thus do the Vasiṣṭhas praise with hymns Indra, the bull whose arm wields the thunderbolt; may he, being lauded, grant us wealth in heroes and cattle. Do you all protect us always with your blessings.
The fire is kindled, O Aśvins; the Gharma is heated; the Virāj has been pressed. Sarasvatī, the cow, milks out the bright Soma, the power of Indra, here.
When the soma is pressed, may both Aśvins, the physicians who protect the body, and Sarasvatī, carry the power of the senses for Indra along the paths through the regions of space.
For Indra, Sarasvatī and the two Aśvins, the physicians, have placed the Soma-drop with the Narāśaṃsa; they have established the honeyed medicine in the pressed juice.
Being invoked, Sarasvatī bestowed sensory powers and heroism upon Indra; with the *iḍā* offerings, the Aśvins bestowed nourishment, vigor, and wealth.
The Aśvins [took] the bright Soma pressed from Namuci by means of the *parisrut* liquor; Sarasvatī brought it upon the sacrificial grass for Indra to drink.
Like wide-opening doors for the Aśvins, like the quarters of space, Sarasvatī milks both worlds like Indra—she milks all desires.
Dawn and Night, the Aśvins, Indra by day, and Indra by night with his powers—being of one mind and well-adorned, they have anointed themselves together with Sarasvatī.
Protect us, O Aśvins, by day; protect us by night, O Sarasvatī! May the two divine Hotṛ-priests, the physicians, protect Indra together at the pressed soma.
The three goddesses—Sarasvatī, Bhāratī, and Iḷā—along with the Aśvins, have pressed the sharp, flowing Soma as a gladdening draught for Indra in three ways.
The Aśvins have bestowed upon us the honey-medicine; Sarasvatī has bestowed the medicine; and Indra, Tvaṣṭṛ, Yaśas, Śrī, and every form have been placed within the pressed juice.
In due season, Indra, the Lord of the Forest, exerts himself with the flowing liquor; Sarasvatī, the cow, milks out the mead, the Kīlāla, for the Aśvins.
O Aśvins, with the milk, with *māsara*, and with the foaming liquor, together with Sarasvatī, you two have mixed the pressed honey for Indra; *svāhā*!
The Aśvins and Sarasvatī, through their inspired wisdom, brought forth for Indra the oblation, the power of the senses, the bright wealth, and the bounty from the Asura Namuci.
The oblation with which the Aśvins and Sarasvatī strengthened Indra—he split Vala and the wealth [of the enemy] together with the Asura Namuci.
Both Aśvins together with Sarasvatī, bestowing that [strength] upon Indra, have celebrated him at the sacrifice with oblation and with powers.
May he who bestowed power upon Indra—Savitṛ, Varuṇa, and Bhaga—he the good protector, attend to the sacrificer, the lord of oblations.
Savitṛ and Varuṇa bestow wealth upon the sacrificing donor; Sutrāman has taken from Namuci the treasure, the strength, and the power of Indra.
Varuṇa [bestows] sovereignty, Savitṛ with Bhaga [bestows] sensory power and glory, and Sutrāman [bestows] strength with renown; bestowing these, they have attained the sacrifice.
With cows the Aśvins increased Indra’s sensory power; with horses, Sarasvatī increased the sacrificer’s manly vigor and strength; and with the oblation, they strengthened Indra.
O Nāsatyas, well-adorned, with golden paths, O Heroes, and you, Sarasvatī, rich in oblations—protect us in our sacred rites, O Indra!
She is the physician of skillful deeds; she is Sarasvatī, the one who yields abundance. She is the slayer of Vṛtra, the possessor of a hundred powers; they have bestowed vital strength upon Indra.
O Aśvins, you two, drinking the Surā together with the Asura Namuci, and Sarasvatī, aided Indra in his heroic deeds.

Like parents for their son, both Aśvins protected you, O Indra, with their poetic wisdoms and wondrous deeds; when you drank the exhilarating surā with your powers, Sarasvatī refreshed you, O Maghavan.

In whom horses, bulls, oxen, barren cows, and rams have been released and offered as oblations—to that Agni, the drinker of sweet nectar, whose back is sprinkled with Soma, the Ordainer—I generate a beautiful hymn from my heart.
The oblation has been poured into your mouth, O Agni, like ghee into the ladle, like Soma into the cup. Bestow upon us wealth that wins booty, rich in heroic sons, highly praised, glorious, and vast.
The Aśvins with splendor bestowed sight; Sarasvatī with breath, vigor; and Indra with speech and power, bestowed sensory capacity upon Indra.
O Nāsatyas, O Aśvins, come hither with cattle and with horses; O Rudras, protect us on our journey.
Neither the outsider nor the insider shall prevail against you, O possessors of abundant wealth; no malicious mortal enemy can overcome you.
O Aśvins, you who are worthy of praise, bring to us wealth of golden hue that finds wide space.
May Sarasvatī, the purifier, rich in spoils and possessing wealth through our inspired thought, desire our sacrifice.
Inciting true words, awakening gracious thoughts, Sarasvatī has established the sacrifice.
A great flood is Sarasvatī; she makes herself known by her signal. She shines forth over all inspired thoughts.
O Indra of wondrous luster, come hither; these pressed juices long for you, purified through the fine strainer.
O Indra, come, impelled by our prayer and urged by the sages, to the sacred formulations of the worshiper who has pressed the soma.
O Indra, Lord of the Bay Horses, come swiftly to our sacred hymns; bestow your favor upon us at this pressed juice.
May the Aśvins, in harmony with Sarasvatī, drink the honeyed mead; may Indra, the good protector and slayer of Vṛtra, enjoy the Soma-sweetness.
O Varuṇa, hear this my invocation; be gracious to me today! Seeking you, I long for you.
That I implore of you, worshipping with sacred prayer; that the sacrificer seeks from you with oblations. O Varuṇa, be present here without anger; O you of wide renown, do not steal away our life.
O Agni, you who know, may you ward off from us the wrath of the god Varuṇa; being the best of sacrificers, the most excellent bearer of oblations, and blazing brightly, release us from all enmities.
As such, O Agni, be our protector; be most near to us at the dawning of this morning. Being gracious, appease Varuṇa for us; seek out mercy, and be one who is easy for us to invoke.

We invoke for our protection the Earth, the mother of those who observe sacred vows, the consort of Cosmic Order—Aditi, the possessor of great dominion, the ageless, the far-reaching, the provider of excellent refuge, and the excellent guide.

May we ascend for our well-being upon the Sutrāman, the Earth, and the faultless Heaven; upon Aditi, the good refuge and the excellent guide; and upon the divine ship, well-oared, sinless, and leakless.
May I board a ship that is leakless, sinless, and equipped with a hundred oars, for my well-being.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, you of noble wisdom, sprinkle our pastures with clarified butter and the regions with honey.
Stretch forth your arms that we may live; sprinkle our pastures with clarified butter. O youthful ones, make us renowned among the people; hear these my invocations, O Mitra and Varuṇa.

May the Vājins be auspicious to us in our invocations during the service of the gods—those who run with measured pace, who possess beautiful voices; crushing the serpent, the wolf, and the demons, may they drive all diseases far away from us.

In every contest for booty, O swift steeds, protect us—you who are wise, immortal, and knowers of the Eternal Law. Drink of this honeyed mead and rejoice; satisfied, depart by the paths traveled by the gods.
The fire is kindled, well-kindled with fuel, most excellent; Gāyatrī as the meter, Indra-power, and the three-year-old steer have bestowed vital strength.
Tanūnapāt of pure vows, Tanūpā, and Sarasvatī; the Uṣṇih metre, Indra-power, and the Dityavāt bull have bestowed vital strength.
Agni, worthy of praise with *iḍā*-invocations, and the immortal god Soma; the *anuṣṭubh* metre, sensory power, the five-year-old cow, and vital strength—these have bestowed [their gifts].
Agni with fine sacrificial grass, accompanied by Pūṣan, the immortal one for whom the grass is strewn; the Bṛhatī metre, sensory power, and the three-year-old bull have bestowed vital strength.
The firm goddesses, the quarters, the great ones; the god Brahmā, Bṛhaspati; the Paṅkti metre, and the sense-power here—these have bestowed vigor upon the four-year-old bull.
The two young Uṣas, well-adorned, all the immortal gods, the Triṣṭubh metre, the sense-power, and the five-year-old bull have bestowed vital strength here.
The two divine Hotṛ-priests, the physicians, together with Indra as their companion, have bestowed the Jagatī metre, sensory power, the ox, and the cow as vital strength.

The three goddesses—Iḍā, Sarasvatī, and Bhāratī—the Maruts, and the Viśve-devas; the Virāj metre, sensory power, and the milch-cow: these have bestowed vital strength here, like a cow bestowing nourishment.
Tvaṣṭṛ, the swift and wonderful one, Indra, and Agni, the increasers of prosperity, have bestowed power through the two-footed metre; they have granted vigor like a bull or a cow.
May Vanaspati pacify us; may Savitṛ, impelling, bestow fortune. Kakubh meter, Indra-power, barren cow, and cow that miscarries—these have bestowed vitality.
Svāhā! May Varuṇa, the one of good dominion, make the sacrifice a healing medicine. Aticchandas, Bṛhat, the bull, and the cow have bestowed sensory power and vital vigor.
By the spring season, the gods, the Vasus, praised with the Trivṛt hymn, have placed the oblation and vital strength in Indra by means of the splendor of the Rathantara.
By the summer season, the gods, the Rudras, have been praised in the fifteenfold hymn; through the Bṛhat-sāman, glory, strength, the oblation, and vital energy have been bestowed upon Indra.

Praised with the Varṣā hymns, with the season, and with the seventeenfold Stoma, O Ādityas, you have, through the Vairūpa chant and with the vigor of the Viśve, bestowed life-sustaining oblation upon Indra.
By the autumn season, the gods, the twenty-one-fold Ṛbhus, have been praised; through the Vairāja chant and with splendor, they have bestowed splendor, oblation, and vital strength upon Indra.
By the winter season, the Maruts, the gods of the twenty-sevenfold [stoma], were praised; with strength and power, they placed the Śakvarī verses, vigor, and the oblation within Indra.
By the winter season, the thirty-three immortal gods have been praised; through truth, the Revatī verses have bestowed dominion, the oblation, and vital strength upon Indra.

Let the Hotṛ worship Agni with the kindling-stick in the place of Iḍā; let him worship the Aśvins, Indra, and Sarasvatī. As a smoky goat [is offered], so may there be healing medicine from wheat, jujube fruits, and young grass—honey, brilliance, sensory power, milk, Soma, foaming liquor, ghee, and honey. Let them enjoy the clarified butter; O Hotṛ, sacrifice!

Let the Hotṛ worship Tanūnapāt; let Sarasvatī [be worshipped]; let the ram and the ewe bring healing medicine by the honeyed path. To Indra, the Aśvins shall bring heroic vigor with jujubes and *upavākā* grains; with young sprouts, milk, Soma, foaming liquor, ghee, and honey—let them enjoy the clarified butter. O Hotṛ, sacrifice!

Let the Hotṛ worship Narāśaṃsa, who is like one not naked; let him worship the Lord with Sura as my medicine—let the ram be the physician, Sarasvatī the healer, and the omentum of the Aśvins like a chariot shining with moonlight. Let the fat of Indra’s heroism be offered with jujube fruits and Upavākā plants; let there be medicine with young sprouts, milk, Soma, foaming liquor, ghee, and honey. O Hotṛ, sacrifice the clarified butter; let them enjoy it! Hotar, perform the sacrifice!

Let the Hotṛ, impelled by Iḍā and being invoked, worship Sarasvatī, strengthening Indra with power through the bull—the sense-power of the cow—and for Indra’s medicine, the Aśvins [offer] honey with barley and jujubes, like *māsara* with parched grain, milk, Soma, foaming liquor, ghee, and honey; let them enjoy the clarified butter. O Hotṛ, sacrifice!

Let the Hotṛ worship the sacrificial grass, soft as wool; let the two Nāsatyas be the physicians, the Aśvins the physicians; let the mare with her foal be the physician, and Sarasvatī the cow who milks medicine for Indra—milk, Soma, fermented liquor, ghee, and honey. Let them enjoy the clarified butter; O Hotṛ, sacrifice!

Let the Hotṛ worship the Doors, the Quarters, wide-expanding like caverns; as the Doors, the Quarters, for the Aśvins; as Indra milked the two worlds, so let Sarasvatī, the Cow, yield medicine for the Aśvins and for Indra. Let the bright light, the power of Indra, the milk, the Soma, the foaming liquor, the ghee, and the honey enjoy [the offering]. O Hotṛ, sacrifice with the clarified butter!

Let the Hotṛ worship the well-adorned Dawn and Night; day and night, he anoints the Aśvins with Sarasvatī’s splendor and the healing power in Indra. Like a falcon through the atmosphere, with his heart, with beauty, like *māsara* and milk—may Soma, the flowing liquor, clarified butter, and honey enjoy the oblation of ghee; O Hotṛ, sacrifice!

Let the Hotṛ worship the two divine Hotṛs, the physicians Aśvins, who are watchful for Indra day and night with their remedies; let Sarasvatī, the physician, with lead, milk out strength, the power of Indra, milk, Soma, foaming liquor, ghee, and honey. Let them enjoy the clarified butter; O Hotṛ, sacrifice!

Let the Hotṛ worship the three goddesses for our medicine—the three who possess triple natures and are skillful in their forms. For Indra, let the golden form [of the milk] be yielded; for the Aśvins, Iḍā; and for Sarasvatī, let Bhāratī yield speech. For the great Indra, let them yield the power of Indra: Soma, the foaming liquor, ghee, and honey. Let them enjoy the clarified butter; O Hotṛ, sacrifice!

Let the Hotṛ worship Tvaṣṭṛ—the lord of the Surā-juice, the bull, the one of manly deeds—as well as Indra and the Aśvins; let him worship Sarasvatī for healing, as a call for vigor and Indra-power. Like a fierce wolf is the physician; glory is the medicine with the Surā. Like beauty is the *māsara* drink, the milk, Soma, the foaming liquor (*parisrut*), the clarified butter, and the honey. Let them enjoy the clarified butter; O Hotṛ, sacrifice!

Let the Hotṛ worship Vanaspati, the immolator, the Lord of a Hundred Powers, like a king who is terrible in his wrath, like a tiger; let the Aśvins with reverence, and Sarasvatī as physician, milk out for Indra their fury, their power, the milk, the Soma, the foaming liquor, the ghee, and the honey. Let them enjoy the clarified butter; O Hotṛ, sacrifice!

Let the Hotṛ worship Agni with Svāhā! With Svāhā for the drops of clarified butter; with Svāhā separately for the portions of fat; with Svāhā the goat for the Aśvins; with Svāhā the ram for Sarasvatī; with Svāhā the bull for Indra; with Svāhā the lion’s power for the sake of strength; with Svāhā Agni as the medicine; with Svāhā Soma as the power; with Svāhā Indra the Good Protector, Savitṛ, Varuṇa, and the Lord of Physicians; with Svāhā Vanaspati, the beloved, the path, the medicine; with Svāhā the gods who drink the clarified butter. May Agni, enjoying the medicine, milk, Soma, the foaming liquor, ghee, and honey, partake of the clarified butter; O Hotṛ, sacrifice!

Let the Hotṛ worship the Aśvins; may they enjoy the omentum and the fat of the goat; O Hotṛ, sacrifice the oblation! Let the Hotṛ worship Sarasvatī; may she enjoy the omentum and the fat of the ram; O Hotṛ, sacrifice the oblation! Let the Hotṛ worship Indra; may he enjoy the omentum and the fat of the bull; O Hotṛ, sacrifice the oblation!

Let the Hotṛ worship the Aśvins, Sarasvatī, and Indra the Good Protector. These Somas are well-blended with goats, rams, and bulls; they are pressed with young grass, sprouts, and parched grains—mighty intoxicants, refined with *māsara*, bright, milky, and immortal. They have been set forth for you, dripping with sweetness. May the Aśvins, Sarasvatī, and Indra the Good Protector, the slayer of Vṛtra, enjoy this Soma-sweetness; may they drink it and partake of it. O Hotṛ, sacrifice!

Let the Hotṛ worship the Aśvins; let them partake today of the goat-oblation. Let them consume from the midst the fat extracted, before the onset of hatred and before the seizure by men. Now, let them eat from the fodder of the wild plains, from the first-fruits of the pasture, from those well-flowing with milk, belonging to the hundred Rudras, consumed by Agni, clothed in fatness—from the ribs, from the haunches, from the shoulder-blades, from the marrow, and from every single limb, as they are portioned out. May the Aśvins indeed act thus; may they enjoy the oblation. O Hotṛ, sacrifice!

Let the Hotṛ worship Sarasvatī; let her partake today of the oblation of the ram—the fat extracted from its midst, before the onset of hatred, before the seizure by men. May she now eat of the fodder of the plains, the first-fruits of the pasture, well-flowing, belonging to the hundred Rudras, consumed by Agni, clothed in fatness—from the ribs, from the haunches, from the flanks, from the marrow, from every limb, portions cut out—may she prepare this; may Sarasvatī enjoy the oblation; O Hotṛ, sacrifice!

Let the Hotṛ worship Indra; let him cause the bull’s oblation to be eaten today, the fat extracted from the middle, before the onset of hatred and before the seizure by men. May he now eat from the fodder of the plains, the first-fruits of the meadow, well-flowing, belonging to the hundred Rudras, consumed by Agni, clothed in fat—cut from the flanks, from the hips, from the shoulders, from the haunches, and from every single limb. May Indra act thus; may he enjoy the oblation. O Hotṛ, sacrifice!

Let the Hotṛ worship Vanaspati, for he has bound [the victim] with a most finely ground and most powerful cord. Where are the beloved abodes of the oblation of the goat belonging to the Aśvins; where are the beloved abodes of the oblation of the ram belonging to Sarasvatī; where are the beloved abodes of the oblation of the bull belonging to Indra; where are the beloved abodes of Agni; where are the beloved abodes of Soma; where are the beloved abodes of Indra Sutraman; where are the beloved abodes of Savitṛ; where are the beloved abodes of Varuṇa; where are the beloved paths of Vanaspati; where are the beloved abodes of the gods who drink the clarified butter (ājyapāḥ); where are the beloved abodes of Agni the Hotṛ—there let him release these [victims], having praised them as it were, having extolled them as it were, having made them more powerful as it were; may the divine Vanaspati accept the oblation; O Hotṛ, sacrifice!

Let the Hotṛ worship Agni Sviṣṭakṛt. Agni has sacrificed to the dear abodes of the Aśvins’ goat-oblation; he has sacrificed to the dear abodes of Sarasvatī’s ram-oblation; he has sacrificed to the dear abodes of Indra’s bull-oblation; he has sacrificed to the dear abodes of Agni; he has sacrificed to the dear abodes of Soma; he has sacrificed to the dear abodes of Indra Sutraman; he has sacrificed to the dear abodes of Savitṛ; he has sacrificed to the dear abodes of Varuṇa; he has sacrificed to the dear paths of Vanaspati; he has sacrificed to the dear abodes of the gods who drink the clarified butter. Let him sacrifice to the dear abodes of Agni the Hotṛ; let him sacrifice to his own greatness. May he perform the sacrifice; may he prepare nourishment; may Jātavedas enjoy the oblations. O Hotṛ, sacrifice!

The divine *barhis*, Sarasvatī, the auspicious Indra, and the Aśvins—like brilliance, they have placed sight in the eyes and sensory power through the *barhis*. For the winning of wealth, for the granting of treasure, may they partake; sacrifice!

The divine Doors, the Aśvins the physicians, and Sarasvatī have placed vital breath and vigor in Indra’s nostrils; as the Doors, may they enjoy the distribution of wealth for the sake of gaining wealth. Sacrifice!

The goddesses Uṣas, the Aśvins, Sutrāman Indra, and Sarasvatī—may they place strength and speech in our mouth; through the two Dawns, may they bestow sensory power for the winning of wealth from the treasury of riches. May they enjoy the sacrifice! Yaja!

The two divine attendants, Sarasvatī, and the Aśvins have strengthened Indra. Like hearing in the ears, they have bestowed glory, the power of the senses, and the portion of the two attendants upon him. May they partake in the sacrifice for the winning of wealth from the treasury of wealth; perform the offering!

May the goddesses Ūrjāhutī and Sudughā yield their milk for Indra; may Sarasvatī and the two physicians, the Aśvins, protect him. Like pure light, place the power of Indra within his two breasts as the two oblations; for the winning of wealth and the granting of treasure, let them partake; sacrifice!

The gods among gods, the two physicians, Indra and the Aśvins, and Sarasvatī with their *vaṣaṭ*-cries have placed brilliance in the heart and mental power within the two priests, like sensory vigor. May they partake of the gift of wealth for the sake of the winning of wealth; sacrifice!

The three goddesses—the three goddesses Aśvinī, Iḍā, and Sarasvatī—have placed vigor and power within the middle of the navel for Indra, for the winning of wealth and the granting of riches. May they enjoy the sacrifice; perform the offering!

O God, Indra’s chariot, praised by men and provided with triple protection, moves along with Sarasvatī and the two Aśvins. Like seed, it is a form of immortal procreation; Tvaṣṭṛ has bestowed powers upon Indra. For the gain of wealth, may they partake of the gift of wealth; sacrifice!

The divine tree, with golden leaves, ripens its honey for Indra, for the Aśvins, and for Sarasvatī, with the gods as its companions; may it bear goodly fruit. Like vigor, like speed, like a bull’s fury, may the Lord of the Forest bestow upon us powers of the senses. In the winning of wealth, may they partake of the gift of treasure; perform the sacrifice!

The divine sacrificial grass of the waters, spread at the sacrifice for the Aśvins—soft as wool and pleasant for Sarasvatī—is your seat, O Indra. For the sake of sovereignty, they have established King Manyu upon the sacrificial grass as a source of power. For the winning of wealth and the granting of treasures, may they partake; perform the sacrifice!

May Agni Sviṣṭakṛt, the god, sacrifice to the gods in their proper order; may the two Hotṛ-priests, Indra, and the Aśvins [sacrifice]; may Vāc [sacrifice] to Vāc, Sarasvatī, Agni, and Soma. Well-sacrificed is Indra the Good Protector, Savitṛ, Varuṇa the Physician, and the god Vanaspati who has been sacrificed to. Well-sacrificed are the gods who drink the clarified butter. Well-sacrificed is Agni by means of Agni; may the Hotṛ-priest Sviṣṭakṛt bestow upon the office of the Hotṛ glory, sensory power, vigor, honor, and the Svadhā-call. May they partake of the gain of wealth from the treasury of wealth; sacrifice!

Today this sacrificer has chosen Agni as the Hotṛ; cooking cooked offerings, cooking sacrificial cakes, binding a goat for the Aśvins, a ram for Sarasvatī, and a bull for Indra; pressing Soma for the Aśvins, for Sarasvatī, and for Indra the Good Protector, and [preparing] surā-soma juices.

Today the divine Vanaspati has become well-established through the goat for the Aśvins, the ram for Sarasvatī, and the bull for Indra. He has accepted those [oblations] from the fat; may he cook them thoroughly. They have increased by means of the sacrificial cakes. The Aśvins, Sarasvatī, and Indra the Good Protector have drunk the pressed Soma and the Surā.

O seer, descendant of seers, grandson of seers, this sacrificer has chosen you today from among many who have assembled, thinking, "This one shall sacrifice for me among the gods for desirable wealth. Whatever divine gifts the gods have given, decree them for him and approve them; you, O Hotṛ, are impelled for the auspicious proclamation. Sent by man for the recitation of the hymns, speak the hymns.
Thou art luster, thou art seed, thou art the immortal, the protector of life; protect my life. On the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins, with the hands of Pūṣan, I take thee.
The sages grasped this rein of Cosmic Order in the ancient times during the sacrificial assemblies; she has come to us at this pressed juice, hastening toward the boundary of Cosmic Order.
Thou art speech, thou art the world, thou art the restrainer, thou art the sustainer; as such, go to Agni Vaiśvānara, the far-extending, consecrated by the cry of Svāhā!

Welcome to you for the gods and for Prajāpati, O Brahman; I shall bind the horse for the gods and for Prajāpati. May I prosper through him. Bind him for the gods and for Prajāpati; through him, may you prosper.

I sprinkle you, acceptable to Prajāpati. I sprinkle you, acceptable to Indra and Agni. I sprinkle you, acceptable to Vāyu. I sprinkle you, acceptable to the All-gods. I sprinkle you, acceptable to all the gods. Varuṇa strikes down the mortal man who seeks to kill the courser; even further off is the dog.
Svāhā to Agni! Svāhā to Soma! Svāhā to the joy of the waters! Svāhā to Savitṛ! Svāhā to Vāyu! Svāhā to Viṣṇu! Svāhā to Indra! Svāhā to Bṛhaspati! Svāhā to Mitra! Svāhā to Varuṇa!

Hail to the utterance *hiṅ*, hail to that which has uttered *hiṅ*; hail to the bellowing, hail to the one who bellows; hail to the snorting, hail to the one who snorts; hail to the scent, hail to the one who smells; hail to the settled, hail to the seated; hail to the bound, hail to the leaping; hail to the sitting, hail to the lying down; hail to the sleeping, hail to the waking; hail to the cooing, hail to the awakened; hail to the yawning, hail to the one who has yawned; hail to the contracting, hail to the one who has contracted; hail to the approaching, hail to the one who has approached; hail to the departing, hail to the one who has departed.

Hail to him as he exerts himself! Hail to him as he runs! Hail to him as he hastens away! Hail to him as he has hastened away! Hail to him as he snorts! Hail to him as he has snorted! Hail to him as he sits down! Hail to him as he stands up! Hail to speed! Hail to strength! Hail to him as he turns about! Hail to him as he has turned about! Hail to him as he shakes himself! Hail to him as he has shaken himself! Hail to him as he listens! Hail to him as he hears! Hail to him as he looks! Hail to him as he has looked! Hail to him as he gazes! Hail to the blinking! Hail to that which he eats! Hail to that which he drinks! Hail to that which he voids as urine! Hail to him as he acts! Hail to him as he has acted! Hail! Hail!
We meditate upon that most excellent splendor of the divine Savitṛ; may he impel our thoughts.
I invoke Savitṛ, the golden-handed, for aid; he, the god, knows the place.
We invoke the great favor of the conscious god Savitṛ, whose bounty is true.
We implore the favor of Savitṛ, who increases our good thoughts, with a well-fashioned hymn; [we pray] to the god who understands the mind.
At dawn, I invoke the great Savitṛ, the lord of the virtuous, the impeller, for the feast of the gods.
With our intellect, we meditate upon the thought of the god Savitṛ, the impeller, who belongs to all the gods; we contemplate Bhaga.
Awaken Agni with a hymn of praise, enkindling the immortal one, so that he may place our oblations among the gods.
He, the immortal bearer of oblations, the eager messenger, well-disposed—Agni brings all things together through our prayer.
I place Agni at the forefront as my messenger; I address him, the bearer of oblations, so that he may seat the gods here.
For you, O Pavamāna, have generated the sun; by your power, you have established the milk in its expanse, hastening with the wisdom that quickens the kine.

Abundant with thy mother, powerful with thy father; thou art a horse, thou art a steed, thou art a racer, thou art a joy-giver, thou art a courser, thou art a swift runner, thou art a prize-winner, thou art a bull, thou art manly-minded. "Yayu" is thy name; "Śiśu" is thy name. Follow the flight of the Ādityas.

O gods, guardians of the quarters, protect this horse sprinkled for the sacrifice for the gods! May there be delight here; may it find pleasure here! May there be steadfastness here; may there be self-steadfastness here! Svāhā!

To the body, svāhā! To whom, svāhā! To which one, svāhā! Svāhā to the one who has meditated upon the meditation! Svāhā to Prajāpati as the mind! Svāhā to the one who perceives as the intellect, to Aditi, svāhā! To Aditi the Great, svāhā! To Aditi the Compassionate, svāhā! To Sarasvatī, svāhā! To Sarasvatī the Purifying, svāhā! To Sarasvatī the Vast, svāhā! To Pūṣan, svāhā! To Pūṣan the Guide on the Path, svāhā! To Pūṣan the Protector of Men, svāhā! To Tvaṣṭṛ, svāhā! To Tvaṣṭṛ the Shedder of Seed, svāhā! To Tvaṣṭṛ of Many Forms, svāhā! To Viṣṇu, svāhā! To Viṣṇu the Abiding One, svāhā! To Viṣṇu Śipiviṣṭa, svāhā!
May every mortal choose the friendship of the divine leader; everyone strives for wealth, may he choose glory so that he may prosper—svāhā!

O Brahman, may a Brāhmaṇa endowed with Vedic splendor be born; in this kingdom, may a Kṣatriya be born who is a hero, skilled in archery, a piercer of the foe, and a great chariot-warrior. May there be a cow that yields milk, a draft-ox that carries the load, a swift steed, a wife of noble character, and a victorious warrior standing in the chariot—may a youthful hero be born to this sacrificer, fit for the assembly. May Parjanya rain for us according to our desire; may our plants ripen with fruit; may our security and prosperity be well-provided.
Hail to the out-breath, hail to the in-breath, hail to the diffused breath, hail to the eye, hail to the ear, hail to speech, hail to the mind!

Hail to the eastern direction, hail to the intermediate direction; hail to the southern direction, hail to the intermediate direction; hail to the western direction, hail to the intermediate direction; hail to the northern direction, hail to the intermediate direction; hail to the upward direction, hail to the intermediate direction; hail to the downward direction, hail to the intermediate direction; hail to the intermediate direction, hail to the intermediate direction.

Hail to the waters! Hail to the floods! Hail to the water! Hail to those that stand still! Hail to those that flow! Hail to those that stream! Hail to those in wells! Hail to those in ponds! Hail to those that are held! Hail to the river! Hail to the ocean! Hail to the lake! Hail!

Hail to the wind! Hail to the smoke! Hail to the cloud! Hail to the rain-cloud! Hail to the lightning! Hail to the thundering! Hail to the crashing! Hail to the raining! Hail to the ceasing from rain! Hail to the rising rain! Hail to the swift rain! Hail to the gathering [clouds]! Hail to that which has gathered! Hail to the sprinkling! Hail to the misting! Hail to the drops! Hail to the hailstones! Hail to the frost! Hail!

Svāhā to Agni! Svāhā to Soma! Svāhā to Indra! Svāhā to the Earth! Svāhā to the Atmosphere! Svāhā to the Sky! Svāhā to the Quarters! Svāhā to the Intermediate Directions! Svāhā to the upward direction! Svāhā to the downward direction! Svāhā!

Hail to the constellations! Hail to those belonging to the constellations! Hail to day and night! Hail to the half-months! Hail to the months! Hail to the seasons! Hail to the seasonal periods! Hail to the year! Hail to Heaven and Earth! Hail to the Moon! Hail to the Sun! Hail to the rays! Hail to the Vasus! Hail to the Rudras! Hail to the Ādityas! Hail to the Maruts! Hail to the All-gods! Hail to the roots! Hail to the branches! Hail to the trees! Hail to the flowers! Hail to the fruits! Hail to the medicinal herbs! Hail!

Svāhā to the earth! Svāhā to the intermediate space! Svāhā to the sky! Svāhā to the sun! Svāhā to the moon! Svāhā to the stars! Svāhā to the waters! Svāhā to the plants! Svāhā to the trees! Svāhā to the floating beings! Svāhā to the moving and unmoving! Svāhā to the reptiles!

Hail to Asu, hail to Vasu, hail to Vibhu, hail to Vivasvat, hail to Gaṇaśrī, hail to Gaṇapati, hail to Abhibhū, hail to Adhipati, hail to Śūṣa, hail to Saṃsarpa, hail to Candra, hail to Jyotis, hail to Malimluca, hail to Divāpat!

Hail to Madhu, hail to Mādhava; hail to Śukra, hail to Śuci; hail to Nabhas, hail to Nabhasya; hail to Iṣa, hail to Ūrja; hail to Sahas, hail to Sahasya; hail to Tapas, hail to Tapasya; hail to Aṃhasaspati!

Hail to strength! Hail to impulsion! Hail to the after-born! Hail to will-power! Hail to heaven! Hail to the head! Hail to the pervasive one! Hail to the final one! Hail to the final one of the world! Hail to the Lord of the World! Hail to the Overlord! Hail to Prajāpati! Hail!

May life be perfected through sacrifice, Svāhā! May breath be perfected through sacrifice, Svāhā! May out-breath be perfected through sacrifice, Svāhā! May diffused breath be perfected through sacrifice, Svāhā! May up-breath be perfected through sacrifice, Svāhā! May middle breath be perfected through sacrifice, Svāhā! May sight be perfected through sacrifice, Svāhā! May hearing be perfected through sacrifice, Svāhā! May speech be perfected through sacrifice, Svāhā! May mind be perfected through sacrifice, Svāhā! May the self be perfected through sacrifice, Svāhā! May the Brahman be perfected through sacrifice, Svāhā! May light be perfected through sacrifice, Svāhā! May heaven be perfected through sacrifice, Svāhā! May the back be perfected through sacrifice, Svāhā! May sacrifice itself be perfected through sacrifice, Svāhā!
Hail to one! Hail to two! Hail to a hundred! Hail to one hundred and one! Hail to the dawning! Hail to heaven!
In the beginning, Hiraṇyagarbha arose; once born, he was the sole lord of all that exists. He supported this earth and yonder sky. To what god shall we offer worship with our oblation?

You are taken with a support; I take you, acceptable to Prajāpati. This is your womb; the sun is your greatness. That greatness of yours which was manifested in the day and in the year, that greatness of yours which was manifested in Vāyu and in the intermediate space, that greatness of yours which was manifested in the sky and in the sun—to that greatness of yours, to Prajāpati, Svāhā! To the gods!
He who by his greatness alone became the sole king of the breathing and blinking world; he who rules over these bipeds and quadrupeds—to what god shall we offer worship with our oblation?

You are taken with a support; I take you, acceptable to Prajāpati. This is your womb; the moon is your greatness. That greatness of yours which was manifested in the night, in the year, on the earth, in Agni, and in the stars, in the moon—to that greatness of yours, to Prajāpati, to the gods, *svāhā*!
They harness the ruddy, bright one as he moves; those who stand around him behold him. The luminous realms shine in heaven.
They yoke his two beloved bay horses to the chariot on either side—red, bold, and daring conquerors of men.
Or when the wind has gone to the waters, to Indra’s beloved body—O singer of praise, by this path bring back that horse of ours to us again.

May the Vasus anoint you with the Gāyatrī metre; may the Rudras anoint you with the Triṣṭubh metre; may the Ādityas anoint you with the Jagatī metre. Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O gods, eat this food—the parched grains, the fried grains, the barley, and the milk-products. O Prajāpati, eat this food!
Who indeed wanders alone? Who indeed is born again? What is the remedy for the cold? And what is the great sowing ground?
The sun moves alone; the moon is born again; fire is the remedy for cold; the earth is the great vessel for sowing.
What was Pūrvacitti? What was the great bird? What was Pilippilā? What was Piśaṅgilā?
The sky was the first thought; the horse was the great vital power. The sheep was the slippery one; the night was the reddish-brown one.

May Vāyu protect you with cooked offerings; Asitagrīva with goats; Nyagrodha with chalices; Śalmali with prosperity. This stallion, fit for the chariot, has come hither on four feet. May Brahmā and Kṛṣṇa protect us. Homage to Agni!
Sharpened by the rein is the chariot; sharpened by the rein is the horse. Sharpened in the waters is the water-born Brahman, who has Soma as his leader.
O Horse, fashion your body yourself; sacrifice yourself; enjoy [the offering] yourself. Your greatness cannot be attained by another.
Verily, you do not die here, nor do you suffer harm; you go to the gods by easy paths, where the doers of good deeds dwell, where they have gone—there may the god Savitṛ establish you.

Agni was the sacrificial animal; with him they sacrificed, and he won this world in which Agni dwells. That world shall be yours; you will conquer it; drink these waters! Vāyu was the sacrificial animal; with him they sacrificed, and he won this world in which Vāyu dwells. That world shall be yours; you will conquer it; drink these waters! Sūrya was the sacrificial animal; with him they sacrificed, and he won this world in which Sūrya dwells. That world shall be yours; you will conquer it; drink these waters!
Hail to the out-breath! Hail to the in-breath! Hail to the diffused breath! O Ambā, O Ambikā, O Ambālikā, no one leads me away; the little horse sleeps with Subhadrā, the inhabitant of Kāmpīla.

We invoke you, the Lord of hosts, among the hosts; we invoke you, the Lord of the beloved, among the beloved; we invoke you, the Lord of treasures, among the treasures, O Vasu, my own. I have become the one who impregnates the womb; may you become the one who impregnates the womb.
May we both extend our four feet together; may you two clothe yourselves in the heavenly world. May the vigorous, potent stallion, the bestower of seed, deposit the seed.
Lift up her thighs and place the vulva below; O bull, cause the ointment to flow, you who are the living prey of women.
The two little birds, *yakāsakau*, flee with a *śakuntikāhalag* cry; they strike at the womb, and the fetters rattle.
The little bird that flies away with a "āhalag" sound—O Adhvaryu, your mouth seems as if it wishes to speak; do not address us.
Your mother and your father climb to the top of a tree; "I am winning," your father says, as he thrusts his fist into the womb.
Your mother and your father once played at the foot of a tree; O Brahmin, your face appears as if you wish to speak—do not speak too much to us.
Raise her up, as one carrying a load upon a mountain; then let her waist swell, like one purifying herself when the wind is cold.
Raise him upward, as one carrying a burden up a mountain; then let his middle part quiver, like one purifying himself in the cold wind.
That which has settled upon her, this breaker of distress—the short yet thick [organ]—her two testicles throb like two small fish in a cow's hoof-print.
When the gods revealed the limp, distorted thing, the woman points with her thigh, as one who has come into the sight of truth.
When the deer eats barley, it does not consider the fodder to be nourishment; when a Śūdra woman has an Aryan lover, she does not desire wealth for the sake of sustenance.
As the deer eats barley, it does not think much of its own nourishment; as a Śūdra is a lover to an Ārya woman, he does not care for his own prosperity.
I have celebrated Dadhikrāvan, the victorious, the spirited horse; may he make our mouths fragrant and may he prolong our lives.
May Gāyatrī, Triṣṭubh, Jagatī, Anuṣṭubh, along with Paṅkti, Bṛhatī, Uṣṇihā, and Kakup, together with the needles, pacify you.
May those with two feet, those with four feet, those with three feet, and those with six feet—those that are without meter and those that have meter—pacify you with their needles.
May the Mahānāmnīs, the Revatīs, all the quarters that grant abundance, the voices of the clouds, and the lightnings with their needles pacify you.
Let the noble women, your wives, comb out the hair with their wisdom; let the wives of the gods, the quarters of space, smooth you with their needles.
The silver, the tawny, and the leaden ones are yoked as partners through their ritual acts; may the boundary-markers, bringing peace, bring peace upon the skin of the vigorous horse.
Surely, just as those who possess barley reap it in due order, separating it out, so do thou bring here the food of those who offer the homage of the sacrificial grass.
Who flays you? Who dissects you? Who carves your limbs? And who is your wise preparer?
May the Seasons, as the immolators, dissect you according to the seasons and the joints; may they prepare you with the splendor of the year and with the implements of the sacrifice.
May the half-months and the months, being prepared, cut your joints; may the Maruts, day and night, heal whatever is injured in you.
May the divine Adhvaryus cut you and divide you; may they prepare your limbs joint by joint, making them smooth as they perform the sacrifice.
May Heaven, Earth, the intermediate space, and Vāyu fill your opening; may the Sun, together with the constellations, prepare a world for you in a proper manner.
May there be well-being for your upper limbs, may there be well-being for your lower limbs; may there be well-being for your bones and marrow, and may there be well-being for your entire body.
Who indeed wanders alone? Who indeed is born again? What is the remedy for cold? And what is the great sowing ground?
The sun moves alone; the moon is born again. Fire is the remedy for cold; the earth is the great vessel for sowing.
What light is equal to the sun? What lake is equal to the ocean? What is greater than the earth? Of what is there no measure?
Brahman is a light equal to the sun; heaven is a lake equal to the ocean; Indra is vaster than the earth; but for a cow, no measure exists at all.
I ask you for knowledge, O friend of the gods, whether you have mentally reached those three steps of Viṣṇu in which he has entered the entire world.
I am also within those three steps in which the entire world has entered; in an instant, I traverse the earth and the sky, and with a single limb, I reach the back of this heaven.
Into what has the Person entered? What things within the Person are fixed? O Brahman, we address this riddle to you; what indeed will you answer us in this matter?
The Person entered within the five; they are fixed within the Person. Reflecting upon this here, I say to you: you are not superior to me through mere illusion.
What was the primordial thought? What was the great vital power? What was the slippery one? What was the devourer of flesh?
The sky was the first thought; the horse was the great vital power. The sheep was the slippery one; the night was the reddish-brown one.
Who is it that flows reddish-brown? Who is it that flows dark-red? Who is it that rushes leaping along? Who is it that creeps along the path?
The reddish goat, the porcupine, and the reddish hedgehog; the hare runs with a spring, and the snake glides along the path.

How many are its stations? How many syllables? How many oblations? In how many ways is it kindled? I ask you about the ordinances of the sacrifice here: how many Hotṛ-priests perform the sacrifice according to the seasons?
Six are its stations, a hundred its syllables, eighty its oblations, and three its fuel-sticks. I proclaim to you these ordinances of the sacrifice: seven priests worship according to the seasons.
Who knows the navel of this world? Who knows heaven, earth, and the intermediate space? Who knows the birthplace of the great sun? And who knows from whence the moon was born?
I know the navel of this world; I know heaven and earth and the intermediate space. I know the birthplace of the great Sun, and I know the Moon from which it was born.
I ask you about the furthest limit of the earth; I ask where the navel of the world is. I ask you about the seed of the stallion; I ask about the highest heaven of speech.

This is the altar, the furthest limit of the earth; this is the sacrifice where the navel of the world is found. This is the seed of the potent horse, this Soma; this is the Brahman, the supreme vault of speech.
Subhū, the self-existent, first in the great ocean, conceived the seasonal germ from which Prajāpati was born.
Let the Hotṛ worship Prajāpati through the greatness of Soma; let him enjoy it and drink the Soma—O Hotṛ, sacrifice!
O Prajāpati, none other than you has encompassed all these forms. Whatever desire we have as we offer this oblation to you, may that be ours.

The horse, the hornless goat, and the gayal—these are dedicated to Prajāpati. A black-necked animal for Agni is at the forehead; a ewe for Sarasvatī is below the jaw; two dark-bellied animals for the Aśvins are on the forelegs; a dark-grey animal for Soma and Pūṣan is at the navel; a white and a black animal for Sūrya and Yama are on the sides; two hairy-thighed animals for Tvaṣṭṛ are on the thighs; a white animal for Vāyu is on the tail; a barren cow for Indra is for his skillful work; and a dwarf bull for Viṣṇu.

The ruddy, the smoke-ruddy, and the jujube-ruddy—these belong to Soma; the tawny, the reddish-tawny, and the parrot-tawny—these belong to Varuṇa; the white-eared, the one with a white ear on one side, and the one with white ears all around—these belong to Savitṛ; the white-armed, the one with a white arm on one side, and the one with white arms all around—these belong to Bṛhaspati; the spotted, the small-spotted, and the large-spotted—these belong to Mitra and Varuṇa.

The Śuddhavāla, the Sarvaśuddhavāla, and the Maṇivāla belong to the Aśvins; the Śyeta, the Śyetākṣa, and the Aruṇa belong to Rudra Paśupati; the Karṇas belong to Yama; the Avaliptas belong to Rudra; and those with the color of the sky belong to Parjanya.

The speckled one, the cross-speckled, and the upward-speckled—these are for the Maruts. The pale, the red-wooled, and the spotted—these are for Sarasvatī. The spleen-eared, the snout-eared, and the liver-eared—these are for Tvaṣṭṛ. The black-necked, the white-flanked, and the marked-thighed—these are for Indra and Agni. The black-marked, the small-marked, and the large-marked—these are for Uṣas.

The *śilpā* cows are for the Viśvedevas; the ruddy ones (*rohiṇyaḥ*) are for Tryaruṇa; those of unknown origin are for Vāc; those of uniform color are for Aditi; the heifers (*vatsataryaḥ*) are for Dhātṛ; and [those] for the wives of the gods.

Those with black necks belong to Agni; those with white brows belong to the Vasus; the ruddy ones belong to the Rudras; the white, shining ones belong to the Ādityas; and those with the color of the sky belong to Parjanya.

The tall ones, the bulls, and the dwarfs are for Indra and Viṣṇu; the tall ones with white forelegs and white backs are for Indra and Bṛhaspati; those of the form of boars and the dappled ones are for Agni and the Maruts; and the dark ones are for Pūṣan.
These are for Indra and Agni; the two-colored ones are for Agni and Soma; the dwarf oxen are for Agni and Viṣṇu; the barren cows are for Mitra and Varuṇa; and the piebald cows are for Mitra.

Those with black necks are for Agni; the brown ones are for Soma; the white ones are for Vāyu; those of unknown color are for Aditi; those of uniform appearance are for Dhātṛ; and the heifers are for the wives of the gods.
The black ones are terrestrial, the smoky ones are atmospheric, the vast ones are celestial, the variegated ones are lightning-born, and the speckled ones are stellar.
He obtains smoke-colored [animals] for Spring, white ones for Summer, black ones for the Rainy season, ruddy ones for Autumn, spotted ones for Winter, and tawny ones for the Cool season.
Three-year-old oxen for the Gāyatrī; five-year-old oxen for the Triṣṭubh; two-year-old oxen for the Jagatī; three-year-old heifers for the Anuṣṭubh; four-year-old oxen for the Uṣṇih.
The draft-oxen are for the Virāj; the bulls are for the Bṛhatī; the stallions are for the Kakubh; the oxen are for the Paṅkti; the milch-cows are for the Aticchandas.

Those with black necks are for Agni; the tawny ones are for Soma; the dappled ones are for Savitṛ; the heifers are for Sarasvatī; the dark ones are for Pūṣan; the speckled ones are for the Maruts; those of many colors are for the Viśvedevas; and the barren cows are for Heaven and Earth.
These have been described as the transference animals: the black ones for Indra and Agni, the speckled ones for Varuṇa, the spotted ones for the Maruts, and the hornless ones for Ka.

He sacrifices first-born animals to Agni Anīkavat; *savātya* animals to the Maruts Sāṃtapanas; *baṣkihā* animals to the Maruts Gṛhamedhins; *saṃsṛṣṭa* animals to the Maruts Krīḍins; and *anusṛṣṭa* animals to the Maruts Svatavantas.
These have been described as the *saṃcaras*: those with horns facing forward are for Indra and Agni; those with many forms are for Mahendra; and those for Viśvakarman.

Smoke-colored, tawny-looking [grains] are for the Soma-drinking ancestors; tawny, tawny-looking [grains] are for the Barhiṣad ancestors; black, tawny-looking [grains] are for the Agniṣvātta ancestors; and black, speckled [grains] are for the Tryambaka deities.
These transference offerings have been described: those for Śuna and Sīra, those for Vāyu, and those for Sūrya, all consisting of white animals.

For Spring he offers *kapiñjala* partridges; for Summer, *kalaviṅka* sparrows; for the Rainy Season, *tittiri* partridges; for Autumn, *vartikā* quails; for Winter, *kakara* pheasants; and for the Cool Season, *vikakara* pheasants.
For the Ocean he obtains crocodiles; for Parjanya, frogs; for the Waters, fish; for Mitra, kulīpaya fish; and for Varuṇa, water-monsters.
He sacrifices swans to Soma, crane-birds to Vāyu, curlews to Indra and Agni, water-fowl to Mitra, and ruddy geese to Varuṇa.
One sacrifices *kuṭaru* birds to Agni; owls to the Vanaspatis; blue jays to Agni and Soma; peacocks to the Aśvins; and pigeons to Mitra and Varuṇa.
One sacrifices *laba* birds to Soma, *kaulīka* birds to Tvaṣṭṛ, *goṣādī* birds to the wives of the gods, *kulīkā* birds to the divine sisters, and *pāruṣṇa* birds to Agni Gṛhapati.

He offers the *pārāvata* birds to the Day, the *sīcāpuṣ* birds to the Night, the *jatū* birds to the junctions of day and night, the *dātyauha* birds to the Months, and the great *suparṇa* birds to the Year.
From the earth he obtains moles; from the intermediate space, sparrows; from the sky, swift birds; from the quarters, mongooses; and from the intermediate directions, brown mongooses.
He sacrifices spotted deer to the Vasus, Ruru antelopes to the Rudras, Nyanku antelopes to the Ādityas, speckled deer to the Viśvedevas, and Kuluṅga antelopes to the Sādhyas.
He dedicates the wild asses to Īśāna, the oxen to Mitra, the buffaloes to Varuṇa, the gayals to Bṛhaspati, and the camels to Tvaṣṭṛ.
To Prajāpati he sacrifices men and elephants; to Speech, gnats; to Sight, mosquitoes; to Hearing, bees.

To Prajāpati and to Vāyu, a gayal; to Varuṇa, a wild ram; to Yama, a black antelope; to the king of men, a monkey; to the tiger, a red deer; to the bull, a gavaya cow; to the swift falcon, a quail; to the blue ox, a worm; to the ocean, a porpoise; to the Himavat, an elephant.

The mayu belongs to Prajāpati; the ulūka, the halikṣṇa, and the vṛṣadaṃśa belong to Dhātṛ; the kaṅka belongs to the Quarters; the dhūṅkṣā belongs to Agni; the kalaviṅka, the red snake, and the puṣkarasāda belong to Tvaṣṭṛ; the curlew belongs to Vāc.

The forest antelope is for Soma; the goat, the mongoose, and the *śaka* bird—these are for Pūṣan; the jackal is for Māyū; the Gauramṛga deer is for Indra; the *pidva* and the *nyaṅku* are for Anumati; and the *cakravāka* crane is for Pratiśrutkā.

The crane belongs to Sūrya; the śārga, the sṛjaya, and the śayāṇḍaka—these belong to Mitra; the śāri that speaks like a man belongs to Sarasvatī; the porcupine belongs to the Earth; the tiger, the wolf, and the viper—these belong to Manyu; the parrot that speaks like a man belongs to Sarasvant.

The Suparṇa for Pārjanya; the Āti, the Vāhasa, and the Darvī for Vāyu; the Paiṅgarāja for Bṛhaspati, the Lord of Speech; the Alaja for the Atmosphere; the Plava, the Madgu, and the fish for the Lord of Rivers; the tortoise for Heaven and Earth.

The male deer belongs to the Moon; the iguana, the *kālakā*, and the woodpecker belong to the Trees; the cock belongs to Savitṛ; the swan, the crocodile, and the *kulīpaya* belong to the Ocean; and the porcupine belongs to Modesty.

The female antelope belongs to the Day; the frog, the mouse, and the partridge belong to the Serpents; the jackal belongs to the Aśvins; the black [antelope] belongs to the Night; the bear, the bat, and the suṣilīkā belong to the Itarajanās; and the snake-skin belongs to Viṣṇu.

The *anyavāpa* belongs to the half-months; the *ṛśya*, the peacock, and the *suparṇa* belong to the Gandharvas; the *udra* belongs to the waters; *kaśyapa*, the *rohit*, the *kuṇḍṛṇācī*, and the *golattikā* belong to the Apsarases; and the black [antelope] belongs to Death.

The peacock belongs to the rains; the mole, the hedgehog, and the *mānthāla* belong to the seasons; the python belongs to the strength of the ancestors; the francolin partridge, the pigeon, the owl, and the hare belong to Nirṛti; and the wild ram belongs to Varuṇa.

The white leper belongs to the Ādityas; the camel, the *ghṛṇīvān*, and the *vārdhrīṇasa* belong to Mṛtyu; the *sṛmara* belongs to the Forest; the *ruru* deer belongs to Rudra; the *kvayi*, the *kuṭaru*, and the *dātyauha* belong to the Vājins; and the cuckoo belongs to Kāma.

The rhinoceros belongs to the Vaiśvadevas; the black-eared dog, the donkey, and the hyena belong to the Rakṣases; the boar belongs to Indra; the lion belongs to the Maruts; the chameleon, the pippakā bird, and the śakuni bird belong to Śaravyā; and the spotted deer belongs to the Viśve Devas.

With his teeth he [takes] the young grass; with the roots of his teeth, the *avakā* plant; with his gums, the clay; with his tusks, the reeds; with his foremost tongue, the tip of the Sarasvatī; with his tongue, the swelling; with his roar, the palate; with his jaws, the strength; with his mouth, the waters; with his testicles, the bull; with his beard, the Ādityas; with his eyebrows, the path; with his eyelashes, heaven and earth; with his pupils, the lightning. Hail to the white! Hail to the black! The upper eyelashes are the far shore; the lower eyelashes are the reeds. The lower eyelashes are the far shore; the upper eyelashes are the reeds.

He places the wind with the out-breath and the in-breath; the nostrils with the lower lip, and the seat (the mouth) with the upper lip; the internal space with the light, and the external space with the reflection; the head with the crown of the head; the thunder with the skull, and the lightning-bolt with the brain; the lightning with the two pupils, and the sense of hearing with the ears; the ears with the two auditory canals; the pain with the lower throat; the waters with the dry throat; the mind with the neck-tendons; Aditi with the head; Nirṛti with the bald spot on the head; the vital breaths with the cries of distress; and the whirlwind with the tuft of hair.

With his hair [he overcame] mosquitoes; with Indra, through his skillful vehicle; with Bṛhaspati, through the bird-seated [chariot]; with his skin [he overcame] tortoises; with his two thighs, the act of treading; with his ribs, the *ṛkṣala* birds; with his speed, the *kapiñjala* partridges; with his shanks, the road; with his arms, the *jāmbīla* tree; with his two shoulders, the forest fire; with Pūṣan, his two forearms; with the Aśvins, his two shoulder-blades; with Rudra, his two collarbones.

The first belongs to Agni; the second to Vāyu; the third to Indra; the fourth to Soma; the fifth to Aditi; the sixth to Indrāṇī; the seventh to the Maruts; the eighth to Bṛhaspati; the ninth to Aryaman; the tenth to Dhātṛ; the eleventh to Indra; the twelfth to Varuṇa; the thirteenth to Yama.

The wing belongs to Indra and Agni; the counter-wing to Sarasvatī; the third to Mitra; the fourth to the Waters; the fifth to Nirṛti; the sixth to Agni and Soma; the seventh to the Serpents; the eighth to Viṣṇu; the ninth to Pūṣan; the tenth to Tvaṣṭṛ; the eleventh to Indra; the twelfth to Varuṇa; the thirteenth to Yama; the right side belongs to Heaven and Earth; and the left side to the Viśvedevas.

The shoulders belong to the Maruts; the first vertebrae belong to the Viśvedevas; the second [vertebrae] belong to the Rudras; the third [vertebrae] belong to the Ādityas; the tail belongs to Vāyu; the two buttocks belong to Agni and Soma; Indra and Bṛhaspati [are placed] in the two hips; Mitra and Varuṇa in the two thighs; the stepping belongs to the two *algas*; strength in the two *sthūras*; and power in the two *kuṣṭhas*.

Pūṣan with the rectum, the blind snakes with the large intestine, the serpents with the small intestines, the *vihruta* with the entrails, the waters with the bladder, the bull with the testicles, the vigorous steed with the penis, offspring with the seed, the blue jays with the bile, the fissures with the anus, and the *kūṣma* fruits with the balls of dung.

The plaything of Indra; the belly of Aditi; the collar-bones of the quarters; the ash of Aditi; the clouds with the heart-membrane; the atmosphere with the pericardium; the mist with the stomach; the cakravāka birds with the two kidneys; heaven with the two kidneys; the mountains with the entrails; the stones with the spleen; the anthills with the lungs; the thickets with the globes; the rivers with the veins; the lakes with the hollows; the ocean with the two flanks; Vaiśvānara with the belly; and the ashes.

The *vidhṛti* he holds with his navel; the waters with his essence; the rays with the broth; the mist with his droplets; the cold with his heat; the fat with his grease; the tears with his sprays; the hailstones with his rheum of the eyes; the *rakṣases* with his flesh; the variegated stars with his limbs; the earth with his form; with his skin [he holds] the *jumbaka*; *svāhā*!
In the beginning, Hiraṇyagarbha arose; once born, he was the sole lord of all that exists. He supported this earth and yonder sky. To what god shall we offer worship with our oblation?
He who by his greatness alone became the sole king of the breathing and blinking world; he who rules over these bipeds and quadrupeds—to what god shall we offer worship with our oblation?
He whose greatness these Himalayas proclaim, who they say is the ocean together with the Rasā river, whose arms are these quarters of space—to what god shall we offer worship with our oblation?

He who is the giver of self and the giver of strength, whose command all the gods revere—he whose shadow is immortality and whose [other side] is death—to what god shall we offer worship with our oblation?

May auspicious thoughts come to us from every side—thoughts that are undeceived, unassailable, and victorious. May the gods be ever with us for our prosperity, our guardians day by day, never failing in their protection.

May the auspicious favor of the gods, who walk uprightly, be ours; may the bounty of the gods turn toward us. We have sought the friendship of the gods; may the gods extend our lifespan that we may live.
We invoke them with the ancient invocation: Bhaga, Mitra, Aditi, Dakṣa the infallible, Aryaman, Varuṇa, Soma, and the Aśvins. May Sarasvatī, the auspicious one, grant us happiness.

May the wind blow that healing balm to us, bringing joy; may Mother Earth and Father Heaven grant it. May the pressing-stones that extract Soma bring that joy; O Aśvins, you who are worthy of praise, hear this!

We invoke for our protection that Lord, the master of all that moves and stands, the stimulator of the intellect; may Pūṣan be the increaser of our wealth, our guardian and undeceivable protector for our well-being.
