May Indra of far-reaching fame grant us well-being; may Pūṣan, the knower of all, grant us well-being; may Tārkṣya with his uninjured wheel-rims grant us well-being; may Bṛhaspati bestow well-being upon us.

The Maruts, whose steeds are spotted, whose mother is Pṛśni, who move in splendor and frequent the assemblies; the Manavas with Agni for their tongue and the Sun for their eye—may all the gods come here to us with their protection.

O Gods, may we hear with our ears what is auspicious; O Holy Ones, may we see with our eyes what is auspicious. With firm limbs and bodies, having offered praise, may we attain that lifespan ordained by the Gods.
A hundred autumns are before us, O gods, within which you have ordained the aging of our bodies; wherein sons become fathers—do not harm our life-span in its middle course.

Aditi is heaven, Aditi is the mid-region; Aditi is the mother, she is the father, she is the son. All the gods are Aditi, the five peoples are Aditi; Aditi is all that has been born, Aditi is all that is to be born.
May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aryaman, Āyu, Indra, Ṛbhukṣan, and the Maruts not look with disfavor upon us, as we proclaim in the assembly the heroic deeds of the prize-winning steed, born of the gods.
When they lead before him the seized gift of the ram covered with wealth and washed clean—the bleating, multiform goat goes straight forward to the beloved path of Indra and Pūṣan.

This goat, the portion for Pūṣan, belonging to all the gods, is led before the vigorous horse; since Tvaṣṭṛ quickens this beloved sacrificial cake together with the steed for the sake of great renown.

When men lead the horse, fit for oblation, three times around the path that leads to the gods according to the seasons—at this point, the goat, Pūṣan’s first portion, goes forth, announcing the sacrifice to the gods.
The Hotṛ, the Adhvaryu, the Āvayāj, the Agnimindha, the Grāvagrābha, and the wise Śaṃstṛ—fill the bellies with this well-prepared, well-offered sacrifice.

May the praise of those who hew the sacrificial post, those who carry the post, those who carve the top-ring for the horse’s post, and those who prepare the cooking-vessel for the steed—may their approval further us.

He has come near; my prayer has been well-placed for him, he whose back is smooth, toward the regions of the gods. The inspired sages rejoice after him; we have made him a good kinsman in the prosperity of the gods.
Whatever halter binds the prize-winning steed, whatever head-stall or rope belongs to him, or whatever grass has been placed in his mouth as fodder—may all those be yours among the gods.

Whatever of the horse’s raw flesh the fly has eaten, or whatever is smeared on the sacrificial post or the axe, whatever is on the hands of the immolator or on his nails—may all that of yours be among the gods.

Whatever undigested food from the belly escapes, whatever odor of raw flesh there is—let the immolators make that well-prepared, and let them cook the sacrificial oblation until it is thoroughly cooked.
Whatever from your body, as it is being cooked by fire after you have been impaled on the spit, drips away—let that not rest upon the earth, nor upon the grass; let it be granted to the longing gods.
May the approval of those who look upon the horse as cooked, of those who say, "It smells good, take it away," and of those who wait for a morsel of the steed's flesh, further us.

The ladle for basting the meat, the cauldron for cooking the flesh, the vessels for pouring the broth, the warming-covers for the pots, the hooks, and the carving-boards—all these attend upon the horse.

Let not the smoke-scented fire crackle at you, nor the glowing cauldron, smelling of fat, burst asunder. O gods, accept this horse—sacrificed, enjoyed, approved, and consecrated with the cry of *vaṣaṭ*.
The stepping forth, the sitting down, the rolling over, and that which is the fetter of the horse; whatever he drank and whatever fodder he ate—may all those things of yours be among the gods.
The garment they spread beneath the horse, the upper covering, the golden ornaments, the halter for the steed, and the fetter—these dear things they offer among the gods.

Whatever of yours was pained by the heel or by the whip when you were urged on with great force in the race—just as one offers oblations with a ladle at the sacrifices, all those [pains] of yours I soothe with a sacred prayer (*brahman*).
The axe meets the thirty-four ribs of the horse, the steed of the divine kin. Make the limbs free from injury; following the joints, carve it apart with skill, proclaiming it joint by joint.
One is the dissector of Tvaṣṭṛ’s horse; two are the guides, and such is the season. Those of thy limbs which I prepare in due order, those very portions I offer as balls into the fire.
Let not your dear self burn you as you depart; let not the axe linger upon your body. Let not the greedy, unskillful carver, overreaching, mangle your limbs haphazardly with the knife.

Indeed, you do not die here, nor do you suffer harm; you go to the gods by easy paths. Your two bay steeds and the two spotted mares have been harnessed; the vigorous steed has taken its place at the pole of the donkey.

May the prize-winning steed grant us abundance of cattle, abundance of horses, male children, and all-sustaining wealth. May Aditi grant us freedom from sin; may the horse, accompanied by our oblation, win for us sovereign power.

Which of these worlds shall we now establish? Indra and all the gods; may Indra, together with the Ādityas and the host of Maruts, prepare medicines for us. May Indra, along with the Ādityas, fully establish our sacrifice, our bodies, and our progeny.
O Agni, be our closest relative, our protector, and our auspicious guardian.
Agni is the Vasu, possessed of Vasu-glory; come hither and grant us most resplendent wealth.
Thee, O most radiant one, shining forth, we now implore for the welfare of our friends.

Agni and the earth bow together; may they both bow for me toward that [goal]. Vāyu and the intermediate space bow together; may they both bow for me toward that [goal]. Āditya and the sky bow together; may they both bow for me toward that [goal]. The waters and Varuṇa bow together; may they both bow for me toward that [goal]. The seven assemblies, with the eighth being the achiever of beings—make the paths favorable to my desire; let there be mutual recognition between me and that person.
So that I may speak these auspicious words to the people: to the Brahmins and the Kṣatriyas, to the Śūdras and the Āryas, to my own kin and to the wandering minstrels.
May I be dear to the gods for the sake of the sacrificial gift of the giver here; may this desire of mine be fulfilled; may the exhilaration bow down toward me.
O Bṛhaspati, that which surpasses the worthy rival, which shines brilliantly and possesses wisdom among the people, and which glows with power, born of the *ṛta*—bestow upon us that wonderful wealth.
You are taken with a support; for Bṛhaspati, you! This is your womb; for Bṛhaspati, you!
O Indra, possessor of cattle, come here; drink the Soma, O Śatakratu, pressed by the sounding stones.
You are taken with a support; for Indra accompanied by cattle, you! This is your womb; for Indra accompanied by cattle, you!
O Indra, slayer of Vṛtra, come hither; O Śatakratu, drink the Soma pressed by the stone-pressers accompanied by cattle.
You are taken with a support; for Indra accompanied by cattle, you! This is your resting place; for Indra accompanied by cattle, you!
We implore Vaiśvānara, the observer of cosmic order, the lord of the light of truth, the imperishable heat.
You are taken with a support; for Vaiśvānara you! This is your womb; for Vaiśvānara you!
May we abide in the good-will of Vaiśvānara; for he is the King, the glory of all beings. Born from here, he beholds this entire universe; Vaiśvānara strives in unison with the Sun.
You are taken with a support; for Vaiśvānara you! This is your womb; for Vaiśvānara you!
May Vaiśvānara come to us for our protection from afar, Agni, brought by means of our hymn of praise.
You are taken with a support; for Vaiśvānara you! This is your womb; for Vaiśvānara you!
Agni is the seer, the purifying one, the priest of the five peoples; we implore him for great wealth.
You are taken with a support; for Agni, you, for splendor! This is your womb; for Agni, you, for splendor!
May Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt, the sixteenfold one, grant protection in the great [battle]; may he slay the evil one who hates us.
You are taken with a support; for Mahendra you! This is your womb; for Mahendra you!
We celebrate with songs that wondrous Indra, the subduer of enemies, who rejoices in the exhilarating soma-juice—just as cows low toward their calf in the stalls.
Sing forth a great hymn to Agni with that which is most effective, O Vibhāvasu; like a mighty queen, from thee wealth and from thee spoils of war arise.
Come here, O Agni; I shall truly proclaim these other songs to you; may you grow strong through these drops.
May the Seasons extend your sacrifice; may the Months protect your oblation. May the Year establish our sacrifice for us, and may it guard our progeny on every side.
In the secret place of the mountains and at the confluence of the rivers, the sage was born through inspired thought.
High is the birth of your juice; seated in heaven, it is received upon the earth—terrible protection and great renown.
Flow forth, O finder of wealth, for that Indra who is worthy of sacrifice, for Varuṇa, and for the Maruts.
Desiring to win all these splendors of the noble one among men, we conquer with this [prayer].

May we prosper with heroes, with cattle, with horses, and with all forms of nourishment; may we prosper with our bipeds and our quadrupeds. O Gods, may you lead our sacrifice according to the seasons.
O Agni, bring here the willing wives of the gods, and Tvaṣṭṛ, for the drinking of the Soma.
Favor our sacrifice; O Gṇās, O Neṣṭar, drink according to the season, for you are the bestower of treasures.
The giver of wealth desires to drink; offer the oblation and step forward; let it be sent forth from the office of the Neṣṭṛ according to the seasons.
This Soma is yours; come hither, most constantly and well-disposed, drink of it! Having sat down upon the sacrificial grass at this sacrifice, O Indra, take this drop into your belly.

Come indeed to us, you who are easy to invoke; sit down upon the sacrificial grass and take your delight. Then, O Tvaṣṭṛ, being well-disposed toward the Soma juice, rejoice with the gods and their wives, together with your excellent host.
Flow with your sweetest and most intoxicating stream, O Soma, pressed for Indra to drink.
The slayer of demons, the observer of all people, has sat upon his seat with wood—the place of assembly that is not struck by iron—near his source.
May the seasons, O Agni, and the years increase thee, along with the seers and those truths; shine forth with the celestial light and illuminate all four quarters.
O Agni, be kindled and awaken him; arise for great good fortune. May he who sits near you, O Agni, not come to harm; may your priests be glorious, and no others.
O Agni, these Brahmins choose you; O Agni, be auspicious to us in our dwelling. As a slayer of rivals and a conqueror of those who seek to harm us, protect our own home with unwearied vigilance.

Right here, O Agni, bestow upon us a stream of wealth; let not those who were previously established as oppressors humble you. O Agni, may sovereign power be easy for you to wield; may he who sits near you increase, unsubdued.

O Agni, with sovereign power (*kṣatra*) grasp your own life-force; O Agni, strive for friendship in the bond of alliance. Stand in the midst of your kinsmen; O Agni, as one to be invoked by kings, shine here.
O Agni, [ward off] excessive cold, excessive heat, lack of thought, and hostility; for you, O Agni, overcome all difficulties. Then grant us wealth together with heroic sons.

Invincible Jātavedas, unassailable Virāj, O Agni, shine here as the upholder of dominion; releasing all fears from men toward every quarter, protect us today with your auspicious blessings for our prosperity.
O Bṛhaspati, O Savitṛ, awaken him; sharpen him who is already sharpened even more. Increase him for great good fortune; let all the gods rejoice after him.

O Bṛhaspati, since you have released us from the curse of Yama regarding our existence in the next world, may the Aśvins and the two physicians of the gods, O Agni, drive death away from us by their powers.
Beholding the higher light beyond the darkness, we have gone to the Sun, the god among gods, the supreme radiance.
Upward rise his fuel-sticks, upward the bright flames of Agni, most radiant for the son of noble countenance.
May Tanūnapāt, the Asura, the all-knowing god among gods, anoint the paths with honey and ghee.
O Agni, being gratified, you approach the sacrifice with honey as Narāśaṃsa; [so too does] the god Savitṛ, the doer of good deeds, who possesses all boons.
The bearer of oblations, praised with reverence, goes forth with power and clarity through the clarified butter, as the ladles are extended in the sacrifices toward Agni.

May he, the Yakṣa, proclaim the greatness of this Agni; may he, the delightful one, well-provided with nourishment, the most excellent bestower of wealth, and the greatest granter of riches, call upon him.
All the goddesses, the doors, follow his laws; they belong to Agni, wide-extending, ruling according to their station.
May those two celestial maidens, Dawn and Night, like two wives in their home, protect this sacrifice and our ritual service.
O two divine Hotṛ-priests, extol our sacrifice upward from the fire; with your ladle, accept it and make it well-performed for us.
May the three goddesses—Iḍā, Sarasvatī, and Bhāratī—sit upon this sacred grass, the great one being praised.
Then may Tvaṣṭṛ release for us the wonderful drop, rich in nourishment, abounding in hero-strength, and the increase of wealth at our very center.
O Lord of the Forest, release [the victim], being gracious by yourself among the gods; let Agni, the immolator, prepare the oblation.
O Agni Jātavedas, offer this oblation with the cry of Svāhā to Indra; may all the gods graciously accept this sacrificial offering.

The wise, white one, the glory of his teams, who increases wealth with plump food, attends upon them. They, being of one mind, have spread themselves out for Vāyu; all these men have performed noble deeds.

For the sake of wealth, these two worlds, Heaven and Earth, brought him forth; for the sake of wealth, the divine Dhiṣaṇā establishes the god. And may his teams of horses attend upon Vāyu, as well as the white one, the bestower of riches, in his exclusive domain.
When the vast waters went everywhere, bearing the embryo and generating Agni, from that there arose the one life-force (asus) of the gods; to what god shall we offer worship with our oblation?
He who by his greatness surveyed the waters as they held creative power and brought forth the sacrifice—he who was the one God above all gods—to what god shall we offer worship with our oblation?

With those teams by which you go toward the donor for the sake of sacrifice in his home, O Vāyu—bestow upon us wealth that provides excellent nourishment, and grant us heroic sons and the gift of cattle and horses.
Come to our sacrifice with your teams of horses, by the hundreds and by the thousands; O Vāyu, rejoice at this libation! Do you all protect us always with your blessings.
O Vāyu, come with your team; this bright [soma] is offered to you. You shall go to the house of the one who presses the juice.
O Vāyu, the bright essence of the honeyed mead is offered to you at the morning sacrifices; come, O desirable god, with your team of horses, for the drinking of the Soma.
May Vāyu, who goes at the head [of the sacrifice] and delights in the sacrifice, come together with the mind to the sacrifice, auspicious with his auspicious teams of horses.
O Vāyu, with those thousandfold chariots of yours, come hither, drawn by your teams of horses, to drink the Soma.
With one and with ten, with two for our desire, and with twenty; with three and with thirty, O Vāyu, you carry us here—unharness those teams.
O Vāyu, Lord of Cosmic Order, Wondrous Son-in-law of Tvaṣṭṛ, we choose your protections for ourselves.
We cry out to you, O Hero, like unmilked cows, to you, Indra, the lord of this moving world, the beholder of heaven, the lord of all that stands still.

But there is no other like you, neither celestial nor terrestrial; none has been born, nor will be born. Desiring horses, O bounteous Indra, and desiring cattle, we who are seekers of strength call upon you.
For we poets indeed call upon you for the winning of booty; O Indra, lords of the virtuous, men call upon you against the Vritras, and upon you in the races of the steed.

As such, O wondrous one, wielder of the thunderbolt, being boldly praised by us, O lord of the pressing-stones—shower upon us cattle and chariot-horses, O Indra, like the total prize of victory for a conqueror.
With what aid has the ever-prospering friend come to us, O Citra? With what most powerful host?
Which true one among the exhilarations, most bountiful, shall intoxicate you with the soma-juice so that you may break open even the firmest wealth?
Be truly our protector, O friend of us who sing your praises; may you be present in a hundred ways for our aid.
With every sacrifice and with every song, we shall extol for your sake Agni, for his skill; we shall praise the immortal Jātavedas, like a beloved friend.
Protect us, O Agni, with one [verse]; protect us also with a second; protect us with three hymns, O Lord of Strength; protect us with four, O Vasu.
Let us serve the Son of Strength with this offering, seeking his favor for the giving of oblations; may he be our helper in battles, our strengthener, and the protector of our bodies.

You are the *saṃvatsara*, you are the *parivatsara*, you are the *idāvatsara*, you are the *idvatsara*, you are the *vatsara*. May your dawns be well-ordered; may your days and nights be well-ordered; may your half-months be well-ordered; may your months be well-ordered; may your seasons be well-ordered; may your year be well-ordered. Go forth to return, come together and move forward! You are the builder of the eagle; by that deity, sit firm like Aṅgiras.

Let the Hotṛ worship Indra with the kindling-stick at the place of libation, upon the navel of the earth. Kindled at the height of heaven, may he, the most powerful subduer of peoples, partake of the clarified butter; O Hotṛ, sacrifice!

Let the Hotṛ worship Tanūnapāt with his aids—the invincible conqueror, the god Indra who finds the light of heaven—through the paths most rich in sweetness; let him partake of the clarified butter through the splendor of Narāśaṃsa. O Hotṛ, sacrifice!

Let the Hotṛ worship Indra, who is praised with invocations, the immortal one being invoked; the god of mighty strength, thunderbolt in hand, the breaker of forts, together with the gods—let him enjoy the clarified butter. O Hotṛ, sacrifice!

Let the Hotṛ worship Indra, the most excellent, the bull, the performer of manly deeds, who sits upon the sacrificial grass together with the Vasus, Rudras, and Ādityas—well-yoked companions. Let him partake of the clarified butter; O Hotṛ, sacrifice!

Let the Hotṛ worship: like vigor, heroism, and conquering might, the Doors have magnified Indra. May they, easy of access and increasing the Truth, open wide for this sacrifice—a self-resounding song for the bounteous Indra. Let them partake of the clarified butter; O Hotṛ, sacrifice!

Let the Hotṛ worship Dawn and the two milch-cows of Indra, the great mothers, easy to milk. Like two self-moving ones in their brilliance, they have nourished Indra, the calf; let them partake of the clarified butter—O Hotṛ, sacrifice!

Let the Hotṛ worship the two divine Hotṛs, the physicians, the friends who heal Indra with the oblation. May the two wise gods, the seers, bestow vital power upon Indra; let them partake of the clarified butter. O Hotṛ, sacrifice!

Let the Hotṛ worship the three goddesses for our medicine—the three who possess triple natures and perform their work: Iḷā, Sarasvatī, and the great Bhāratī. Let these wives of Indra, rich in oblations, enjoy the clarified butter; O Hotṛ, sacrifice!

Let the Hotṛ worship Tvaṣṭṛ, the divine Indra, the physician, the well-sacrificing, the one adorned with ghee, the multiform, the rich in seed, the munificent. May Tvaṣṭṛ bestow powers upon Indra; let him partake of the clarified butter. O Hotṛ, sacrifice!

Let the Hotṛ worship Vanaspati, the immolator of a hundredfold power, the lover of prayers, the essence of Indra. Smearing him with honey along easy paths, he makes the sacrifice sweet with honey and ghee; let him partake of the clarified butter. O Hotṛ, sacrifice!

Let the Hotṛ worship Indra: Svāhā to the clarified butter, Svāhā to the fat, Svāhā to the drops, Svāhā to the consecrations with *svāhā*, Svāhā to the hymns of oblation! Svāhā! May the butter-drinking gods, and Indra, graciously partaking of the clarified butter, enjoy it; O Hotṛ, sacrifice!

The divine sacrificial grass (*barhis*), well-divine with the gods, spread upon the altar, has strengthened Indra, the hero-filled one. Chosen at evening and brought forward at dawn, it has surpassed those possessing the grass through its wealth. For the winning of goods, may it partake of the gift of wealth; sacrifice!

The divine doors, firm in their assembly, have strengthened Indra on his journey. May they, driving away the jointless Reṇukakāṭa with a young calf and a living boy, enjoy the gift of wealth from the treasury of wealth; sacrifice!

The two goddesses, Dawn and Night, have summoned Indra as the sacrifice proceeds. The divine clans have set forth; well-pleased and well-disposed, may they partake of the gift of wealth for the sake of the winner of riches. Sacrifice!

The two divine consorts, the bestowers of wealth, have magnified the god Indra. One of them drives away hatreds; the other, skilled in her task, shall bring desirable riches to the sacrificer. For the winning of wealth and the granting of treasure, let them both enjoy [the offering]; sacrifice!

The two goddesses, Ūrjā and Āhutī, have milked out the milk for Indra and caused him to grow. One shall bring nourishment and vigor; the other, food and drink together. Bestowing the old upon the new, they have established the new through the old. Strengthening with vigor, O Ūrjā and Āhutī, bestow riches upon the sacrificer, you who are skilled. For the winning of wealth, partake of the gift of wealth; sacrifice!

The two divine Hotṛ-priests have strengthened the god Indra; having struck down the evil-speakers, they have brought hither desirable riches for the sacrificer. Skilled in their task, may they partake of the gift of wealth for the sake of winning wealth; sacrifice!

The three goddesses—the three goddesses—strengthened their husband Indra. Bhāratī touched the sky; Sarasvatī, with the Rudras, [touched] the sacrifice; and Iḍā, rich in wealth, [touched] the houses. May they partake of the gift of wealth from the treasury of wealth; sacrifice!

O God, Indra, praised by men, possessing triple protection and triple-seated chariot, has magnified the divine Indra. Borne by a hundred white-backed steeds, he proceeds with a thousand. O Mitra and Varuṇa, his office of Hotṛ is worthy; O Bṛhaspati, his Stotra is yours; O Aśvins, his Adhvaryu-work is yours. For the winning of wealth, for the bestowing of treasure, let him enjoy it; sacrifice!

The divine Lord of the Forest, with golden leaves, honeyed branches, and excellent fruit, having been strengthened by the gods for the sake of the divine Indra—touching the sky with his summit, filling the intermediate space, and supporting the earth—let him partake of the gift of wealth for the sake of obtaining riches; sacrifice!

The divine *barhis* of the water-plantations has magnified the divine Indra; seated comfortably together with Indra, it has surpassed all other *barhis* grasses. For the winning of wealth, for the granting of treasure, let it enjoy [the offering]; sacrifice!

The divine Agni Sviṣṭakṛt has strengthened the divine Indra. Making the sacrifice well-offered, may Sviṣṭakṛt make our sacrifice well-offered today. For the winning of wealth and for the granting of treasure, may he accept it; perform the sacrifice!

Today this sacrificer has chosen Agni as the Hotṛ-priest; cooking the cooked offerings, he cooks the sacrificial cake and binds the goat for Indra. Today the divine Vanaspati has become well-situated for Indra with the goat. He has eaten it from the fat; he has taken his portion from the cooked offering and has grown strong with the sacrificial cake.

O Ṛṣi, descendant of Ṛṣis, grandson of Ṛṣis, this sacrificer has chosen you today from among many who have assembled, thinking, "This one shall sacrifice for me among the gods for desirable wealth. Whatever divine gifts the gods have given, ordain them for him and approve them; you, O Hotṛ, are impelled for the auspicious proclamation. Sent by man for the recitation of the hymns, speak the well-spoken words.

Let the Hotṛ worship Agni, the kindled one, the great glory, well-kindled and most excellent; [let him worship] Indra, the bestower of vitality. Bestowing the Gāyatrī metre, sensory power, a three-year-old cow, and vigor, let him partake of the clarified butter. O Hotṛ, sacrifice!

Let the Hotṛ worship Tanūnapāt, the piercer, whom Aditi bore as her pure embryo—Indra, the bestower of vital strength. Bestowing the Uṣṇih meter, sensory power, the Dityavāh ox, and life-force, let him partake of the clarified butter; O Hotṛ, sacrifice!

Let the Hotṛ worship the one worthy of praise, the praised, the greatest slayer of Vṛtra, the strength that is to be lauded with invocations—the Soma, Indra, the bestower of vital power. Bestowing the Anuṣṭubh metre, the sense-power, the five-year-old cow, and vitality, let him partake of the clarified butter; O Hotṛ, sacrifice!

Let the Hotṛ worship the immortal Puṣan, who possesses a good sacrificial grass and is accompanied by [the Maruts], as he sits upon the beloved sacrificial grass—Indra, the immortal, the bestower of vigor. Bestowing the Bṛhatī metre, sensory power, a three-year-old bull, and vitality, let him partake of the clarified butter; O Hotṛ, sacrifice!

Let the Hotṛ worship the divine Doors—spacious, easy of access, increasers of cosmic order, golden-hued—who [bring] Indra, the Brahman, the bestower of vitality. May they, bestowing the Paṅkti meter, sensory power here, the four-year-old draft-ox, and vigor, partake of the clarified butter. O Hotṛ, sacrifice!

Let the Hotṛ worship with the two great ones, well-adorned and well-fashioned, like the beautiful Night and Dawn; [let him worship] Indra, the bestower of vigor, the all-encompassing. May they partake of the clarified butter, bestowing here the Triṣṭubh metre, sensory power, and a draft-ox as a vehicle, providing vital strength. O Hotṛ, sacrifice!

Let the Hotṛ worship with the two wise ones, the supreme glory of the gods; let the two divine Hotṛs, the sages, together with Indra, the bestower of vital strength, partake. Bestowing the Jagatī metre, sensory power, the ox, the cow, and vitality, let them enjoy the clarified butter; O Hotṛ, perform the sacrifice!

Let the Hotṛ worship the three goddesses, the adorned ones—Bhāratī, Sarasvatī, and Ilā—who are golden, vast, and great; let him worship Indra, the Lord who bestows vital strength. May they bestow here the Virāj metre, sensory power, and the cow as a milch-cow providing nourishment. O Hotṛ, sacrifice with the clarified butter!

Let the Hotṛ worship Tvaṣṭṛ, the possessor of good seed, the increaser of prosperity, who bears various forms; [let him worship] Indra, the bestower of vigor, who possesses nourishment and two-footed meters. Bestowing strength like a bull or a cow, may he partake of the clarified butter; O Hotṛ, sacrifice!

Let the Hotṛ worship Vanaspati, the immolator, the lord of a hundred powers, golden-leaved, worthy of hymns, bearing the tether, the controller, Bhaga, Indra the bestower of vigor; may he, bestowing the Kakubh metre, sensory power, the barren cow, the cow that miscarries, and vitality, partake of the clarified butter—O Hotṛ, sacrifice!

Let the Hotṛ worship with *svāhā*-utterances Agni the householder, Varuṇa separately as the healer, Indra the sage who bestows dominion and vital strength; may they partake of the clarified butter, bestowing the Atichandas metre, sensory power, the great [Sāman], the bull, the cow, and vigor—O Hotṛ, sacrifice!

The divine sacrificial grass has strengthened the divine Indra, the bestower of vigor. Through the Gāyatrī metre, it has bestowed sensory power and sight upon Indra, granting vitality for the winning of wealth and the granting of treasure. May he accept; sacrifice!

The divine Doors have magnified Indra, the pure bestower of vital strength; through the Uṣṇih metre, they have bestowed power, breath, and vitality upon Indra. For the winning of wealth and the granting of treasure, may they partake; sacrifice!

The two goddesses, Dawn and Night, have magnified the god Indra, the bestower of vital strength; through the Anuṣṭubh metre, they have bestowed sensory power, strength, and vitality upon Indra. For the sake of winning wealth, for the granting of treasure, let them partake; sacrifice!

The two divine ones who enjoy together, the bestowers of wealth, have caused the divine Indra, the bestower of vital strength, to grow; through the Bṛhatī metre, they have bestowed sensory power, hearing, and vigor upon Indra. For the winning of wealth, for the granting of wealth, may they partake; sacrifice!

The two goddesses, Ūrjā and Āhutī, the well-milking milkers, have nourished Indra, the god who bestows vital strength; through the Paṅkti metre they have bestowed power and bright vigor upon Indra. For the winning of wealth, for the granting of treasure, let them enjoy [the offering]; sacrifice!

The two divine Hotṛ-priests have magnified the god Indra, the bestower of vital strength; with the Triṣṭubh metre, they have bestowed sensory power, brilliance, and vigor upon Indra. For the winning of wealth, may they partake of the gift of riches; sacrifice!

The three goddesses—the three goddesses—increased their husband Indra, the bestower of vital strength. Through the Jagatī metre, may they bestow sensory power, vigor, and life-force upon Indra; for the winning of wealth, may they partake of the gift of wealth. Sacrifice!

The divine Narāśaṃsa has magnified the divine Indra, the bestower of vital strength; through the Virāj metre, he has bestowed sensory power and form upon Indra, granting him vigor. For the winning of wealth, may he enjoy the gift of riches; sacrifice!

The divine Vanaspati has caused the divine Indra, the bestower of vital strength, to grow; through the Dvipadā metre, bestowing power, fortune, and vitality upon Indra, may he partake of the sacrifice for the winning of wealth and the granting of treasures—perform the offering!

The divine *barhis* has magnified Indra, the god who bestows vital strength, among the waters; it has magnified every god. Bestowing sensory power, glory, and vital strength upon Indra through the *kakubh* meter, may it partake of the gift of wealth for the sake of winning wealth. Sacrifice!

The divine Agni Sviṣṭakṛt has caused the divine Indra, the bestower of vital strength, to increase the god; through the Aticchandas meter he has bestowed sensory power, sovereignty, and vitality upon Indra. For the winning of wealth, let him partake of the offering of wealth; sacrifice!

Today this sacrificer has chosen Agni as the Hotṛ-priest; cooking the cooked offerings, he cooks the sacrificial cake and binds a goat for Indra, the bestower of vigor. Today the divine Vanaspati has become well-established for Indra, the bestower of vigor, by means of the goat. He has eaten it from the fat; he has taken the first portion of the cooked offering and has grown strong with the sacrificial cake.

O Rishi, descendant of Rishis, grandson of Rishis, this sacrificer has chosen you today from among many who have assembled, thinking: "This one shall sacrifice for me among the gods for desirable wealth. O God, those divine gifts which the gods have bestowed, decree them for him and pronounce them; you, O Hotar, are impelled for the auspicious proclamation. Being sent by man for the recitation of the hymns, speak the well-spoken words.

Kindled by the thoughts of those who offer oblations, O Agni, swelling with honeyed ghee, you who are a prize-winning steed carrying the prize, O Jātavedas, carry us to the beloved assembly-place of the gods.

Anointing the god-faring paths with ghee, may the prize-winning steed, knowing them well, go toward the gods. O courser, let the quarters follow you; bestow this self-sustaining power upon this sacrificer.

You are worthy of praise and worthy of worship, O swift steed; you are fleet and fit for sacrifice, O racer. May Agni Jātavedas, in harmony with the Vasu deities, carry you—the beloved bearer—forward.

The sacrificial grass is strewn, well-spread; may Aditi, in harmony with the gods, accept it as it extends wide and broad upon the earth. May she, making it a pleasant seat, establish us in prosperity.
May these blessed, multiform divine Doors—expanding with their wings, rising up with their frames, lofty yet sounding, and being adorned—be easy of access for you.

Moving between, O Mitra and Varuṇa, you two who are in agreement regarding the face of the sacrifices—O Dawn and Night, you who possess beautiful gold and beautiful forms—I establish you here in the womb of Cosmic Order (Ṛta).

First among you two are the golden ones, riding in the same chariot, O gods, beholding all beings; I have extended my offerings to you, measuring out your impulses, O Hotṛs, pointing out the light by means of the quarters of space.

May Bhāratī with the Ādityas desire our sacrifice; may Sarasvatī together with the Rudras protect us. Invoked along with the Vasus, may the goddesses Iḍā, being in harmony, place our sacrifice among the immortals.
Tvaṣṭṛ begot the hero who loves the gods; from Tvaṣṭṛ was born the swift, fleet horse. Tvaṣṭṛ brought forth this entire world; O Hotṛ, worship here the maker of much.
Anointed with ghee by its own nature, let the horse go to the gods according to the seasons; may the Lord of the Forest, knowing the world of the gods, carry the offerings made savory by Agni.

Increasing through the ascetic fervor of Prajāpati, as soon as you were born, O Agni, you took possession of the sacrifice. As the leader, go with the oblation consecrated by Svāhā; let the Sādhyas, the gods, eat the offering.
When you first neighed at birth, rising from the ocean or from the primordial waters, with the wings of a falcon and the forelegs of a deer—O steed, your great birth is worthy of praise.
Yama gave him; Trita harnessed him; Indra was the first to mount him. The Gandharva grasped his rein; O Vasus, you fashioned the horse from the sun.
You are Yama; you are Āditya, O steed; you are Trita by your secret vow. You are divided from Soma by an interval; they say you have three bonds in heaven.
They say you have three bonds in heaven, three in the waters, and three within the ocean. O Varuṇa, you are as if pleased with me, O Courser, at that place where they say is your highest birthplace.
These, O steed, are your groomings; these are the places where the hooves of the winner are set. Here I beheld your auspicious reins, which the guardians of the Eternal Law protect.
I recognized you as yourself from afar with my mind, like a bird flying through the sky; I beheld your head, the winged one, speeding along easy paths that are free from dust.
Here I beheld your supreme form, desiring to win the nourishment at the station of the cow; when the mortal has attained your enjoyment, then, O most voracious one, you have awakened the plants.

After you, O steed, follows the chariot; after you, the young man; after you, the cows; after you, the fortune of maidens. After you, the troops have sought your friendship; after you, the gods have measured out their heroic power.
Golden-horned, his feet were of iron; swift as thought was Indra, who came after him. The gods indeed came to eat his sacrificial oblation—he who was the first to mount the courser.
With swelling haunches and slender waists, the divine coursers are like heroes; like swans they draw up in rows when the horses have reached the celestial racecourse.
O steed, your body is prone to flight; your mind is swift-gliding like the wind. Your horns are spread far and wide; they move flickeringly in many forests.
The swift steed has approached the place of sacrifice, meditating with a mind directed toward the gods. The goat, his kinsman, is led before him; behind him follow the sages and the singers.

He has approached the highest dwelling place, toward his father and mother, the swift steed; for today he shall go to the gods as one most welcome, and then he shall bestow desirable boons upon the donor.
Kindled today in the house of man, O Jātavedas, you, a god, worship the gods. Bring them hither, O you who are great as Mitra; you are the wise messenger, the seer, and the one of keen insight.

O Tanūnapāt, fair-tongued one, anointing the paths that lead along the way of Ṛta with honey, make them sweet; prosper our prayers through our meditations and the sacrifice, and bring our ritual to the gods.
We shall praise with sacrifices the greatness of these, of the worshipful Narāśamsa; those gods who are wise, pure, and supporters of prayer, who relish both kinds of oblations.

Being invoked, worthy of praise and adoration, come, O Agni, in harmony with the Vasus! You are the youthful Hotṛ of the gods; as such, being impelled, perform the sacrifice for them as the most skilled sacrificer.

The sacrificial grass is strewn toward the east according to the direction of the earth; at the beginning of the days, it is gathered for her dwelling. It spreads itself out further and wider, a pleasant seat for the gods and for Aditi.
Let the spacious doors open wide, like women adorning themselves for their husbands; O divine, lofty, all-impelling doors, be easy of access for the gods.

May the two worshipful ones, Dawn and Night, flowing with sweetness, sit down close together in their proper place—the two celestial maidens, lofty and richly adorned, bestowing splendor and radiant beauty.

The two divine Hotṛ-priests, the first, eloquent ones, measuring out the sacrifice for man to worship; the two poets who impel [the rite] in the assemblies, pointing toward the eastern light by their direction.
May Bhāratī come quickly to our sacrifice; may Iḷā, like Manu, be mindful here. May the three goddesses—Sarasvatī and the others, skilled in their work—sit upon this pleasant sacrificial grass.
O Hotṛ, you who are more skilled in sacrifice, being impelled today, worship here with knowledge that god Tvaṣṭṛ, who fashioned these two parents, Heaven and Earth, and all beings with their forms.

Release [the victim] by yourself, anointing it, according to the seasons, for the path of the gods and the oblations. May Vanaspati, the immolator, and the god Agni sweeten the offering with honey and ghee.

As soon as he was born, Agni measured out the sacrifice; he became the leader of the gods. At the command of this Hotṛ, according to the word of Ṛta, let the gods eat the oblation consecrated with Svāhā.
Making a signal for the signalless, making a form for the formless, O men—you were born together with the dawns.
Like a cloud, is his appearance when the armored warrior goes into the lap of the contending hosts; with an uninjured body, may you be victorious—may the greatness of this armor protect you.

With the bow may we win cattle, with the bow may we win the battle; with the bow may we conquer fierce assailants. The bow frustrates the enemy’s purpose; with the bow may we conquer all the quarters.
As if about to speak, she comes close to the ear, embracing her dear friend; like a woman, this bowstring twangs upon the stretched bow, carrying us across in the assembly.

Acting together like a woman toward her husband, may they bear [the arrow] in their lap like a mother her son; may these two bow-ends, acting in concert and vibrating, pierce the enemies and strike down the foes.
The father of many, his son is manifold; he makes a whizzing sound as he enters the fray. Tied upon the back, the quiver—impelled by him—conquers all encounters and hostile armies.
Standing in the chariot, the skilled charioteer leads the horses forward wherever he desires. Admire the greatness of the reins: the traces follow behind, directing the mind.
Making loud noises with their hooves like bulls, the horses, striving for prize along with the chariots, trampling the enemies with their forefeet, destroy the foes without turning back.
The chariot-stand is his name, where his oblation, his weapon, and his armor are laid; there let us sit upon the auspicious chariot, always well-disposed in spirit.

The Fathers, who sit at the sweet draught, bestowers of vital strength, who have endured hardships, powerful, profound, possessing diverse armies, strong with arrows, never-failing, truly heroic, vast, and conquerors of hosts.

The Brahmins, our Soma-loving ancestors, and the auspicious, faultless Heaven and Earth—may Pūṣan protect us from misfortune, O increasers of Truth; guard us, and let no one who speaks evil have power over us.
She clothes herself in an eagle’s plumage; her tooth is a deer; bound with cow-hide, she flies forth when discharged. Where men run together and apart, there may the arrows grant us protection.
O straight-flying one, protect us; let our bodies be as stone. May Soma speak for us, and may Aditi grant us refuge.
They strike their flanks; they beat upon their haunches. O horse-whip, you who are full of wisdom, urge the horses forward in the battles.
Like a serpent with its coils, it encircles the arm, warding off the blow of the bowstring; the hand-guard, knowing all the secret ways, as a man, shall protect the man from every side.
O Lord of the Forest, may you be firm-limbed, our friend, a furtherer, and a possessor of noble heroes; you are bound with cow-hides, so be steadfast—may your rider win all that is to be won.

The strength drawn forth from heaven and earth, the power brought together from the lords of the forest, the vigor of the waters, encompassed by cattle—that chariot which is Indra’s thunderbolt, worship it with an oblation.
The thunderbolt of Indra, the vanguard of the Maruts, the offspring of Mitra, and the navel of Varuṇa—O divine chariot, enjoying this our offering of oblations, accept these gifts.
Cause the earth and the sky to resound; let the world, scattered in many places, take heed of you. O drum, in harmony with Indra and the gods, drive our enemies far, even to the furthest distance.
Shout forth strength; bestow vigor upon us; thunder, driving away misfortunes! O drum, blow away all ill-fortune from here. You are Indra’s fist; be firm!
Drive those away and bring these back; the drum speaks aloud as a signal. Our heroes, winged with horses, come together; O Indra, let our chariot-warriors be victorious!

The one with a black neck is for Agni; the ewe is for Sarasvatī; the tawny one is for Soma; the dark-grey one is for Pūṣan; the white-backed one is for Bṛhaspati; the speckled one is for the Viśvedevas; the ruddy one is for Indra; the dappled one is for the Maruts; the piebald one is for Indra and Agni; the one with a white mark below the neck is for Savitṛ; the black one is for Varuṇa; and the ram with one white foot is for the Unborn.

For Agni Anīkavat, a red-marked ox; two for Savitṛ, with white spots on their bellies; two for Pūṣan, silver-navelled; two for the Viśvedevas, reddish-brown and hornless; one for the Maruts, brindled; one for Agni, black; a goat for Sarasvatī; a ewe for Varuṇa; and a ram for Varuṇa.

To Agni, who is associated with the Gāyatrī metre, the Trivṛt stoma, and the Rathaṃtara sāman, [there is] an offering on eight potsherds; to Indra, who is associated with the Triṣṭubh metre, the Pañcadaśa stoma, and the Bṛhat sāman, [an offering] on eleven potsherds; to the Viśve Devas, who are associated with the Jagatī metre, the Saptadaśa stoma, and the Vairūpa sāman, [an offering] on twelve potsherds; to Mitra and Varuṇa, who are associated with the Anuṣṭubh metre, the Ekaviṃśa stoma, and the Vairāja sāman, [there is] a milk-curd offering (payasyā); to Bṛhaspati, who is associated with the Paṅkti metre, the Triṇava stoma, and the Śākvara sāman, [there is] an oblation of cooked rice (caru); to Savitṛ, who is associated with the Uṣṇih metre, the Trayastriṃśa stoma, and the Raivata sāman, [there is] an offering on twelve potsherds; to Prajāpati, [there is] an oblation of cooked rice; to Aditi, the wife of Viṣṇu, [there is] an oblation of cooked rice; to Agni Vaiśvānara, [there is] an offering on twelve potsherds; and to Anumati, [there is] an offering on eight potsherds.

O divine Savitṛ, impel the sacrifice; impel the lord of the sacrifice for his prosperity. May the celestial Gandharva, the purifier of intentions, purify our intention; may the Lord of Speech make our strength savory.
We meditate upon that most excellent splendor of the divine Savitṛ; may he impel our thoughts.
O God Savitar, drive away all misfortunes; send us that which is auspicious.
We invoke Savitṛ, the beholder of men, the distributor of wonderful wealth and bounty.

A Brāhmaṇa for Brahman; a Rājanya for the Kṣatra; a Vaiśya for the Maruts; a Śūdra for austerity; a thief for darkness; a slayer of heroes for hell; a eunuch for evil; an Ayogū for deception; a harlot for lust; and a Māgadha for excessive shouting.

For dancing, a charioteer; for singing, an actor; for righteousness, an attendant of the assembly; for the Nariṣṭhā [sacrifice], a Bhīmala; for jesting, a Rebha; for laughter, a maker; for bliss, one who finds pleasure in women; for merriment, the son of an unmarried woman; for intelligence, a cartwright; for steadfastness, a carpenter.

To austerity, the potter; to illusion, the smith; to form, the jeweler; to beauty, the weaver; to the arrow-case, the arrow-maker; to the weapon, the bow-maker; to action, the bowstring-maker; to destiny, the rope-maker; to death, the hunter; to the ender, the dog-handler.

From the rivers, the Pauñjiṣṭha; from the Ṛkṣīkas, the Naiṣāda; for the tiger among men, the Durmada; from the Gandharvas and Apsarases, the Vrātya; from the Prayujes, the Unmatta; from the serpents and divine beings, the Apratipadāmayin; from the Īryatā, the Akitava; from the Piśācas, the Bidalakārī; and from the Yātudhānas, the Kaṇṭakīkārī.

For reconciliation, a paramour; for the household, a lover; for affliction, one who has been superseded by a younger brother; for destruction, one who has superseded his own elder brother; for failure, the husband of a younger sister whose elder sister is unmarried; for expiation, a female artisan; for recognition, a female embroiderer; for the fulfillment of desire, a female attendant; for beauty, one who is submissive; for strength, a female servant.

To those who cause depression, a hunchback; for joy, a dwarf; from the doors, one who is lame; for sleep, a blind man; for the half-way state, a deaf man; for purification, a physician; for discernment, one who observes the stars; for instruction, an interrogator; for further instruction, one who asks counter-questions; for the boundary, one who adjudicates questions.

For weapons, a keeper of elephants; for speed, a keeper of horses; for nourishment, a cowherd; for vigor, a keeper of sheep; for splendor, a keeper of goats; for refreshment, a plowman; for sweet drink, a maker of spirits; for prosperity, a house-guardian; for excellence, a steward of wealth; for supervision, an attendant charioteer.

He gives a wood-gatherer for Bhāya; a fire-kindler for Prabhā; one who sprinkles [water] for Bradhna’s summit; an attendant for the highest firmament (nāka); a decorator for the world of the gods; a weaver for the world of men; a scatterer for all worlds; a churner for misfortune and destruction; a washerwoman for sacrifice; and a dyer for pleasure.

For Truth, a thief-hearted man; for the slaying of enemies, a slanderer; for Separation, a door-keeper; for the office of overseer, an assistant door-keeper; for Youth, an attendant; for Abundance, a parasite; for the Beloved, a sweet-talker; for Safety, a horse-breaker; for the World of Heaven, a tax-collector; for the Highest Firmament, a waiter.

One who brings heat for fury, an exit for anger, a yoker for yoga, one who goes forth toward grief, a releaser for security, one who stands firm on high ground, one who fashions honor for beauty, one who applies collyrium for virtue, a weaver of baskets for destruction, and a mother for Yama.

To Yama, a woman who has borne a child; to the Atharvans, one who has miscarried; to the Saṃvatsara, one who has gone astray; to the Parivatsara, one who has not yet given birth; to the Idāvatsara, one who moves too fast; to the Idvatsara, one who stumbles; to the Vatsara, one who is worn out; to the Saṃvatsara, one who is grey-haired; to the Ṛbhus, one whose sinews are like leather; to the Sādhyas, one who wears skins.

From the rivers [he chose] the Dhaivara; from the standing waters, the Dāśa; from the pond-lakes, the Vainya; from the reed-beds, the Śauṣkala; for the further shore, the Mārgāra; for the near shore, the Kevarta; from the fords, the Ānda; from the uneven places, the Maināla; from the sounds, the Parṇaka; from the caves, the Kirāta; from the ridges, the Jambhaka; and from the mountains, the Kiṃpuruṣa.

To loathing, a Paulkasa; to color, a goldsmith; to the balance, a merchant; to the after-gloom, a weary man; to all beings, a leper; to prosperity, one who stays awake; to non-prosperity, one who sleeps; to affliction, a gossip; to failure, a coward; to the breaking-up, a cutter-off.

For the King of Dice, [one should designate] a gambler; for the Kṛta age, one who sees no fault; for the Tretā age, one who is capable; for the Dvāpara age, one who is excessively capable; for Skanda, the pillar of the assembly hall; for Death, the stealer of cattle; for the Ender, the killer of a cow; for Hunger, one who stands begging while another is carving up a cow; for Evil Deeds, the teacher of wandering mendicants; for Sin, the oil-presser.

One who cries out for an echo, one who barks for the sake of sound, one who talks much for the sake of an end, and one who is mute for the sake of infinity; one who strikes a drum for the sake of noise, one who plays the lute for the sake of greatness, one who blows a flute for the sake of shouting, and one who blows a conch for the sake of the distant; one who tends the forest for the sake of the woods, and one who tends the brush for the sake of the remote wilderness—[these are the ones you must avoid].

For amusement, he buys a harlot; for laughter, a courtesan; for water-sports, a village headman, an accountant, and a reviler; for splendor, a lute-player, a hand-clapper, and a flute-player; for dance, a dancer; and for joy, a cymbal-player.

To Agni, one fat; to the Earth, one who crawls on his haunches; to Vāyu, a Caṇḍāla; to the Intermediate Space, one who dances on a bamboo pole; to Heaven, one with a bald head; to Sūrya, one with tawny eyes; to the Nakṣatras, one speckled; to Candramas, one afflicted with leprosy; to the Day, one white with tawny eyes; to the Night, one black with tawny eyes.

Therefore, one should sacrifice these eight deformed ones: one who is too tall, one who is too short, one who is too stout, one who is too thin, one who is too fair, one who is too dark, one who is too bald, and one who is too hairy. They are non-Śūdras and non-Brāhmaṇas; they belong to Prajāpati. The Māgadha, the harlot, the gambler, and the eunuch—these are non-Śūdras and non-Brāhmaṇas; they belong to Prajāpati.
The Puruṣa has a thousand heads, a thousand eyes, and a thousand feet; having pervaded the earth on all sides, he stood beyond it by the measure of ten fingers.
The Person alone is all this—whatever has been and whatever is to be—and he is the lord of immortality, as well as of that which grows by means of food.
Such is his greatness, and the Puruṣa is even greater than this; all beings constitute one quarter of him, while his three quarters are the immortal in heaven.
The Puruṣa rose up three-quarters above; one quarter of him remained here again. From there he strode out in all directions toward that which eats and that which does not eat.
From him Virāj was born; from Virāj was born Puruṣa. Once born, he extended beyond the earth, both behind and before.
From that sacrifice in which everything was offered, the speckled butter was gathered; he made those animals—the ones belonging to Vāyu, whether wild or domestic.
From that sacrifice in which everything was offered, the Ṛg-verses and the Sāman-chants were born; from it the meters were born, and from it the Yajus-formulas were produced.
From him were born horses and whatever animals have two rows of teeth; from him indeed were born cows, and from him were born goats and sheep.
They sprinkled that sacrifice upon the sacrificial grass—the Puruṣa who was born in the beginning; with him, the gods, the Sādhyas, and the Ṛṣis performed the sacrifice.
When they divided the Puruṣa, into how many parts did they arrange him? What was his mouth, what were his two arms, what were his thighs, and what are his feet called?
The Brāhmaṇa was his mouth; the Rājanya was made from his arms; that which was his thighs became the Vaiśya; and from his feet the Śūdra was born.
The moon was born from his mind; from his eye the sun was born; from his ear came the wind and the breath; and from his mouth fire was born.
From his navel the intermediate space arose; from his head the sky evolved; from his feet the earth and from his ears the quarters—thus they fashioned the worlds.
When the gods performed the sacrifice with man as the oblation, spring was its clarified butter, summer the fuel, and autumn the offering.
Seven were its enclosing sticks, thrice seven were the fuel-sticks prepared, when the gods, performing the sacrifice, bound Puruṣa as the victim.
With sacrifice the gods sacrificed to the sacrifice; those were the first ordinances. They, the mighty ones, attained the heights where the ancient Sādhyas, the gods, abide.

Gathered from the waters and from the essence of the earth, he came into being in the beginning from Viśvakarman. Tvaṣṭṛ, fashioning his form, enters him; this is the godhead of mortal man, his origin in the beginning.
I know this great Person, resplendent like the sun, beyond the darkness. Only by knowing Him does one pass over death; there is no other path for the journey.
Prajāpati moves within the womb; though unborn, he is born in many ways. The wise behold his source; in him all worlds are established.
To him who shines upon the gods, who is the domestic priest of the gods, who was born before the gods—to that radiant one belonging to the Brahman, let there be homage.
Generating the splendor of Brahman, the gods spoke this in the beginning: "The god shall be under the control of that brahmin who knows this thus."

Śrī and Lakṣmī are your two wives; day and night are your two sides; the constellations are your form; the Aśvins are your open jaws. Bestowing [blessings], bestow them upon me; bestow this world upon me; bestow the entire world upon me.
That indeed is Agni, that is Āditya, that is Vāyu, and that is Candramas; that indeed is Śukra, that is Brahman, those are the Waters, and he is Prajāpati.
All moments of time were born from the Puruṣa, as was lightning; no one has grasped him from above, nor from across, nor from within.
There is no likeness of him whose name is Great Glory; he is this one called Hiraṇyagarbha; "May he not harm me"—this is [the mantra]; "From whom none has been born"—this is [the mantra].

This very God pervades all the quarters; he was born first, and he is within the womb. He alone is born, and he is yet to be born; facing all directions, he stands before all people with faces on every side.
Since nothing whatsoever existed before he was born, he who brought all worlds into being—that Prajāpati, rejoicing with his offspring, accompanies the three lights; he is the lord of the world.

By whom the formidable heaven and the firm earth were made fast, by whom the sky was propped up and the vault of heaven; he who is the measurer of the mid-air and of the realm of dust—to what god shall we offer worship with our oblation?
To whom the two worlds, supported by his aid, looked up while trembling in their minds; upon whom the risen sun shines forth—to which god shall we offer worship with our oblation?
When the vast waters [were gathered], whatever [strength] was in the waters.

Vena, beholding that which is deposited in the secret cave, wherein all becomes a single nest—within that everything comes together and disperses; he, the pervasive one, is woven across and through all creatures.
Let the Gandharva, knowing it, proclaim that immortal [truth] which was established in secret; three steps of his have been placed in concealment—he who knows them shall be the father of the Father.
He is our kinsman, our progenitor, and our ordainer; he knows all abodes and all worlds, wherein the gods, having attained immortality, established themselves in the third station.

Having encompassed all beings, having encompassed the worlds, and having encompassed all the intermediate and cardinal directions, he approached the first-born of Cosmic Order and entered into himself by means of his own self.

Having instantly traversed heaven and earth, having passed beyond the worlds, beyond the quarters, and beyond the sun—he beheld that which was stretched out as the thread of *ṛta*; that became, and that existed.
I have approached the wonderful Lord of the Assembly, the beloved and desirable friend of Indra, for the sake of winning wisdom; Svāhā!
O Agni, with that wisdom which the hosts of gods and the ancestors revere, with that wisdom make me wise today; svāhā!
May Varuṇa grant me intelligence; may Agni and Prajāpati grant me intelligence; may Indra and Vāyu grant me intelligence; may Dhātṛ grant me intelligence—svāhā!
May this my priesthood and nobility both attain prosperity; may the gods bestow upon me supreme prosperity—svāhā to that for you!
His are the ageless fires, the pilots of the dwellings, with glowing smoke, purifying; white-shining, strengthening, restless, resting in the woods like winds, like Soma juices.
The bay steeds, smoke-bannered and swift as the wind, the fires strive separately toward the sky.
Sacrifice for us to Mitra and Varuṇa; sacrifice to the gods and to the great Ṛta; O Agni, sacrifice in your own dwelling.
Yoke, O Agni, like a charioteer, the horses that best invite the gods; sit down as the ancient Hotṛ-priest.

Two of different forms move about for their own purpose; one after the other, they suckle the calf. With the one, he becomes tawny, self-dependent; with the other, he is seen bright and full of splendor.

This one was established here as the first by the creators, the most excellent invoker, to be praised at the sacrifices; he whom Apnavāna and the Bhṛgus caused to shine forth, the wondrous and pervasive one, for every clan within the woods.

Three thousand, three hundred, and thirty-nine gods have honored Agni; they have sprinkled him with clarified butter, strewn the sacrificial grass for him, and then established him as the Hotṛ priest.
The gods have generated Agni Vaiśvānara—the head of heaven, the steward of earth, born in the cosmic order (ṛta)—the seer, the sovereign, the guest of men, as a vessel for their mouths.
May Agni, seeking wealth, strike down the obstacles with his inspired praise—kindled, bright, and invoked with oblations.
O Agni, drink the Soma-mead with all [the gods], with Indra and Vāyu, according to the ordinances of Mitra.

When the brilliance reached the lord of men for nourishment, the pure seed was poured down from heaven in the encounter; Agni brought forth and perfected the blameless, youthful, and well-disposed host.
O Agni, be strong for great good fortune; may your splendors be most excellent. Make the household lordship easy to govern; trample down the powers of those who act as enemies.

For we have chosen you, the most delightful one, with the flames of our hymns; hear our great prayer, O Agni! No other deity equals you in power like Indra; the most heroic men satisfy you with their bounty as they do Vāyu.
O Agni, well-invoked with *svāhā*, may the wise patrons be dear to you—those liberal lords of men who bestow wide pastures of cattle.
Hear us, O Agni, you whose ear is keen, together with the gods who are the carriers and your companions; let Mitra, Aryaman, and those who travel at dawn sit upon the sacrificial grass at our rite.
Aditi among all those worthy of sacrifice, the guest of all human beings—may Agni Jātavedas, choosing the protection of the gods, be gracious to us.

In the protection of the great, kindled Agni, may we be sinless before Mitra and Varuṇa for our well-being; may we abide in the most excellent impulsion of Savitṛ. We choose that favor of the gods today.

Even the waters have swelled like barren cows; your singers, O Indra, have reached the Eternal Law (*ṛta*). Come toward us as Vāyu with his teams of horses, for through our prayers you distribute spoils of war.
The two great ones, the bestowers of abundance upon the sacrifice, have come down to the cattle; both their ears are made of gold.
When the sun has risen today, may Mitra, Aryaman, Savitṛ, and Bhaga impel us toward sinlessness.
Pour the glory into the pressed juice, the glory that pervades heaven and earth; let the essence take up the bull.

As he stood there, all [the gods] adorned him; clothed in splendors, he moves, self-luminous. That is the great name of the bull-like Asura; assuming all forms, he has taken his stand upon the immortal realms.

Sing forth for the great Indra, who rejoices in the soma-juice, he who belongs to all men and is the source of all things—he whose well-made strength, great fame, and manly valor both heaven and earth revere.
Great indeed is their fuel, abundant their praise, and wide their sacrificial post—those whose friend is the youthful Indra.
O Indra, exhilarate yourself with the soma-juice at all the soma-pressings; you are the great one, most helpful through your might.

Indra, whose intent is to destroy, encompassed Vṛtra; his form was deceptive as he struck down the wiles of the guileful. He slew Vyamsa, burning fiercely in the forests, and made manifest the lowing of the cows of the nights.

From where do you come alone, O Indra, though you are mighty, O Lord of the Good? What is it thus that you ask when meeting with the radiant ones? Tell us that, O Lord of Bay Horses, which is yours among us.
Great is Indra by his might; never are you barren, never do you neglect us.

To this of yours, O Indra, those who seek you have offered praise, they who desire to burst open the stall rich in cattle—those who wish to milk the great, lofty, thousand-streamed cow that has many sons at once.

I offer this great prayer to you, the Great One, since my inspired thought has been adorned for his praise. At the festival and at the impulse [of sacrifice], the gods have followed Indra with power, honoring him who is victorious.

May the radiant and great one drink the Soma-mead, bestowing unimpaired life upon the lord of the sacrifice; he who, impelled by the wind, protects by his own self, has nourished all creatures and shines forth in many ways.
Upward his rays bear that god Sūrya, the knower of all beings, so that everyone may behold him; Svāhā!
O Purifier, with that eye wherewith you behold the people as they stir about, even so do you, O Varuṇa, look upon us.
O two divine Adhvaryus, come hither on your chariot with sun-bright skins; anoint the sacrifice with honey.
As of old, this Vena [sings]—the wondrous [glory] of the gods.

May the god Savitṛ, the friend of all men, come to our sacrifice with nourishing gifts and fair praise; so that you, O youths, may exhilarate us at the conclusion of the rite, as all the world does with its thought.
Whatever has risen today, O Vṛtra-slayer, and whatever the sun shall rise over—O Indra, all that is under your control.
O Sūrya, you are the deliverer, visible to all, the maker of light; you illuminate the entire radiant realm.

That is the divinity of the Sun, that is his greatness: in the midst of his work he has withdrawn what was spread out. When he has unyoked his bay steeds from their station, then Night spreads her garment over all.
In the lap of heaven, Sūrya assumes that form of Mitra and Varuṇa for all to behold; one part of his radiant power is endless and white, while the other is black, which the bay steeds bring together.
Great art thou in majesty, O Sūrya; great art thou as Āditya. The greatness of thee, who art great, is truly praised; indeed, O God, thou art great.
Truly, O Sūrya, you are great in glory; truly, O God, you are great. By your greatness, you are the divine priest of the gods, the far-reaching, invincible light.
Turning toward him as if toward the sun, may all partake of Indra’s riches; at every birth, we look toward our portion with power, as if toward a share.
O gods, at the rising of the sun today, deliver us from distress and from reproach! May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven grant this to us abundantly.
Advancing through the dark expanse, establishing both the immortal and the mortal, the god Savitṛ comes upon his golden chariot, beholding all beings.

The sacrificial grass, easy to tread upon, has been spread out for them; like two lords of the people, they hasten to the gathering-place of the tribes at the first invocation of night and dawn—Vāyu with his team of horses and Pūṣan, for our well-being.
Indra and Vāyu, Bṛhaspati, Mitra and Agni, Pūṣan, Bhaga, the Ādityas, and the host of Maruts.
May Varuṇa be our protector and Mitra with all his aids; may they both make us richly prosperous.
Be mindful of us, O Indra and Viṣṇu, among these kinsmen; come also, O Maruts and Aśvins!
As of old; this Vena; those who are the gods; may they come to us with nourishing offerings; with all [the gods], [let there be] the Soma-mead; O protectors, supporters of the people.
O Agni, Indra, Varuṇa, Mitra, and gods, grant us strength, O Maruts and Viṣṇu! May both the Nāsatyas, Rudra, the divine wives, Pūṣan, Bhaga, and Sarasvatī be pleased.
I invoke Indra and Agni, Mitra and Varuṇa, Aditi, the Sun, Earth, Heaven, the Maruts, and the Mountains; I call upon Viṣṇu, Pūṣan, Brahmaṇaspati, Bhaga, Śaṃsa, and Savitṛ for our protection.

May the Rudras, the liberal ones, and the mountains, being of one accord in the slaying of Vṛtra at the call of battle, protect us—those gods who, with Indra as their chief, have been established as a firm support for him who recites and praises. May they favor us.
Turn toward us this day, O worshipful ones; fearing, I would enter into your very heart. Save us, O gods, from the devouring wolf; save us, O worshipful ones, from falling into the pit.
May all the Maruts come today with every aid; may all the fires be well-kindled. May all the gods come to us with their protection; may all wealth and vigor be ours.

O All-Gods, hear this my invocation—you who are in the intermediate space and you who dwell in heaven; you whose tongue is Agni, or you who are worthy of sacrifice—having seated yourselves upon this sacred grass, rejoice!
For first indeed for the gods worthy of sacrifice you produce immortality as their supreme portion; then, O Savitṛ, you unfold the gift for men according to their successive lifespans.

Toward Vāyu let this lofty hymn go forth—a great wealth, all-desirable, filling the chariot—O most worshipful one, you, the seer, seeking the seer, fly with your teams of horses whose paths are radiant.
O Indra and Vāyu, these pressed juices are here; come hither with refreshments, for the drops long for you both.
May we be united with Varuṇa, whose will is pure, and with Mitra, the destroyer of enemies, as they perfect our prayer that flows with clarity like clarified butter.
O Dasyūs, O Nāsatyas, these juices pressed for you have been prepared upon the strewn sacrificial grass; come hither, O you whose path is like that of Rudra!
Him as of old; this Vena.

When Saramā found the cleft in the mountain, she made the great, ancient path wide for her own company; the swift-footed one led the way at the head of the flowing streams, and knowing them well, she went first toward the roar.
For the gods did not find any other touchstone than this Vaiśvānara Agni as a leader; they, the immortals, strengthened this immortal Vaiśvānara for the conquest of the field.
Fierce and dispellers of enemies, we invoke Indra and Agni; may they both be gracious to us in such a plight as this.
Sing forth, O men, for this Indu as he flows clear; he desires to worship the gods.

O Maghavan, those who strengthened you at the slaying of Ahi, those at the battle for Śambara, O Lord of Bay Steeds, and those at the quest for cattle—those sages who now rejoice after you, drink the Soma, O Indra, together with your host of Maruts.

You were born fierce for victorious power, delightful, most mighty, and full of great pride; even the Maruts strengthened Indra on that occasion when his mother brought forth the hero as the most excellent giver.
Come then to our side, O Indra, slayer of Vṛtra; great one, with your mighty aids.
O Indra, you are the conqueror of all rival hosts in battles; you are the slayer of the malevolent, the progenitor, and the overcomer of all. Do you overcome those who seek to overcome us.
The two worlds, heaven and earth, follow after your surging might as mother cows follow their calf; all your adversaries yield before your wrath when you, O Indra, strike down Vṛtra.
The sacrifice goes toward the favor of the gods; O Ādityas, be gracious. May your benevolence turn hitherward, which is the best finder of wide space even from distress.
O Savitṛ, with your unfailing and auspicious protections, guard our household today. O golden-tongued one, protect us for new-found prosperity; let no malevolent person have power over us.

For you both, the pure ones, the honeyed pressed juices have been offered by the *adhvaryu* priests through heroic deeds. O Vāyu, bring your teams; come hither! Drink of the pressed soma for exhilaration.
The two great ones, the yielders of abundance for the sacrifice, have come down to us like cows; both their ears are made of gold.
The two poets, destroyers of enemies, have come through the power of the sacrifice into the dwelling of Dakṣa, to their common abode.
O two divine Adhvaryus, come hither on your chariot with sun-bright skin; anoint the sacrifice with honey.
Him, as of old; this Vena.
A transverse ray was stretched across them; was there depth below, or was there height above? There were seed-bearers, there were powers; self-sustenance was below, and impulse was beyond.

He has filled the two worlds and the great light, when they, the skillful ones, supported him at his birth; he, the sage, is led forth for the sacrifice like a steed set loose for the winning of booty.
With hymns and songs of praise, they seek to win over those two greatest slayers of Vṛtra, who are truly exhilarated by the chant and the song of glory.
May the sons of immortality hear our songs; may they be gracious unto us.

The sacred hymns are mine, my thoughts are pressed out; my vigor stirs, the pressing-stone is set forth for me. They call upon you and welcome the hymn of praise; these two bay steeds carry you toward us.
O Maghavan, there is none superior to you; indeed, no deity is known who is your equal. Neither one being born nor one already born can attain you. Do what you must do, O exalted one!
That indeed was the eldest among all beings, from which was born the fierce one of brilliant valor; as soon as he was born, he overthrew his enemies—he in whom all his helpers rejoice.
O Lord of abundant wealth, may these songs of mine increase your strength; the pure, wise ones, bright as fire, have celebrated you with their hymns of praise.
He for whom this entire world—the Ārya, the Dāsa, and the enemy who guards the treasure—is subject; even from the noble Ruśama Parīru, that wealth is driven toward you.
This one, made mighty by a thousand seers, has spread out like the ocean. His greatness is true; his power is praised at the sacrifices in the kingdom of the inspired poets.
O Savitṛ, with your undeceivable and auspicious protections, guard our household today. O golden-tongued one, protect us for the sake of new prosperity; let no malevolent person have power over us.
O Vāyu, come to our sacrifice that touches the heavens with your benevolent thoughts; being mixed above the filter, this bright [soma] is offered to you.
We invoke Indra and Vāyu here, who are beautiful to behold and easy to call upon, so that every person in our assembly may be free from disease and well-disposed toward us.
Truly, that mortal has indeed labored successfully for the service of the gods, who now has brought Mitra and Varuṇa near for his protection and for the offering of oblations.
Come hither, attend to us, and drink of the honeyed mead, O Aśvins! You have milked the milk, O bulls, possessors of noble wealth; do not neglect us, but come!
May Brahmaṇaspati come forward; may the goddess Sūnṛtā come forward. May the gods lead our sacrifice toward the hero, the manly one who bestows fivefold wealth.
The moon runs within the waters; as a well-winged bird, it hastens in the sky. Tawny-hued, bellowing loudly, it goes toward abundant, much-desired wealth of golden color.
God after god we invoke for your protection; god after god we call upon for our aid. Singing with divine prayer, let us invoke god after god for the winning of the prize.
Established in heaven, Agni Vaiśvānara has shone forth, great; increasing upon the earth with his might, well-disposed, he dispels the darkness with his light.
O Indra and Agni, this one has come first, though she is footless among those who have feet; leaving her head behind, moving while speaking loudly with her tongue, she has stepped down thirty steps.
For all the gods, being of one mind with Manu, are together givers of gifts; may they today and in the future be finders of wide space for our progeny.
He blew away the curses, the slayer of the reviler; then Indra became resplendent in glory. O you of great luster, leader of the Marut host, the gods have striven for your friendship, O Indra.
Sing forth a prayer to the great Indra, O Maruts; may the Vṛtra-slayer, the lord of a hundred powers, slay Vṛtra with his hundred-knotted thunderbolt.
In the exhilaration of this pressed juice, Indra increased his manly strength and power within the expanse of Viṣṇu; today, as in former times, living beings praise that greatness of his.
These [songs] for you; he whose this [is]; this one, a thousandfold; upright, lift us up.

That divine [mind] which goes far away from the waking state, that indeed comes in the same way to one who is asleep; the far-reaching, the single light of lights—may that mind of mine be of auspicious resolve.
That by which the wise and skillful perform their works at the sacrifice during the assemblies—that unprecedented, wondrous power within all creatures—may that mind of mine be of auspicious intent.

That which is wisdom, as well as thought and steadfastness, that light which is the immortal within living beings—that without which no action whatsoever is performed—may that mind of mine be of auspicious resolve.

May that mind of mine be of auspicious intent—the mind by which this past, present, and future world is entirely encompassed by the immortal, and by which the sacrifice with its seven priests is performed.

In whom the Ṛg-verses, the Sāman-chants, and the Yajus-formulas are established, like spokes in the hub of a chariot wheel; in whom the entire consciousness of all creatures is woven—may that mind of mine be of auspicious intent.
Like a skilled charioteer who guides horses with the reins, or like swift steeds being led, may that mind of mine—which is established in the heart, agile, and most rapid—be of auspicious intent.
Now I shall praise the drinker, the one of great laws and power, by whose might Trita shattered Vṛtra limb from limb.
O Anumati, may you approve this; grant us well-being and impel us toward wisdom and skill. Prolong our lifespans.
May Anumati favor our sacrifice today among the gods; and may Agni, the bearer of oblations, be a source of joy to the donor.
O Sinīvālī, broad-tressed one, you who are the sister of the gods—be pleased with the oblation offered; O goddess, grant us progeny.
Five rivers with their currents flow into the Sarasvatī; yet in that region, the Sarasvatī herself became a river divided into five streams.

O Agni, you were the first Aṅgiras, the seer; as a god, you became the auspicious friend of the gods. Under your law, the Maruts—the wise ones, active through their insight—were born with glittering spears.

O Agni, O God, do thou guard us with thy protections, O worshipful one, both our patrons and our own bodies. Thou art the savior of our children and progeny and of our cattle; in thy service, protect us with unblinking vigilance.

Place him down upon her who lies supine; being wise, he has been conceived at once. The ruddy-hued one has brought forth the bull; his bright form has shone, and the Son of Iḍā has been born according to the sacred law.
O Jātavedas, Agni, we place you upon the navel of the earth, in the station of Iḍā, so that you may carry the oblation.

We meditate upon a hymn of strength for the mighty one, a song of praise like that of the Aṅgirases for the lover of songs; with well-fashioned verses let us extol him who is worthy of praise, and sing a hymn to the renowned Hero.

Bring forth great homage to the Great One; offer a song of praise, a *sāman*, to the Mighty One, by which our ancient fathers, the Aṅgirases, who knew the tracks, found the cows while offering their hymns.
The Soma-loving friends desire you; they press the Soma and present the offerings. They endure the insults of men, for from you, O Indra, comes every source of wisdom.

The highest realms are not far for you; come hither with your two bay horses, O Lord of the Bay Steeds. These libations have been prepared for the steadfast bull; the pressing-stones are set in motion while the fire is kindled.

O Soma, may we rejoice after you—you who are invincible in battles, the deliverer in armies, the winner of light, the winner of waters, the guardian of the stronghold, born for the fray, possessing a secure dwelling, renowned, and victorious.

Soma gives a milch-cow; Soma gives a swift steed; Soma gives a hero who is skillful in action—one who is fit for the household, fit for the assembly, fit for the council, and renowned among his ancestors—to him who offers oblations to him.
O Soma, you have generated all these plants; you have generated the waters and the cows. You have stretched out the wide mid-air; you have dispelled the darkness with light.
