O divine Soma, with your divine mind, O victorious one, fight for our share of wealth! Let it not hold you back; you are the master of heroic power. Provide for both sides in the quest for cattle.
He has revealed the eight quarters of the earth, the three desert regions, and the seven rivers. The golden-eyed god Savitṛ has arrived, bestowing desirable treasures upon the donor.
Savitar, the golden-handed, all-seeing, moves between both heaven and earth; he drives away disease and impels the sun; with his dark radiance, he reaches toward the sky.

May the golden-handed Asura, the good leader, the most gracious and self-reliant one, come hither; driving away the Rākṣasas and Yātudhānas, the god has taken his stand, being praised at every twilight.
O Savitṛ, those ancient paths of yours which are dustless and well-prepared in the mid-air—by those easy-to-traverse paths, protect us today and speak for us, O God.
Drink both of you, O Aśvins; grant us protection both of you, with your unfailing aids.

O Aśvins, make our speech full of wealth; O wonder-workers, bulls, grant us inspired thought. In this lack of success, I invoke you both for protection; be with us for our increase in the winning of the prize.
Day and night, O Aśvins, protect us with unharmed blessings. May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven grant this to us.
Advancing through the dark expanse, establishing both the immortal and the mortal, the god Savitṛ comes upon his golden chariot, beholding all beings.
O Night, you have filled the earthly realm with the abodes of your father; vast one, you spread across the seats of heaven, and your brilliant darkness rolls forth.
O Uṣas, rich in prizes, bring to us that wonderful wealth by which we may provide for our children and our grandchildren.
At dawn we invoke Agni; at dawn Indra; at dawn Mitra and Varuṇa; at dawn the Aśvins; at dawn Bhaga, Pūṣan, and Brahmaṇaspati; at dawn we shall call upon Soma and Rudra.

May we invoke the fierce Bhaga, won in the morning, the son of Aditi who is the distributor; him whom even the weak man, even the swift man, and even the king, thinking of him, says, "May I partake of Bhaga."
O Bhaga, leader; O Bhaga, whose gifts are true; O Bhaga, favor this prayer and grant us wealth. O Bhaga, increase us with cattle and horses; O Bhaga, may we be rich in men through our heroes.
May we now be in the favor of the Blessed Ones—at the beginning, at the end, and in the midst of the days; and at the rising of the sun, O Maghavan, may we abide in the benevolence of the gods.
O gods, let Bhaga alone be the possessor of fortune; through him may we become possessed of fortune. O Bhaga, everyone invokes you; as such, O Bhaga, be our leader here.
May the Dawns bow down to the sacrifice, as Dadhikrā does toward the pure station. May they bring hither to us Bhaga, the finder of wealth, as swift horses draw a chariot.
May the auspicious Dawns, rich in horses, cows, and heroes, shine upon us forever; yielding clarified butter and overflowing on every side, do you protect us always with your blessings.
O Pūṣan, under your protection may we never come to harm; we here are your praisers.

With speech, he has reached the protector of every path, fashioned by desire; he has attained the hymn of praise. May that Pūṣan grant us riches with golden tips; may he bring each and every prayer to fulfillment.
Viṣṇu, the infallible guardian, strode forth his three steps, thereby upholding the sacred laws.
The wise, ever-vigilant and full of praise, kindle that which is the supreme station of Viṣṇu.
Rich in ghee, the glory of all beings, wide and broad, yielding honey, well-adorned—Heaven and Earth are held apart by the law of Varuṇa, ageless and abounding in seed.
May those who are our rivals be driven away; with Indra and Agni we repel them. The Vasus, Rudras, and Ādityas have made him—the fierce, perceiving, and sovereign lord—our protector from above.
O Nāsatyas, come here with the thirty-three gods for the drinking of the honeyed mead, O Aśvins! Prolong our lifespan, wipe away our sins, drive off our enemies, and be our companions.

This hymn is for you, O Maruts; this song of the poet Māndārya, the son of Māna. May it bring offspring for our own bodies. May we find strengthening food and a secure dwelling that bestows life-sustaining gifts.

Accompanied by hymns, accompanied by meters, with their ritual turnings, with their measures, the seven divine seers—having gazed upon the path of the ancients, the wise ones took hold [of it], as charioteers take hold of the reins.
Bestowing long life, bestowing luster, increasing wealth, and breaking forth from the earth—may this lustrous gold enter into me for the sake of victory.

Neither the *rakṣas* nor the *piśācas* overcome that, for this is the first-born vigor of the gods. He who wears the gold of Dakṣa’s lineage secures long life among the gods; he secures long life among men.
The gold which the Dākṣāyaṇas bound on for Śatānīka with well-disposed minds—that I bind on myself, so that I may live a hundred autumns, long-lived and reaching old age.
And may Ahi Budhnya hear us, and Aja Ekapād, the Earth, and the Ocean; may all the gods who increase the cosmic order (*ṛta*), being invoked, and the hymns recited by sages, protect us when praised.
These hymns, dripping with clarity, I ever offer with the ladle to the Ādityas, the kings. May Mitra, Aryaman, Bhaga, the many-born Varuṇa, Dakṣa, and Aṃśa hear us.

Seven seers are appointed within the body; they guard it always with vigilance. Seven waters go to the world of the sleeper; there, two gods remain awake, sleepless, and seated at the sacrificial session.
Arise, O Brahmaṇaspati! We, seeking the gods, call upon you. May the Maruts, the bounteous givers, come forward; O Indra, be swift in our company.
Now indeed Brahmaṇaspati utters the hymn worthy of praise, in which Indra, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman, and the gods have made their dwellings.
O Lord of Prayer, be the guide of this hymn and prosper our offspring. All that the gods protect is auspicious; may we, blessed with brave sons, speak aloud at the assembly.
He who [made] all these things; Viśvakarman; he who is our father; O Lord of Food, give us food.
Let the Panis depart, those who are ill-disposed and haters of the gods; this world belongs to him who has pressed the soma.
May Yama grant him a dwelling place, clearly revealed by days, nights, and watches.
May Savitṛ seek a place for you upon the earth from among your bodily parts; therein let the rays of light be joined.
May Vāyu purify; may Savitṛ purify; by the brilliance of Agni, by the splendor of Sūrya, let the cows be released.
The holy fig tree is your seat; the leaf has been made your dwelling. You shall indeed be sharers of cattle if you win back the man.
May Savitṛ strew your remains upon the lap of the Mother; O Earth, be auspicious to him.
I place you, O [Name], in Prajāpati, in the deity, in the world where there is water; may it burn away our evil.
Go away, O Death, along your own path, which is other than the way of the gods; I speak to you who have eyes and hear: do not harm our progeny, nor our heroic sons.
May the wind be auspicious for you; may its heat be auspicious for you; may the bricks be auspicious for you; may the earthly fires be auspicious for you—let them not consume you.
May the quarters be favorable to you; may the waters be most auspicious for you, and the rivers. May the intermediate space be auspicious for you, and may all the quarters be favorable to you.
The stony river flows; hold fast to one another, arise, and cross over, O friends! Here let us leave behind those who were unpropitious; may we, being auspicious, cross over toward strengths.
Drive away misfortune, drive away sin, drive away the malevolent spell, and drive away affliction; O Apāmārga plant, drive the evil dream far away from us.
May the waters and plants be friendly to us; may they be unfriendly to him who hates us and whom we hate.
We take hold of the bull, the offspring of Surabhi, for our well-being; may he be for us like Indra among the gods—a carrier who brings us safely across.
Beholding the higher light beyond the darkness, we have gone unto Sūrya, the god among gods, the supreme radiance.
I set up this boundary for the living, so that no other among them may now go to that goal. May they live a hundred abundant autumns, placing death beyond them with this mountain.
O Agni, purify our lives; bring us strength and nourishment; drive misfortune far away.

O long-lived Agni, increasing by the oblation, may you have drops of clarified butter as your crest and clarified butter as your source. Having drunk the clarified butter and the sweet, pleasant product of the cow, protect these [people] as a father protects his son; svāhā!
These men have led the cow around; they have carried Agni around. They have established glory among the gods—who shall dare to attack them?
I send the flesh-eating Agni far away; let him go to the realm of Yama, carrying off impurities. Let this other Jātavedas remain right here, conveying the oblation to the gods with full knowledge.
O Jātavedas, carry this omentum to the ancestors where you know them to be placed in the distance; let streams of fat flow toward them, and may their true blessings be fulfilled—svāhā!
O Earth, be pleasant to us, thornless, and a place of rest; grant us wide-spreading shelter.
May it burn away our evil.
From this you were born; from you may he be born again. May he go to that heavenly world, svāhā!

I take refuge in the *ṛc* as speech; I take refuge in the *yajus* as mind; I take refuge in the *sāman* as breath; I take refuge in sight and hearing. May speech, vigor, and power, as well as the out-breath and in-breath, abide within me.
Whatever flaw there may be in my eye, my heart, or my mind that is easily pierced—may Bṛhaspati mend that for me. May he who is the Lord of the world bring us well-being.
Bhūr Bhuvaḥ Svaḥ. We meditate upon that most excellent splendor of the divine Savitṛ; may he impel our thoughts.
With what aid will our wondrous friend, who ever prospers us, come to us? With what most powerful host?
Which true one among the exhilarations, most bountiful, shall intoxicate you with the soma-juice? He who breaks open even firm wealth.
Be truly our protector, O friend of us who sing your praises; may you be with us for our aid a hundredfold.
With what aid do you, O Bull, rejoice? With what [aid] will you bring [wealth] to those who praise you?
Indra rules over all; may there be well-being for our bipeds and well-being for our quadrupeds.
May Mitra be auspicious to us, may Varuṇa be auspicious, and may Aryaman be auspicious to us; may Indra and Bṛhaspati be auspicious to us, and may Viṣṇu of the wide stride be auspicious to us.
May the wind blow auspiciously for us; may the sun shine auspiciously upon us; may the god Parjanya, thundering loudly, rain down auspiciously for us.

May the days be auspicious for us; may the nights be established as auspicious. May Indra and Agni be auspicious to us with their protections; may Indra and Varuṇa, to whom oblations are offered, be auspicious to us. May Indra and Pūṣan be auspicious to us in the winning of booty; may Indra and Soma be auspicious for our well-being and for health and prosperity.
May the divine waters be auspicious for our aid and for our drink; may they flow toward us with peace and well-being.
O Earth, be pleasant to us, thornless, and a place of rest; grant us wide-spreading protection.
O Waters, you are indeed the sources of bliss; grant us strength for great joy and for the sake of beholding.
Whatever most auspicious essence you possess, grant us a share of it here, like longing mothers.
Therefore, we come gladly to you, for whose dwelling you quicken us; O Waters, give birth to us as well.

Heaven is peace, the atmosphere is peace, the earth is peace, the waters are peace, the herbs are peace, the trees are peace, the All-gods are peace, the sacred word is peace, everything is peace; peace indeed is peace—may that peace be mine.
O leather bag, be firm! May all beings look upon me with the eye of Mitra. With the eye of Mitra, I look upon all beings. With the eye of Mitra, may we look together.
O leather bag, be firm; may I live long in your sight; may I live long in your sight.
Homage to your heat, to your flame; homage be to your radiance! May your missiles scorch others than us; O Purifier, be auspicious toward us.
Homage be to you, O lightning; homage be to you, O thunder; homage be to you, O Blessed One, from whom you strive toward the light of heaven.
From whatever direction you seek [us], from that grant us fearlessness; grant us well-being for our progeny and fearlessness for our cattle.
May the waters and plants be friendly to us; may they be unfriendly to him who hates us and whom we hate.

May that eye, ordained by the gods, the bright one rising in the east, behold us for a hundred autumns; may we live for a hundred autumns, hear for a hundred autumns, speak forth for a hundred autumns, remain undepressed for a hundred autumns, and even more than a hundred autumns.
At the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins and the hands of Pūṣan, I take thee; thou art a woman.

The inspired priests harness their minds and harness their thoughts for the sake of the great, inspired, and wise one. He alone, the knower of the sacred ordinances, has established the priestly functions. Vast indeed is the praise of the divine Savitṛ. Svāhā!
O divine Heaven and Earth, may I today successfully prepare the head of Makha upon the earth’s place of sacrifice to the gods; for Makha you, for the head of Makha you!
O divine ants, you who are the first-born of existence—may I today prepare the head of Makha for you upon the earth’s place of sacrifice to the gods; for Makha, you! For the head of Makha, you!
So much was there in the beginning; may I today accomplish the head of thee, Makha, upon the earth’s place of sacrifice to the gods. For Makha thee! For the head of Makha thee!

You are the vigor of Indra; may I today accomplish the head of Makha for you upon the earth at the place of sacrifice to the gods. For Makha you; for the head of Makha you; for Makha you; for the head of Makha you; for Makha you; for the head of Makha you.
May Brahmanaspati go forward; may the goddess Sūnṛtā go forward; may the gods lead our sacrifice toward the heroic, manly one who bestows fivefold wealth.

For Makha thee; for the head of Makha thee; for Makha thee; for the head of Makha thee; for Makha thee; for the head of Makha thee; for Makha thee; for the head of Makha thee; for Makha thee; for the head of Makha thee.

For Yama thee! For Makha thee! For the heat of Sūrya thee! May the god Savitṛ anoint thee with honey! Protect from contact with the earth! Thou art flame; thou art radiance; thou art heat.

Invincible from the east, under the overlordship of Agni, grant me long life. On the south, belonging to those with sons, under the overlordship of Indra, grant me progeny. Easy to sit upon from the west, under the overlordship of the god Savitṛ, grant me sight. The flowing one from the north, under the overlordship of Dhātṛ, grant me increase of wealth. The supporting one from above, under the overlordship of Bṛhaspati, grant me vigor. Protect me from all destructive powers. Thou art the mare of Manu.
Svāhā! Be adorned by the Maruts; protect from the touch of heaven. Honey, honey, honey!
The father of the gods, the lord of prayers, the master of creatures—he, the god, has united with the god Savitṛ; he shines together with Sūrya.

Agni has united with Agni; he has shone together with the divine Savitṛ, together with Sūrya. Svāhā! Agni has united with fervor; he has blazed forth together with the divine Savitṛ, together with Sūrya.
The upholder of heaven shines forth through his fervor upon the earth; the immortal god, the upholder of the gods, born of fervor—bestow upon us speech that seeks the gods.
I have seen the Herdsman, who never rests, moving hither and thither along his paths; he, clothed in converging and diverging rays, revolves repeatedly within the worlds.

O Lord of all worlds, O Lord of every mind, O Lord of every speech, O Lord of all speech! O God, you who are heard by the gods, O divine Gharma, as a god protect the gods! Here you have helped us for the feast of the gods; [we offer] honey to the two lovers of honey, honey to the two who possess sweetness.
For the heart thee, for the mind thee, for the sky thee, for the sun thee! Standing upright, place the sacrifice among the gods in heaven.

You are our father; be our father. Homage be to you; do not harm me. Accompanied by Tvaṣṭṛ, let us serve you. Bestow sons and cattle upon me; bestow progeny upon us. May I remain unharmed together with my husband and offspring.
May Day, with its banner, accept [this offering], well-luminous with light; Svāhā! May Night, with its banner, accept [this offering], well-luminous with light; Svāhā!
At the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins and the hands of Pūṣan, I take thee; thou art the girdle of Aditi.
Iḍā, come! Aditi, come! Sarasvatī, come! So-and-so, come! So-and-so, come! So-and-so, come!
You are the girdle of Aditi; you are the turban of Indrāṇī. You are Pūṣan; shine forth for the Gharma!
Overflow for the two Aśvins! Overflow, O Sarasvatī! Overflow for Indra! Svāhā, accompanied by Indra! Svāhā, accompanied by Indra! Svāhā, accompanied by Indra!

That breast of yours which is inexhaustible, which is refreshing, which bestows jewels, which finds wealth, and which is most bountiful—that by which you nourish all desirable things, O Sarasvatī, bring that here for suckling.
I follow along the wide mid-region.

You are the Gāyatrī metre; you are the Triṣṭubh metre. I enclose you with heaven and earth; I support you with the intermediate space. O Indra and the Aśvins, drink the Gharma of the honey of the bees; O Vasus, sacrifice! Vāṭ! Svāhā to the ray of the sun, the bringer of rain!

To you, the wind of the ocean, Svāhā! To you, the wind of the flood, Svāhā! To you, the invincible wind, Svāhā! To you, the unassailable wind, Svāhā! To you, the wind that brings aid, Svāhā! To you, the wind free from impurity, Svāhā!

To Indra, accompanied by the Vasus and the Rudras, svāhā! To Indra, accompanied by the Ādityas, svāhā! To Indra, the slayer of adversaries, svāhā! To Savitṛ, accompanied by the Ṛbhus, the Vibhus, and Vāja, svāhā! To Bṛhaspati, accompanied by all the gods, svāhā!
To Yama, accompanied by the Aṅgirases and the Pitṛs, svāhā! Svāhā to the Gharma! Svāhā, the Gharma to the Father!
Seated in the south, you have sacrificed here to all the quarters and to all the gods. O Aśvins, drink of this honeyed Gharma, consecrated with the cry of Svāhā.
Place this sacrifice in heaven; place this sacrifice in heaven. Svāhā to Agni, worthy of sacrifice; may there be well-being through the Yajus formulas.
O Aśvins, drink the Gharma that gladdens the heart, day by day with your daily aids; O weavers of the web of sacrifice, homage to Heaven and Earth!
May the Aśvins drink the hot offering; may Heaven and Earth give their approval. May the gifts remain right here.

Swell for nourishment! Swell for strength! Swell for the Brahman! Swell for the Kṣatra! Swell for Heaven and Earth! You are Dharma, the Good Dharma; you are not to be harmed. Bestow upon us manly powers; uphold the Brahman; uphold the Kṣatra; uphold the people.

Svāhā to Pūṣan for his seed! Svāhā to the pressing-stones! Svāhā to those who respond! Svāhā to the Fathers who sit upon the high sacrificial grass and drink the Gharma! Svāhā to Heaven and Earth! Svāhā to all the gods!

Svāhā! To Rudra, the invoker of Rudra! Svāhā! May light be united with light! May the Day, with its banner, accept [this]—the beautiful light with light, svāhā! May the Night, with its banner, accept [this]—the beautiful light with light, svāhā! O divine Gharma, may we obtain this honeyed oblation in the most Indra-like Agni; homage be to you; do not harm me.
This sage has become as vast as the greatness of heaven; he has extended himself even over the earth with his glory. Sit down, for you are great; shine forth, O best invoker of the gods!
O Gharma, may that divine heat of yours which is in the Gāyatrī and in the Havirdhāna—may it swell for you, may it settle for you; to that of yours, Svāhā!

That heat of yours which is in the atmosphere, that which is in the *triṣṭubh* meter, and that which is in the *āgnīdhra* hearth—may it swell for you, may it settle for you; to that of yours, *svāhā*!
O Gharma, that heat of yours which is on the earth, which is in the Jagatī meter, and which is in the Sadas—may it swell for you, may it settle for you; to that of yours, Svāhā!
For the protection of the ruling power, guard the body of the sacred word; we, the people, shall follow you according to the law for the sake of new prosperity.

The navel of Cosmic Order has four corners and is far-extending; may it be far-extending for us with full life, may it be far-extending for us with complete life. We have driven away the hatred and the guile of him who follows another's law.
O Gharma, this is your soil; with it, grow and swell. May we also grow and may we also swell.
The tawny bull has bellowed; great and fair to behold like Mitra, he has shone together with the sun, a treasure-house, an ocean.
May the waters and plants be friendly to us; may they be unfriendly to him who hates us and whom we hate.
Beholding the light higher than darkness, we have risen up; we have gone to Sūrya, the god among gods, the highest light.
You are fuel; may we prosper. You are kindling; you are splendor; bestow splendor upon me.

As far as heaven and earth extend, and as far as the seven rivers are spread out—so great, O Indra, is your draught; I take it up with strength, imperishable; I take it up within myself, imperishable.

In me be that great vital power; in me be skill and in me be wisdom. The three-pointed Gharma shines forth together with sovereign splendor, together with light, with sacred formulation, and with brilliance.

The milk is brought as semen; may we obtain its draught year after year. You who gather brilliance, for the sake of will and skill, you who have been pressed—O Agni, you who are offered in oblation, you who are well-disposed, you who are drunk by Indra, consumed by Prajāpati, full of sweetness: being invited, I partake of you who are invited.
Svāhā to the vital breaths together with their presiding deities! Svāhā to the earth! Svāhā to Agni! Svāhā to the intermediate space! Svāhā to Vāyu! Svāhā to the sky! Svāhā to Sūrya!
Svāhā to the quarters! Svāhā to the Moon! Svāhā to the constellations! Svāhā to the waters! Svāhā to Varuṇa! Svāhā to the navel! Svāhā to the purified one!
Svāhā to speech! Svāhā to the out-breath! Svāhā to the out-breath! Svāhā to the eye! Svāhā to the eye! Svāhā to the ear! Svāhā to the ear!
May I obtain the desire of the mind and the intention; may I obtain the truth of speech. May cattle, the form of food, and its essence—glory and prosperity—rest within me. Svāhā!

Prajāpati is being gathered; the Samrāj is gathered; the Vaiśvadeva is settled; the Gharma is offered; the Tejas is lifted up; the Āśvina is when the milk is being brought forward; the Pauṣṇa is when it is quivering; the Māruta is when it is being stirred; the Maitra is when the froth is being skimmed; the Vāyavya is when it is being carried forth; the Āgneya is when it is being offered; and Speech is when it has been offered.

Savitṛ [presides] on the first day, Agni on the second, Vāyu on the third, Āditya on the fourth, Candramas on the fifth, Ṛtu on the sixth, the Maruts on the seventh, Bṛhaspati on the eighth, Mitra on the ninth, Varuṇa on the tenth, Indra on the eleventh, and the Viśve Devās on the twelfth.
Ugra and Bhīma and Dhvānta and Dhuni, Sāsahvān and Abhiyugvan and Vikṣipa—svāhā!

With the heart [he offers] to Agni; with the tip of the heart to Aśani; with the entire heart to Paśupati; with the liver to Bhava; with the kidneys to Śarva; with the fury (manyu) to Īśāna; with the membrane between the ribs to Mahādeva; with the rectum to Ugra; with the lower jaw to Vasiṣṭha; with the testicles to Śiṅgin.

[He assigns] Ugra with blood, Mitra with good vows, Rudra with bad vows, Indra with play, the Maruts with strength, and the Sādhyas with joy. [He assigns] the throat to Bhava, the inner ribs to Rudra, the liver to Mahādeva, the large intestine to Śarva, and the pericardium to Paśupati.

Hail to the body hairs, hail to the body hairs; hail to the skin, hail to the skin; hail to the blood, hail to the blood; hail to the fats, hail to the fats; hail to the flesh, hail to the flesh; hail to the sinews, hail to the sinews; hail to the bones, hail to the bones; hail to the marrow, hail to the marrow; hail to the semen, hail to the anus.
Hail to exertion! Hail to effort! Hail to exhaustion! Hail to weariness! Hail to rising! Hail to the burning one! Hail to the one who burns! Hail to the one being burned! Hail to sorrow!

Hail to the heat! Hail to that which is heated! Hail to that which is being heated! Hail to that which has been heated! Hail to the Gharma! Hail to expiation! Hail to atonement! Hail to the healing medicine!
Svāhā to Yama! Svāhā to Antaka! Svāhā to Mṛtyu! Svāhā to Brahmā! Svāhā to the murder of a Brahmin! Svāhā to the Viśvedevas! Svāhā to Heaven and Earth!
The Lord alone owns all this, whatever moves in the world. By renouncing it, you should enjoy; do not covet the wealth of anyone.
Performing actions here in this world, one should desire to live for a hundred years; thus it is with you, and not otherwise than this—for action does not cling to a man.
"Sunless indeed are those worlds, shrouded in blind darkness; to them go after death all those people who are slayers of the self."
One thing moves not, yet it is swifter than the mind; the gods have not overtaken it as it sped on before them. It passes others who run while standing still; in it Mātariśvan lays the waters.
That moves, and that moves not; that is far, and that is near; it is within all this, and it is outside of all this.
But he who perceives all beings in the Self alone, and the Self in all beings, thereafter no longer doubts.
When for the one who perceives all beings have become the Self alone, what delusion and what sorrow can there be for him who beholds this unity?

He has gone around [the world]: bright, bodiless, woundless, without sinews, pure, unpierced by evil; a seer, wise, all-pervading, self-existent—he has established the objects of reality according to their true nature for eternal years.
Into blind darkness enter those who worship the Unmanifest; into even greater darkness, as it were, enter those who delight in the Manifest.
"They say that [the world] is one thing from its arising, and they say it is another from its dissolution; thus have we heard from the wise who explained this to us."
He who knows both origination and destruction together—having crossed over death by means of destruction, he attains immortality through origination.
Into blind darkness enter those who worship ignorance; into a darkness even greater than that, as it were, enter those who delight in knowledge alone.
They say that knowledge is one thing and ignorance is another; thus we have heard from the wise who explained this to us.
He who knows both knowledge and ignorance together—having crossed over death by means of ignorance, he enjoys immortality through knowledge.
The wind is the breath, the immortal; and this body ends in ashes. Om! O Kratu, remember! O Kliba, remember! Remember what was done!
O Agni, lead us by a good path to prosperity, O God who knowest all ways; remove from us the sin that leads astray, and we shall offer unto thee the most abundant homage.
The face of Truth is covered by a golden vessel; that Person who is there in the sun, he is I.
Oṃ Khaṃ Brahman.
